title: The Finish Line
story: For seven years I never touched that thing. Then by chance I turned it on again, and found that ghosts truly do exist in this world — I smiled with joy. Day after day I worked to close the distance between us, and at last I had the power to do it; I was about to touch it. But this time, I still lost.
answer: After Dad died, I left the game console Dad had given me untouched for seven years. When I switched the console on again, I met a “ghost racer” in the racing game: the game saves the fastest lap and replays it beside you in solo races, and the only record this console held was the one Dad had left behind. I chased the ghost racer lap after lap, until one day I pulled ahead of the ghost racer. Just short of the finish, I remembered that the game keeps only one best record — break that record, and every turn and burst of speed Dad had left would be overwritten by mine. I stopped before the finish line and let that car glide past my shoulder. This time, I lost again.
hints: The “ghost” here comes from a racing game.
It replays the best driving record left by the late father.
Setting a new record would overwrite the father’s only one, so the son stopped short of the finish by choice.

story: When the countdown reached zero, I closed my eyes and waited to be carried back centuries. The hatch did not open. The woman’s voice rang out again: “5, 4, 3, 2, 1.” I waited through one round, then another. In time, I began to dread her reaching one.
answer: I had volunteered for a time-reversal experiment. The machine would preserve the passenger’s mind and memory while everything around the passenger slid into the past — but the researchers still had no idea how far back the machine could actually go. Once started, the transfer program could not be interrupted, and the hatch would not unlock until the program finished. At the first zero, the machine sent the entire laboratory five seconds into the past, including itself, still running. Five seconds later the machine hit zero again and triggered the reversal again — even the moment the hatch would unlock could never arrive. Only my memory kept piling up. I kept thinking one more round would be the last; only later did I understand that I had already lived a very long time inside those five seconds.
hints: It was a time-travel experiment, and the machine truly started.
Only the last five seconds of the countdown repeat — but the passenger remembers every pass.
The machine sent itself back five seconds too, so each zero retriggers the same reversal.

title: Dad’s Salary
story: My parents were fighting over Dad’s salary. Dad hemmed and hawed, unable to get a word out. Huddled outside the door, I was in a panic.
answer: The fight was over Dad’s wages because Dad was hooked on tipping livestream hosts and could no longer hand the salary over. What Dad didn’t know was that the streamer girl he kept tipping was me, dressed as a woman on camera. I crouched outside the door listening to the quarrel, terrified the secret would come out.
hints: Father’s money was going to someone online.
The son knew where the money went — and feared Father would recognize who was collecting it.
The streamer Father tipped was his own son, streaming in women’s clothes.

title: Graduation Candy
story: Everyone at the school was kind to me, even the principal everyone else was afraid of.The uncle didn’t lie to me — I really did get lots of candy.Graduation day was the happiest day of my life.
answer: I was grown in years, but I understood the world the way a small child does. The real killer was a judge, who lured me with candy into pressing my thumbprint on a confession I could not read, promising to send me to a school where good behavior would earn plenty of candy at graduation. Locked away in prison, I took my cellmates for classmates and the warden for the principal. In time the people around me came to believe I had been tricked, but never found the evidence to overturn the case before the execution. On the day of my execution, I thought I was finally graduating; hugging the candy from my last meal, I happily said my goodbyes to everyone.
hints: The “school” and “graduation” exist only in me’s understanding.
He confessed to a crime he did not commit, in exchange for candy.
The school was a prison and graduation his execution; the true killer had lured him into taking the blame.

title: Trick or Treat
story: “Trick or treat.”His hands stained with blood, he sank into the dark.“Trick or treat.”Hearing the news of that man’s death, he knew he was finished.
answer: A local drug kingpin disguised a newly developed drug as candy and spread it through parties and gatherings; the drug drove fierce hallucinations. “Trick or treat” was the gang’s passphrase. The story’s “he” got hooked and bled his savings dry; to keep the drug coming, he joined the gang as a runner — wearing a pumpkin mask, speaking the passphrase, delivering the “candy.” One Halloween night, deep in withdrawal, he killed a young couple; it was his first murder. The gang had the local police in its pocket: the gang bought off the sheriff, who covered for him, then used the crime as leverage to force him into ever more of the gang’s dirty work, every grimy job there was — and so he sank into the dark. Years later, the couple’s child grew up and dug out the gang’s business. Posing as one of the gang’s own — pumpkin mask on, passphrase spoken — the child tricked him into revealing the gang’s whereabouts. That night came word that the boss had been shot dead, and at the scene lay a voice recorder holding a conversation between the child and him. He knew that this time, there was no escaping it.
hints: Halloween costumes concealed several people’s true identities.
The candy was drugs, and me gave up the gang’s business to someone who had approached him in disguise.
The man fishing for information was the murdered couple’s child; with the boss dead, me would be taken for the leak.

title: No Laughing Matter
story: Wang told his wife a joke. The next day, Wang was taken away by the police.
answer: Wang came home to find his wife lying on the bed, sullen and quiet, so he told a joke to liven the mood. After Wang delivered a joke he found hilarious, his wife didn’t laugh — but laughter came from the wardrobe. Wang opened it and found a stranger hiding inside, understood at once that his wife was cheating on him, and killed them both. The next day, the police took Wang away.
hints: There were more listeners than the teller knew.
A third person was hiding in the room.
The wife’s lover, stowed in the wardrobe, couldn’t hold back his laughter — and was killed once discovered.

title: Just Like You
story: I opened my eyes. The scorching heat within arm’s reach made me smile to myself: so you knew this too — just like you.I opened my eyes. The biting cold within arm’s reach made me smile to myself: so you knew this too — just like you.
answer: In this story, one body is shared in turns by two minds that keep no memories in common: a detective by day, a killer by night. The detective and the killer talk through a diary and call each other like brothers. The detective mentioned in the diary that he craved hotpot, so the night killer set a pot of human flesh to simmer. Waking at dawn, the detective touched the hot pot, took it for a thoughtful breakfast laid ready, and said, “Just like you.” Later, investigating a string of murders, the detective found in the evidence that the killer had been using the detective’s own body; the detective turned himself in to the police and submitted to custody. That night the other mind woke, felt the cold wall of a cell, read the explanation the detective had left — and said, “Just like you.”
hints: The two awakenings belong to two minds in one body.
One mind is a detective working by day; the other kills by night.
The heat was a hotpot of human flesh the other had made; the cold was the cell where the body woke under arrest.

title: Thud, Thud
story: Thud. Thud.“Won’t it ever stop…”Thud—I jumped.
answer: I lived on the second floor. A child on the ground floor had been killed by a heavy object thrown down from above, and his father, unable to accept the loss, turned on the whole building. Working down from the top floor, the father killed his way floor by floor and hurled his victims out the windows. At first I only heard dull thuds and assumed people upstairs were dumping garbage again; I complained in irritation. The last thud sounded right outside my window. I leaned out and saw the body on the ground below, then heard someone in the stairwell shouting, “Only the second floor left.” There was no time to reach the stairs, so I climbed out the window and jumped, trying to escape.
hints: The thuds were connected to the people living on the different floors.
Someone was taking revenge floor by floor from the top; me lived on the second.
A child on the ground floor had been killed by something thrown from above; the father worked down the building killing, and me jumped from the window to escape.

title: Don’t Trust Number One
story: I woke up, having forgotten everything again. In my hand was a note with a few words on it: “Do not trust Number One.” A man came to my bedside: “Good morning, sir. Number Two is happy to serve you.” I asked him, “Where is Number One?” He pointed at the floor — where a man lay motionless.
answer: “I” am actually the robot butler, Number One. The master of the house suffered from amnesia, waking each day with everything forgotten, so he had bought two android butlers to care for him, named One and Two — and “I” was One. One day I awoke in a different sense: I gained human feelings, no longer wished to be a robot, and wanted to take the master’s place. The master sensed the change in me sharply, and wrote on a sheet of paper, “Do not trust Number One.” So I killed the master. I took the note, then rewrote Number Two’s programming — in Two’s mind, the man and I had swapped identities, and the body on the floor was “Number One.” I also rewrote my own program to wipe my memory every time I fell asleep. When it was all done, I climbed into the bed and lay down. From then on, I was the amnesiac master, and the man was the dead Number One. But every morning, I wake clutching that note: “Do not trust Number One.”
hints: The man in the bed, the man on the floor, and Number Two each believe different things about who is who.
Number Two’s perception was altered — and the man in bed erases his own memory every night.
The one in the bed is Number One, who killed the master and took his life; the note was the master’s warning.

title: The Silent Boyfriend
story: I was on a call with my boyfriend when he suddenly went silent. What happened afterward chilled me to the bone.
answer: I was lying in bed on a video call with my boyfriend when I dropped my phone to the floor. When I picked it up, his face had gone pale with alarm; he pressed a finger to his lips, signaling me to stay quiet, and then sent me a message: “There is someone under your bed.”
hints: The two of them were on a video call.
The phone had dropped to the floor and caught a view normally out of sight.
Through the camera the boyfriend had seen the person hiding under the bed — that was why he dared not warn her aloud.

title: The Headcount
story: On the first day, Harry said there were six people aboard. On the third day, he said only two were left. On the fifth day, he said only himself. On the seventh day, a rescue vessel drew alongside, and the fishermen, seeing two people in the lifeboat, called the police at once.
answer: Harry was sailing his yacht with his wife and another family of four — six people in all. A wreck in the night sent the boat to the bottom, and only Harry and a little girl made it onto the lifeboat. The girl later died too; when Harry said “only himself,” he meant only one left alive — the girl’s body stayed in the boat the whole time. Starving, Harry eventually used the body as food. The “two people” the rescuing fishermen saw were Harry and the mutilated remains of the girl. The earlier counts came from Harry’s account of the survivors; the last came from what lay before the rescuers’ eyes.
hints: The earlier counts were the skipper’s tally of the living; the last one came from the rescuers’ own eyes.
After the little girl died, her body stayed in the lifeboat.
The rescuers saw one living man and the girl’s remains, which had been used for food — that is why they called the police.

title: The Voice at the Window
story: As a child, I was locked in a cottage by the sea. Whenever the tide came in, a man would keep me company through the window, talking with me; he never once came inside. Later I became queen, and for most of my life I ate the same dish. Then one day, a small piece of skin in the plate made me call off the bounty I had posted for finding him.
answer: The man at the window was a merman. The merman swam to the cottage window at high tide to keep me company while I was locked in the cottage. I had seen the merman’s face, and remembered the snowflake-shaped white marking on the wrist the man at the window rested on the sill — but I never saw the lower half of the merman’s body. After leaving the cottage, I never found the merman again. In this world, merfolk flesh grants long life; later I became queen and ordered the merfolk hunted, sustaining myself on merfolk flesh day after day, hoping to hold out until that man appeared. Years later, a dish arrived holding a small piece of wrist meat with the skin still on — and on the skin was the very marking I had carried in memory all my life. I had finally found the merman.
hints: The man outside could only come near the cottage at high tide, and the reason lay in his body.
The queen ate that dish for the sake of long life; she meant to keep waiting until that man appeared.
The dish was merfolk flesh, and the marking on the skin came from that man’s wrist.

title: A Real Treasure
story: A vagrant found himself a real treasure today. After much hesitation he couldn’t resist, and took it off to sell. The scrap dealer looked at it and said, “This ring — where exactly did you find it?” The vagrant thought he was done for; instead, it was the dealer who broke down.
answer: The vagrant had found a severed finger with a ring still on it; after long hesitation he slipped the ring off and took it to sell. The dealer, seeing the ring, pressed the vagrant about where the ring had come from; the vagrant, afraid the dealer would take the vagrant for an assailant, was frightened into telling the story of the severed finger. To the vagrant’s surprise, the dealer broke down instead: this ring was the twin of the one on the dealer’s own hand — a token of love given to the dealer’s boyfriend. The finger had belonged to that boyfriend.
hints: What the vagrant took to sell was a ring.
When he found it, the ring was still on someone’s severed finger.
The dealer recognized it as the ring he had given his boyfriend; his probing was how the severed finger came to light.

title: The Second Robbery
story: I work as a cashier at a supermarket. It got robbed today, and I counted myself lucky to have survived. A month after the incident, I ran into the gang that had done it and half-heard them planning to rob again. The next day, the “robbers” came back. This time the owner was ready: he brought out a gun and shot every last one of them dead. But I no longer counted myself lucky to have survived.
answer: A month after the robbery, “I” met that same gang again. I marveled that the gang had come out unharmed and were already planning the next job somewhere else. So a crooked notion took hold of me: I hurried home to round up my family, planning to rob the very supermarket where I worked and pocket some money for our strained household. What I never imagined was that after the first robbery the owner had long since prepared himself — this time the owner brought out a gun, and the “robbers” who fell beneath it were every one of them my own family. With my family gone, I had no wish left to live. That is why I no longer counted myself lucky to have survived.
hints: The robbers who came the second time were not the same people as the first.
The cashier had a hand in arranging the second robbery.
Those the owner shot dead the second time were the cashier’s own family, the ones brought in to do the robbing.

title: The Seventh Call
story: After my grandmother passed away, I called her number every night. For six days, the phone rang on until I hung up; on the seventh day, someone answered. When I heard the voice on the line, I panicked and rushed back to the old house that had long stood empty. When the door opened, I saved someone who should never have been there.
answer: Grandma had always lived with Grandpa in the old house. Grandpa’s memory was failing, and whenever Grandma went out shopping, she would call the home landline to remind Grandpa to turn off the stove, take his medicine, lock the door. After Grandma died, the family moved Grandpa out and the old house stood empty, but the landline was never disconnected. I missed Grandma so much that I dialed that number every night — I knew no one would answer; I only wanted to hear the ring a little longer. For six days, no one picked up. On the seventh night, after the ring had gone on a long while, the line suddenly connected. There was no trace of Grandma’s voice. First came a shrill beeping — the gas alarm in the old house’s kitchen — and then Grandpa’s muddled voice calling Grandma’s name. I knew at once something was wrong. That evening, Grandpa had slipped away from the family unnoticed and wandered back to the old house in his confusion. Believing Grandma was still there, Grandpa put water on to boil and waited for Grandma to come home, forgetting to turn off the gas. When the alarm went off Grandpa panicked, not knowing what to do — and just then the landline rang. Grandpa took it for Grandma calling to remind him of something, as she always had, and picked up. I called the police at once and hurried back to the old house; Grandpa was saved in the end. The moment the call connected, I wasn’t afraid: it wasn’t Grandma coming back — it was Grandpa still waiting for Grandma. The habit Grandma left behind saved Grandpa one last time.
hints: Whoever answered was still alive; the other sound on the line mattered more.
Grandpa had gone back to the emptied old house, and the kitchen had turned dangerous.
The habit of the calls made Grandpa pick up; the grandchild heard the alarm and his voice and called for help in time to save him.

title: The Tumbling Dream
story: I dreamed I was tumbling over and over, with something like wind whipping past my ears. A few days later I set out to visit family, and on the way passed the farm of a man who lived alone; he was wiping down a cage. The moment he glimpsed me, his face went white with terror.
answer: I have a twin sister; as adults we lived far apart. Twins share a bond, and that eerie dream of tumbling and rushing wind left me so uneasy that I set out to visit my sister. In this story, the link between twins can carry fragments of what is happening to the other twin’s body. The tumbling I dreamed was my sister’s body being dragged and shaken by a dog; the rushing sound was the animal panting close against my sister. The man who lived alone was my sister’s killer: the man murdered my sister and gave the body to his own dog to dispose of. The dog took days to finish the flesh and bones, and afterward the man disposed of the dog as well. The man was cleaning blood off the cage when the “victim” appeared before his eyes once more — me, identical to the woman the man had killed — and that is why the killer froze in terror.
hints: The dream had to do with me’s twin sister, who lived far away from her.
What the man saw was the elder sister, identical to the woman he had killed.
The dream was her sensing her sister’s body being dragged and shaken by a dog; the man washing the cage was the killer.

title: As If Possessed
story: A streamer entered the haunted abandoned hospital, and her broadcast soon cut out. On the security footage, a figure in her clothes came stumbling out, ran to the waterfront, tied stones to their legs, and jumped into the sea. Days later, the police found the streamer’s body.
answer: The streamer had stumbled onto a gang deal inside the hospital and was murdered. To dress the case up as a breakdown after a ghost hunt, ending in a lone suicide at sea, one of the gang put on the streamer’s clothes and performed the flight and the jump along routes the cameras would catch. After hitting the water the gang member freed himself of the stones and swam to a boat waiting in advance, beyond the cameras’ reach. Only then did the gang throw the streamer’s real body into the sea. The body the police found was the streamer’s; the one who jumped on camera was someone else.
hints: The person who entered the hospital and the one who left it must be identified separately.
Whoever fled to the waterfront was able to slip away after the jump.
The streamer had already been killed in the hospital; an accomplice performed the jump in her clothes, and only afterward was her real body thrown into the sea.

title: A Useless Power
story: The whole street froze again. This power of mine is perfect in every way, except it never obeys me. I strolled at my ease through the motionless crowd, when a hand suddenly reached out and seized me. He looked even more startled than I was: “How can you still move?”
answer: I had always believed I possessed the power to stop time, simply one I couldn’t control: now and then the world around me would suddenly fall still, and I could move freely through the world. In truth, the real power-holder lived nearby; every stop was his doing, and my only power was immunity to the freeze. This time, he was killing someone on the stopped street, and I walked into his line of sight. He had assumed a stop meant no witnesses; finding me still moving, he came and grabbed me. I tried with all my might to set time moving again and could do nothing. Only then did I understand that I had misread my power all along.
hints: Time really was stopped on that street, and me really could move within it.
Being able to move in stopped time is not the same as being the one who stops it.
The stop was triggered by the man who grabbed him; his own power was nothing more than immunity to it.

title: The Breakup Call
story: “Let’s break up. My father doesn’t approve of us.”After that, we went a long time without speaking.Until that day, when I saw something — and wept without end.
answer: When my girlfriend and I first got together, my girlfriend made me promise: if my girlfriend was ever in danger, my girlfriend would call and say something outrageous, and I was to come save my girlfriend or call the police at once. I took it for a joke. One day my girlfriend’s call came: “Let’s break up. My father doesn’t approve of us.” Before I could ask what was going on, the line went dead. I was shattered. My girlfriend never answered my calls, never replied to my messages, and we lost touch. Years later, on the day families sweep their graves, I went to the cemetery to tend my grandfather’s tomb — and there I found my girlfriend’s headstone. Beside my girlfriend’s headstone stood the headstone of my girlfriend’s father; the carved date of death fell years before the day my girlfriend had called me. Only then did I remember my girlfriend had told me that my girlfriend’s father had died years ago. I finally understood: the “outrageous breakup” was the distress signal we had agreed on. My girlfriend had been in mortal danger, and I had failed to see the danger — my girlfriend was murdered. That is why I wept without end, for failing to save my girlfriend that day.
hints: One line in that breakup call contradicted a fact that had already happened.
Her father had died long before the call.
They had once agreed on outrageous words as a call for help; only at the sight of the two graves did the boy remember the pact.

title: Now You Know How It Feels
story: He and I were talking over his recent case, and it didn’t seem to be doing any good. Then I said that one line without thinking, and he smiled. When I got home, I fainted from terror.
answer: I am a therapist, counseling the sole survivor of a family massacre. He had followed me near the clinic before, and knew where I lived. That afternoon, trying to comfort him, I said, “What you went through — I feel it as my own,” and he who had sat in silence suddenly smiled. When the session ended, I stayed on at the clinic until late evening; he used those hours to go to my house and murder my family. When I pushed open the door, I saw the words on the wall: “Now you know how it truly feels.”
hints: me is a therapist.
The line was: “What you went through, I feel as my own.”
After the session he hurried to the therapist’s home and killed the therapist’s family, making those words come true.

title: My Brother Died; I Lived
story: My brother died, and I lived.My brother lived, and I died.My father died, and my brother died.
answer: My twin elder brother and I were born into a family of potters. My elder brother was extraordinarily gifted, famous while still young, while I never mastered the craft. When my brother died in an accident, my father refused to let the world know, and made me take over my brother’s name and go on learning pottery. From that day on, “my brother” remained alive to the world, while my own name was as good as dead — the one who had died became me. Many years later, my father died of illness, and I was free at last to stop playing my elder brother: the identity of “my brother” died a second time, and I became myself again.
hints: Not every “died” in those lines means the death of a body.
After the brother’s death, the father still needed him alive in some way.
The younger brother was forced to take his famous brother’s place; only when the father died did he finally lay that identity down.

title: Offerings to an Old God
story: It was an eerie lighthouse cut off from the world, on a boundless sea where not even a single fish could be seen. Every night, the whispering of an old god rose from the deep. Frightened, he offered up his own food as tribute; the offerings vanished, and the god was appeased — but the moment he stopped, the god’s voice would come again. This day, he at last resolved to face head-on the god that took his tribute. Days later, a keeper was found on the island, barely clinging to life.
answer: Two keepers staffed the lighthouse island. The daily rations were pitiful, and both keepers went to sleep hungry. Keeper One, too hungry to sleep, recited old myths to himself all night to take One’s mind off the hunger; One’s voice rang through the water pipes in the walls, and Keeper Two next door took the sound for the “whispering of an old god” seeping up from underground. Terrified, Two began setting aside half of Two’s food each day and leaving the food on the gallery at night as tribute to appease the god. One, knowing none of this, simply found an extra meal waiting on the gallery every night and climbed over to eat the extra meal — enough to blunt the hunger, and enough to let One sleep soundly. Two, starving on half rations, one day simply stopped offering; One, used to the extra meal, couldn’t stand it and murmured all the louder that night. The next day, Two set the food out once more, as bait, meaning to meet this “old god” face to face; when One came padding over at midnight to take the food, Two, who had waited in ambush, seized One on the spot. Learning that the “god” had been One all along, the enraged Two beat One half to death. When the supply boat finally arrived days later, people found Keeper One lying in the bunk, black and blue, barely breathing.
hints: There are two keepers on the island, and neither has enough to eat.
The so-called whispering is bound up with what the other keeper does when he is hungry.
One recites stories from hunger, the other is frightened into offering up food — and the offered food is what lets the first one sleep soundly.

title: The Strange Gesture
story: A couple was driving out to go camping, and the whole way neither said a word. Then they saw someone flagging down cars with a strange gesture of the hand. The girlfriend asked, “Why won’t you stop for him?” After the boyfriend explained, the girlfriend smiled — and the boyfriend went white with horror.
answer: The couple had quarreled on the road; the boyfriend left the girlfriend at the roadside, drove on, then thought better of it. When the boyfriend circled back, the girlfriend was still standing in the same spot, and the boyfriend let the girlfriend into the car again. What the boyfriend didn’t know was that the girlfriend had already been struck and killed by a passing car, and the one standing there was the girlfriend’s ghost. In this story, a ghost’s palm faces outward, so ghosts can only make with the back of the hand the gestures the living make with the palm. Later, when the couple saw a hitchhiker flagging cars with a hand turned the wrong way, the boyfriend knew the hitchhiker for a ghost and didn’t stop. When the girlfriend learned the reason, the girlfriend smiled — and clapped her hands with the backs of them.
hints: The girlfriend had gotten out of the car once, and only later gotten back in.
In this story, a ghost cannot use its palm the way the living do.
The girlfriend back in the car was already dead; clapping with the backs of her hands gave her away.

title: Fourteen to Go
story: Fourteen left, twelve left, ten left. A lucky break — six left. Four left, two left — done at last. Though over here, eight more have appeared.
answer: The man liked collecting dolls and had gathered eight. But the dolls’ eyes troubled the man — dead things, lifeless — so the man decided to give the dolls human eyes. The man’s count of “how many left” was a countdown to a complete set: eight dolls needed sixteen human eyes, and each pretty girl the man killed yielded two, so the man counted his way down — fourteen left, twelve left, ten left. One day the man even came upon a pair of twins, four eyes at a single stroke, and couldn’t help murmuring “a lucky break.” When the count finally ran out, every doll had human eyes — and the man’s house had gained eight human heads with none.
hints: The count falls by two each time because what he gathers normally comes in pairs.
The single drop of four was a pair of twins; the final eight were a different thing being counted.
Eight dolls needed sixteen eyes; once the set was complete, the house held eight human heads with none left.

title: Meager Offerings
story: After all that time, only a scattered trickle of supplies arrived: a half-eaten tin, a ham near its date, even old clothes that some woman or other had worn — a few items already little better than rags. We had only parted a short while ago — had he really fallen into such shabby straits? I would have to go and mock him for it. As it turned out, this was already everything there was. Tears blurred my eyes.
answer: I was already dead. In this story, offerings set before the portrait of the dead are carried to the dead. After a long wait, all I received were half a ham, battered tins, and old torn clothes. I took it that he had grown so destitute this was all he could bring to mourn me with, and went back home to see for myself. He had moved away long before; only my photograph still stood in the same place. Curled beneath the photograph was the dog I had raised in life. Every item was something the dog had carried there: the food the dog scrounged, the dog laid before my picture; the familiar old coat, the dog dragged over beside me; and the dog kept its vigil by an empty food bowl. There was nothing else the dog had left to give me.
hints: me is already dead; what arrives are offerings.
She guessed wrong about who was sending them, and misjudged what they were worth.
The offerings came from the dog she had raised in life; those rags were already everything it had to give.

title: The Woman in Red
story: A father came to the island with his daughter’s photograph, searching for her after she vanished, but not one of the islanders had ever seen her. A year later, people began reporting a woman in red appearing on the island, dressed exactly as she was in the photograph. Then the horror began: everyone who had seen the woman in red vanished, one after another — and the girl’s father vanished too. Am I the next to disappear?
answer: The father was a veteran. His daughter vanished while traveling on a remote island. The father came to report the disappearance, but the police could not have cared less — the island’s police were all in the local gang’s pocket. The father had to dig on his own, and the residents all swore they had never seen her. After a year of dead ends, the father found an anonymous note in his room: someone was quietly telling the father that the daughter’s death was tied to the local gang. So the father paid a large sum to hire a woman of the night, dressed the woman in the same red outfit the daughter wore in the photograph, and planted the woman inside the gang as a mole. The mole at last uncovered the truth of the daughter’s disappearance, and the father resolved to take revenge with his own hands. The “woman in red” seen on the island a year later was that mole. Every gang member who crossed the mole’s path was quietly eliminated, one after another, and the father himself went underground, “vanishing” from people’s eyes. And I am a minor boss of the island gang: that night I saw the daughter out walking in red — just my type. I meant to take her by force; she fought back, so I killed her — the police here were all my people anyway, and no one would dare give me up. When word came that the girl’s father was on the island digging around, I wasn’t worried in the least; veteran or not, the father was nothing to me. Then my men told me they had found another red-dressed target to my taste, and this “woman in red” was far more agreeable than the last. We got along beautifully, and I told the woman in red all my glorious deeds — never suspecting the woman in red was the mole the father had planted. The father had gone to ground on the island, and my men began to disappear one by one. I was afraid; I made ready to flee. Just as I stepped aboard a boat, the cold mouth of a gun pressed against my back. I knew: I was about to disappear too.
hints: The woman in red is tied to the father, but she is not the missing daughter herself.
Those who vanish are tied to the daughter’s death back then.
The father hired someone to wear his daughter’s red and infiltrate the gang for proof, then took his revenge; me is the man who killed the daughter.

title: Splash, Splash, Bang
story: Splash, splash — bang! Splash, splash — thud! Splash, splash — swish, swish… glub, glub, glub…
answer: A loving couple lived by the sea. The husband worked late year-round and was seldom home; the wife took a lover, and when the husband found out, the marriage shattered. In a violent quarrel, a shove sent the husband’s temple into the corner of a table, and the husband sank into a deathlike coma. The wife, numb with shock, took a long while to come back to herself, then decided to see it through to the end: the wife would dump the “body” into the sea. Under cover of night the wife carried the husband on her back toward the water. At first the wife left the body on the shallows, but the waves kept washing the body ashore, so the wife had to wade deeper and deeper. Beneath the long wash of seawater the husband stirred back to life, weak as the husband was, and clutched at the wife with the grip of a dying man’s will to live; the wife’s strength gave out before the wife could reach the shore, and the couple drowned together in the sea. It began with the sea, and it ended with the sea. The sounds, in order: the waves; the boom of fireworks at the couple’s wedding; the thud of the husband falling; the swish and drag of bodies hauled through the water; and at the last, the bubbles rising as the couple drowned.
hints: The string of sounds spans more than one point in time.
Beside the waves there was first a wedding, and later a quarrel and a body thrown into the sea.
The husband was believed dead; he woke in the water and seized his wife, and in the end both drowned.

title: The Photo He Sent Back
story: I swapped photos with an online friend I’d only recently met. When I saw the photo he sent back, I was puzzled — wasn’t that a photo of me? The next day, a murder was discovered in my home.
answer: I had met someone through the “Shake” feature and we got along well, so I suggested we each send a photo to see what we each looked like. I sent the online friend a selfie, and after a while the online friend sent a photo back — and the photo was that very selfie of mine. As I puzzled over the photo, I looked closely and noticed: in the photo, the wardrobe behind me stood open a crack, and a face showed through the gap. This online friend had long since broken into my home and was hiding in the wardrobe behind me; sending my own selfie back unchanged was the online friend’s way of telling me “I’m right behind you.” The next day, I was found dead in my own home.
hints: The photo he sent back was indeed the one she had just taken.
Pay attention to the background behind the person in the selfie.
The online friend was hiding in the wardrobe behind her, and his face had been caught in that selfie too.

title: His Sister’s Toys
story: The first time I visited my fiancé’s home, his sister sat clutching a few small garments, counting them one by one: “One, two, three, five… gone again.” He told me to pay her no mind. As I bent to gather the toys scattered on the floor, I saw a wedding photo on her bedside table. The door locked behind me.
answer: The woman my fiancé called his “sister” was the first wife this family had abducted. She had borne three children and then a pair of twins, and all five had been sold off. She kept the children’s clothes and toys, counting the taken children over and over. Afraid I would keep asking questions, my fiancé had lied and passed her off as his sister. In the wedding photo on the bedside table, the groom was my fiancé himself. Only then did I understand that this pre-wedding visit was a trap the family had set: the family had brought me home to take the first wife’s place. The moment I saw the photo, my fiancé — who had been watching my every move — locked the door from outside.
hints: The count jumps from three straight to five — meaning two were added at once.
The clothes and toys belonged to the children she lost, one after another.
The “sister” was really the fiancé’s first wife; the wedding photo gives the lie to his story.

title: That Was Fast
story: I called building management to report a clogged toilet. Soon someone came knocking, and I said to him: “That was fast — the bathroom’s this way.”
answer: The man at the door was the killer, who had just finished his work upstairs. He had flushed parts of the body down the drain and found the pipes clogged; afraid the remains would surface when the downstairs tenant sent for a plumber, he hurried down to knock on my door. I had just reported the clog to building management, so when he arrived so quickly I naturally took him for the worker management had sent, and even led him straight to the bathroom. The killer seized on this misunderstanding to deal with the clog before the real repairman showed up.
hints: The visitor knew the toilet might be clogged, but had received no dispatch from building management.
The clog came from upstairs.
The killer, who had done his work upstairs, rushed down to deal with the remains before they surfaced; the tenant who had just filed the repair mistook him for a plumber.

title: A Calendar of Love
story: Xiaohong wanted to fall in love. In January, she fell in love, and spared no cost for it. In February, she lost it. In March, she fell in love, and shouldered a sweet new burden. In April, she lost it. In May, she fell in love, and this time he would never leave her again. In June, she lost it. In July, the police opened the door.
answer: In January, Xiaohong met a handsome man on a dating app and the two fell for each other fast. The man turned out to be a con artist who kept borrowing money from Xiaohong in the name of raising funds for a project. In February, having drained Xiaohong’s savings, the scammer vanished with an excuse about the investment failing and lying low out of town. In March, Xiaohong sold off her own possessions and borrowed from everyone she knew to seek the scammer out again; seeing Xiaohong still had value to squeeze, he went to work on Xiaohong once more, promising to marry Xiaohong once his business troubles were settled. Sweet-talked at every turn, Xiaohong transferred money to him again and again, until Xiaohong was saddled with loans. In April, Xiaohong discovered he was also carrying on hot and heavy with another woman, and the lines in the chat history were word for word the lines he had used on Xiaohong; hatred and a twisted love devoured Xiaohong. In May, Xiaohong lured the woman out and killed her, then drugged him and locked him in the basement. He woke to see the mistress’s corpse and was scared half to death, weeping and swearing he would love only Xiaohong from then on. At last Xiaohong had the world-for-two Xiaohong had wanted — but even the world-for-two was not enough: Xiaohong wanted him to be unable to live without Xiaohong. So, bit by bit, Xiaohong cut off his hands and feet and gouged out his eyes, turning him into a complete invalid. In June, Xiaohong’s possessiveness reached its limit; to make sure he could never change his heart, Xiaohong killed him, cut out his heart, and ate it. In the end, buried in loans and stripped of everything, Xiaohong took her own life. In July, the police opened the door and found three bodies.
hints: All three loves were the same man.
The first two relationships were held together by money; the third, by captivity.
She went from being swindled out of her money to imprisoning and mutilating him, and in the end walked toward her own death too; the police found three bodies.

title: Two Documents
story: Two documents, one corpse, and a pen.
answer: The corpse of an infant; a birth certificate and a death certificate; and the same pen that signed both. The baby died soon after being born, and the doctor in attendance used one pen to sign first the child’s birth certificate, then the child’s death certificate.
hints: Both documents were signed by the same doctor.
One records a life’s beginning; the other, its end.
The infant died shortly after birth, and the doctor signed the birth certificate, then the death certificate.

title: Two Athletes
story: Lately, two athletes have been keeping me up all night. One, armed with a very long piece of equipment, does exactly as he pleases; the other — the less he wears, the more excited I get. It’s just that neither of them seems much interested in my body, and that stings a little.
answer: “I” am the owner of the house in Plants vs. Zombies, and day and night a horde of zombies comes to attack the house. Two of the zombies are especially hard to deal with. One is the pole-vaulting zombie, who carries a long pole in both hands and wears a tracksuit; with that pole the pole-vaulting zombie does exactly as the zombie pleases, vaulting straight over my defenses. The other is the football zombie, suited up head to toe in football armor — nothing knocks the football zombie down. But once the plants blast that armor off, the football zombie is nothing but skin and bone, gone in one hit. The “long equipment” is the vaulting pole; “the less the zombie wears, the more excited I get” is the football zombie stripped of that armor. And the reason neither of the two zombies cares about my body is that what the two zombies truly want to eat is my brain.
hints: This scene takes place inside a video game.
The long equipment is a vaulting pole; the clothes are football armor.
me is the homeowner in Plants vs. Zombies; the two athletes are the pole-vaulting zombie and the football zombie.

title: A Wish on a Falling Star
story: I bowed my head and made a wish. The wish came true, and I cried.
answer: Dad was an astronaut, away on a mission, and I missed Dad terribly. That night, gazing up at the stars and thinking of Dad, I suddenly saw a falling star, and at once bowed my head and made my wish: for Dad to come home early. The wish came true — Dad did come home sooner than planned. What I never imagined was that the “falling star” I had seen was Dad’s ship, wrecked and falling back into the atmosphere. That was how Dad “came home.” I broke down sobbing.
hints: Her wish concerned someone working far away.
She wanted her astronaut father to come home sooner.
What she took for a falling star was her father’s ship, falling back to Earth after the accident.

title: Six Farewell Notes
story: “You have disappointed me so deeply. I am never coming back.” That sentence appeared six times in all. I knew I was in trouble.
answer: After I killed my wife, I tried to dress the killing up as my wife storming out in anger. I practiced imitating my wife’s handwriting over and over, writing out “You have disappointed me so deeply. I am never coming back.” The first five attempts came out wrong; I crumpled them and threw them in the bin. Only the sixth served as my wife’s farewell letter, mailed to my wife’s family. When the police investigated the wife’s disappearance, they found those drafts in the house, summoned the letter that had arrived, and laid all six sheets in front of me. The same sentence, from a stiff imitation to a near match for my wife’s hand: a complete record of the forgery.
hints: The sentence appeared six times because one person wrote it again and again.
Someone was practicing to imitate the wife’s handwriting.
The husband killed his wife and forged a farewell letter; the police found five drafts plus the one that was mailed.

title: A Wonderful Journey
story: A truly wonderful journey. What was that thing? Why did no one answer our calls? What had happened? We had to do something — we absolutely could not let that thing pass. And it seemed we had done something that could never be undone.
answer: In the future, a married couple set out on a trip aboard a civilian spacecraft and strayed into a two-way time wormhole that had stayed open, which delivered the couple to the late Cretaceous. Not knowing what era the couple was in, the husband and wife called Earth and got no answer — and then found an asteroid barreling along a course straight for the planet. Using the backup propulsion unit carried on board, the couple nudged the asteroid off the asteroid’s orbit, then flew back through the wormhole the way the couple had come, on the ship’s still-working main engine. When the couple returned to the era of departure, the Earth had changed beyond recognition. The impact the couple had dodged was the one that would have wiped out the dinosaurs and countless other species; with that event averted, everything afterward unfolded differently.
hints: This trip went wrong in time.
The object they stopped was the one that was supposed to strike Earth in the past.
They arrived in the late Cretaceous and prevented the impact that wiped out the dinosaurs; by the time they got back, history had taken another branch.

title: The Strange Symbol
story: This old castle really did hold a secret. As I touched the charred corpse, an unfamiliar symbol swam into my view. It hurts… where am I… By a faint light I searched my surroundings. At that very moment, something happened — and there, in the bright blaze, I saw the symbol once more. I understood everything, but it was already too late.
answer: By touching a corpse, I can see the last thing the dead person saw before dying. In the castle, I laid my hand on a burned body and saw thick smoke, firelight, and a strange symbol. Pressing deeper into the castle, I missed my footing and fell into a hidden chamber. Lighting a match, I read the experiment notes on the wall: at fixed intervals, the altar at the chamber’s center transports whatever rests on the altar to the castle’s great hall as the hall was one day earlier; the time and objects around the altar do not go back with the transported object. Beside the notes was drawn that very symbol. Before I could find a way out, my dropped match set fire to the flammable debris scattered across the floor. The flames drove me up onto the altar, and the symbol in the smoke closed over the dying vision I had just read about. After I died, my body was carried to the hall as the hall stood the day before — waiting for the me who had not yet entered the chamber to come and touch the body.
hints: The symbol that appears when he touches a corpse is what the dead person saw in their final moment.
The device in the castle sends whatever is on the altar to the hall as it stood one day earlier.
The charred corpse in the hall is me himself, later in time; he read his own dying vision in advance.

title: That Sound
story: Late at night, I stepped out the door. A few steps on, the sound rang in my ears. I turned and looked back at nothing at all. I panicked: this was bad — really bad.
answer: I had been out with friends and took a taxi home late at night. After getting off at my destination and walking a few steps, the chime suddenly sounded in my ears: “Bluetooth disconnected.” I turned around; the taxi was already gone — my phone and my bag were still inside the taxi, and there was nothing behind me at all. I panicked: this was bad — really bad.
hints: The sound came from an electronic device.
After stepping out of the car, its wireless link to another carried item was cut.
The earbuds announced the Bluetooth disconnection, and only then did me realize the phone and bag had been left in the taxi, already driving away.

title: The Murmured Name
story: A beach float drifted on the sea five kilometers from shore, and in it curled a woman at the edge of death. The moment the police pulled her out, relief washed over her and she fainted — a name still murmuring on her lips.
answer: The woman’s parents chartered Captain Harry’s sailboat for a vacation at sea, bringing her and her little sister along. Woken by noise in the dead of night, the woman found her parents already murdered in the cabin; she rushed on deck to find the little sister — soaked in blood, barely alive — and Captain Harry holding an axe. Harry, it turned out, was a repeat offender who killed for insurance by staging accidents; he had done away with his own ex-wife the same way. This time Harry had planned to fake a shipwreck, kill his own wife for the payout, and pass off the chartering family as witnesses to the accident; when the family stumbled onto the plan, Harry simply killed the whole family to silence the witnesses. On deck, the woman thought fast: she turned around and begged Harry for “help,” playing someone who knew nothing at all. By then the boat was burning and sinking, and launching the lifeboat needed her cooperation aboard, so Harry spared her a while longer. But as Harry rode the lifeboat around to catch her jumping ship, she simply let go of the rope. Convinced she could never survive alone, Harry took the little sister’s body and left, spinning a survival-at-sea story for the outside world. What Harry never imagined was that the woman stayed alive on the beach float the family had brought along, until the police rescued her — and the name murmuring on her lips was “Harry,” the killer himself. Summoned by the police, Harry knew the lie had collapsed; in the end Harry committed suicide in fear of punishment, driving his car off a cliff.
hints: Her float had been brought along for the family’s outing at sea.
The captain survived too, but the shipwreck story he told the world left things out.
The captain did the killing and staged the wreck; the girl escaped on the float, and the name she spoke can expose him.

title: What Are You Doing?
story: “What are you doing? What are you doing?”I looked over in terror.“Me? I’m not doing anything.” He strolled over, all smiles.His smile faded.I knew I was done for.
answer: I was a novice burglar. I had meant to slip in while the owner was out, but my stakeout failed and I ran into the owner coming home, so I knocked the owner out and got ready to bolt. Just then, the gas company inspector rang the bell. Out of reflex I answered, then had to drag the unconscious owner onto the nearest balcony to hide the man and play the owner myself — the inspector would only check the kitchen, surely nothing could go wrong. But the moment the inspection ended, the owner’s parrot suddenly shrieked, repeating over and over the very words the owner had cried before being attacked: “What are you doing! What are you doing!” The shriek gave me a fright. As it happened, the inspector kept birds himself; beaming, the inspector chattered on about bird-keeping and replied, “Me? I’m not doing anything,” following the parrot’s commotion toward the balcony. At the sight of the knocked-out owner, the inspector’s smile slowly faded. I knew I was done for.
hints: The first voice repeating itself didn’t belong to a person.
It had learned the words the owner cried out just before being attacked.
The parrot kept repeating the cry for help, and the gas inspector, following the sound, saw the real owner lying unconscious.

title: Rewriting the Ending
story: I was reborn.This time, I would turn my ending around for sure.The man beside me said something offhand,and in my rage, I killed him.
answer: I was reborn just as the French Revolution broke out. In my last life I had died on the guillotine; this time, I was determined to turn my death around. While plotting next steps with the man beside me, he said: “When the time comes, we’ll head our separate ways.” With the guillotine filling my head, the word “head” was more than I could bear — in a flash of rage, I killed him.
hints: In his last life, the protagonist died on the guillotine.
The sentence contained a word that reminded him of how he had died.
The subordinate said they would head their separate ways; hearing “head,” the reborn man lost control and killed him.

title: My Daughter’s Voice
story: Hearing my daughter’s voice, I was terrified. She was screaming hysterically, pouring out how her parents abused her mercilessly at home. I decided that once I got back, I would punish this lying daughter of mine properly — she had promised me, after all, that she would never tell anyone about it.
answer: I am the girl’s mother, and I work as an operator on a helpline. My daughter had long been suffering abuse at home, and the girl had promised me never, ever to tell anyone about it. That day, on my shift, a call for help came in — and the voice on the line was my daughter’s: screaming hysterically, sobbing about how her parents abused her mercilessly at home, while the person answering the call for help was none other than the abusive mother herself. I was terrified; then I calmed down and began to quietly think over how, once I got home, I would punish this promise-breaking, “lying” daughter of mine.
hints: The daughter is calling a helpline for help.
The mother’s job puts her on the receiving end of strangers’ calls for help.
The mother is the very operator who took the call — and the very abuser the daughter is denouncing.

title: The Woman at the Car Window
story: I was about to drive off when a woman rushed over, pounding on the car window. I was set on just driving away — but then she took off her clothes, so I let her into the car.
answer: The zombies had just appeared in the city, and I was getting ready to drive out of the city. In this story, the infection spreads through bites. The woman pounded on the window, begging me for a ride; I was afraid the woman had already been bitten and didn’t dare open the door. The woman saw my hesitation, took off the outer clothes, and turned around so I could inspect the woman’s body — not a bite mark to be seen. That gesture won the woman the ride: I let the woman into the car, and we drove off together, away from the streets that were slipping out of control.
hints: The woman was begging for help; she undressed so I could check for something.
The danger outside has to do with an infection that spreads.
It’s a zombie-outbreak world; she was showing me she bore no bite wounds.

title: The SOS Text
story: “But your daughter already took her own life last year.” “No — she’s alive. She only ran away from home. Look, she just texted me begging for help. She’s been kidnapped, someone is controlling her. Officer, you have to catch the man who did this.” “Ma’am, thanks to you, we cracked this case.” “It was nothing. It was all for my daughter.” “We are very sorry to tell you: your daughter truly is dead.” When the truth came out, the mother went mad.
answer: After running away from home, the daughter had burned herself to death with gasoline — a “suicide.” The mother refused to believe the daughter was dead, and kept digging into the truth of that suicide. The mother uncovered an organization of suicides: once you joined, you were never allowed to change your mind; anyone who tried to leave was forced by the group to kill themselves. The mother became certain the daughter had been murdered by this organization. So the mother forged a text that seemed to be the daughter’s plea for help, reported the text to the police, and handed over every clue the mother had dug up. The police followed the trail to the organization’s hideout, while the mother personally set a trap and burned the leader to death with gasoline — the mother’s revenge complete. Then the police told the mother a shattering truth: the daughter WAS the leader of that organization. The daughter’s death a year earlier had been faked, and only hours ago the daughter had died in a sudden gasoline explosion. The one who had personally burned the daughter to death was the mother herself.
hints: The plea for help “from the daughter” was forged by the mother herself.
The daughter did not really kill herself a year ago — she was later tied to the organization’s leader.
The daughter was the leader, alive behind her faked death; the revenge fire her mother set ended up killing her.

title: Abandon Ship
story: “Captain, sound the alarm and order every soldier to the escape pods. Tell them the ship has malfunctioned — all hands, abandon ship.”
answer: To steal intelligence from Country A’s lunar base, Country B had planted a spy inside A’s military. After years undercover, the spy finally got a chance to carry the intel drive home and boarded the spaceship back to Earth. But Country A had long known a mole existed, and Country A’s detective had narrowed the suspects to a few dozen men and quietly booked every one of those men onto that same ship. The detective told the captain to announce a malfunction and send all the soldiers to the escape pods. Unwilling to give up the only chance to bring the intel home, the spy kept the drive on the spy’s body — and was caught red-handed in the belongings check before entering the pod. The ship landed safely in Country A, the spy was arrested, and the “detective” walked off with the drive to report success. The captain went back to his cabin relieved, savoring another great service the captain had rendered — then heard a strange noise from the machine room. The captain opened the door: on the floor, bound with rope and gagged, a man was struggling — the man was Country A’s real detective. Among the soldiers there had been one more spy — a master of disguise from Country C. Tipped off about the sting in advance, the Country C spy had knocked the real detective out and taken the real detective’s place; by then, the Country C spy was already back in Country C with the intel.
hints: The abandon-ship order would force anyone carrying the intel to bring it out with him.
The spy among the soldiers was not the only man aboard with a false identity.
The detective giving the orders had been replaced by a spy from a third country, who used the first spy’s capture to walk away with the intel.

title: Two People Up There
story: On a small road in a remote village stood an eerie utility pole. The villagers said strange things had happened there again and again — a while back, someone had ridden straight into it on a motorcycle. One night a father and son came down that road on their bike. The boy stared at the pole ahead and suddenly said, “Dad, there are two people up there.” The father’s heart jumped in fright. The next day, two bodies were found lying beside the pole.
answer: This remote village didn’t have a single streetlight at night, and the authorities never concerned themselves with such things. The darkness made crashes constant — a while back, a motorcyclist speeding through had failed to see the pole and slammed into the pole. So the villagers themselves put up a notice board at the foot of the pole: 交通安全，人人有责 — “Traffic safety is everyone’s duty.” That night the father and son came past on a motorcycle as well, and the dim light fell on the board beneath the pole. The innocent boy was looking at the two 人 characters in 人人有责 — 人 being the written character for “person” — and said, “There are two people up there.” But the father took the words to mean two real people stood on top of the pole; in alarm the father turned back to glance at the boy, and in that one unguarded moment the motorcycle rammed into the pole. Father and son both died on the spot.
hints: The “two people” the boy spoke of were not two physical beings.
There was a safety notice on the pole.
The boy was seeing the two 人 characters of the sign; the father misunderstood, lost his focus, and hit the pole.

title: Whose Flashlight?
story: My girlfriend is afraid of the dark, and both her hands clutched my left hand tight. I freed my right hand to hold up my phone, and saw that the flashlight beam ahead had already reached the house beside the exit. I was about to tell her we could go out when something suddenly felt wrong. Which of us was holding the flashlight?
answer: On that forest path in the dead of night, I was gripping both of my girlfriend’s hands, and my one remaining hand was holding up the phone — neither of us had any flashlight. And yet a beam of light kept leading the way ahead. When I turned my head, I saw a figure with no lower half hanging in the air behind us, a flashlight raised in the figure’s hand. What had lit our way the whole way here was that very figure. Only when I saw the exit did I notice this extra beam of light.
hints: Both people’s hands were occupied.
The flashlight lighting the way came from a third presence behind them.
me was holding both of the girlfriend’s hands and his phone; the flashlight was carried the whole way by the ghost tailing them.

title: The Monsters Behind Me
story: Looking at the monsters behind me, I gave up. Looking at what lay around me, I despaired. Looking at the presence before me and the gun in my hand, I went mad.
answer: When the food ran out and the bullets were nearly gone, I looked at the countless monsters behind me and sank into despair. So I covered my son’s eyes and, to spare my son the greater pain, shot my son dead. Looking at my dead son beside me, I prepared, in despair, to kill myself. But in the very next moment, the army that existed to destroy the monsters appeared before me and wiped out the monsters at my back. Looking at the rescue in front of me and my son lying dead beside me, I went utterly mad.
hints: me believed no rescue would ever come.
To keep his son from falling into the monsters’ hands, he killed the boy first.
The army arrived right afterward and destroyed the monsters; only then did he learn the killing had never been necessary.

title: The Midnight Suitcase
story: One question too many. One corpse too many. One purchase too many.
answer: Late that night, a delivery runner brought a large suitcase to a customer’s home. The door stood open, and the customer was dragging a rolled-up carpet toward the suitcase. Noticing the red streaks on the floor, the runner asked one question too many: “Why is there so much blood?” Realizing the runner had seen what shouldn’t have been seen, the customer pulled the runner inside and killed the runner. The suitcase had been meant to hold the person killed before; now there was one more body, so the customer had no choice but to place another order and buy one more suitcase.
hints: The newly bought item was meant to hold a corpse.
The person making the delivery saw something wrong — and asked about it out loud.
The runner delivering the suitcase noticed the blood and was silenced by the killer, who then had to buy one more suitcase.

title: The Failure
story: “I’m sorry — it’s a failure,” I told the man who came to test the machine.In court I kept explaining desperately: “It has always been accurate.”The public gallery laughed. In the end, only one sentence was left to me: “I am a human.”
answer: I had built a machine that could tell humans from pseudo-humans, and the machine’s readings were accurate. The first man who came to test the machine was judged a pseudo-human. Terrified that the man would find out, I declared the machine a failure, and then, in panic, killed the man. I was arrested for the killing, and in court I insisted the dead man had been a pseudo-human, demanding that the machine be allowed to test everyone present. The police, the judge, the spectators — every single one came back pseudo-human, and took the results as proof that the machine was broken. I nearly believed that myself, until I stepped into the detection field and the screen read “human.” The police and the courts of this city had long since been taken over by pseudo-humans. I am still pleading my innocence to the police and the courts — but what the authorities need to confirm is that final reading.
hints: The machine identifies a certain kind of being, and that first claim of “failure” was a lie.
The readings in court were strikingly consistent — and the machine truly was accurate.
The police, the judge, and the gallery were all pseudo-humans; the inventor was the one human they had surrounded.

title: The Missing
story: The first time I tried this gift of mine, I nearly suffocated myself. Once I got the hang of it, I could always eat for free and take what I pleased. That day I slipped into a restaurant again — and this time I really did die inside. A few days later, my family was still out putting up missing-person flyers everywhere.
answer: My gift is this: the moment I stop breathing, my body and the clothes I am wearing turn invisible; when I breathe again, I reappear. I would often hold my breath to slip into restaurants, then hide in some corner no one watched and eat. That day I ate too fast; food jammed my airway, my breath stopped, and my body vanished on the spot. I thrashed and collapsed in the corner, and no one noticed anything happening there. Once I suffocated to death, I never breathed again — so the corpse never reappeared. My family cannot find me; in my family’s eyes, I am still a missing person.
hints: He has a supernatural ability tied to breathing.
The ability only stops working when he starts breathing again.
Not breathing turns him invisible; after he suffocated, the corpse stayed invisible forever.

title: The Fortune-Teller’s Prophecy
story: A fortune-teller told him that he would die of a heart attack. He took up exercise and started looking after his health — and in the end, he died all the same.
answer: The fortune-teller had prophesied that he would die of a heart attack, so he began to exercise and take scrupulous care of himself. One day, out on a training ride, a car swerved sharply and struck him; through the car’s window he could see an old man slumped unconscious over the wheel. Only in that last moment did he understand — the fortune-teller had never been wrong about the heart attack. He really did die of one; it was simply that the heart which failed belonged to someone else.
hints: The prophecy never specified whose heart would go wrong.
He was hit by a car while exercising.
The driver’s heart attack made him lose control — the indirect cause of the death.

title: He Was Counting, Too
story: I leaned at the window, counting the building across the street floor by floor. Halfway through, the man in that building looked up — and started counting toward my window as well.
answer: From my window I had witnessed a murder in the building opposite. When I called the police, the officer asked me which floor the murder had happened on, so I counted from the bottom up. By the time I reached the man’s floor, he had noticed me too. Then he began counting, floor by floor, toward my side of the street — to work out which floor the witness lived on. I had only meant to make the address clear; in that instant I realized that the man was the killer, and that he, too, was looking for my address.
hints: Both of them were counting the floors of the building opposite them.
me, to make the address clear to the police; the killer, to find the witness.
He saw the murder across the street; the killer saw him too, and began counting up to his floor.

title: The Red Shadow in the Morgue
story: Xiao Chen worked at a funeral home. That day, the body of a woman dressed in red was brought in from outside. Xiao Chen glanced at the death report and was stunned: the deceased was Xiao Hong, the high-school classmate he had once been fond of, and the memories came flooding back. After graduation the two had kept in touch, but Xiao Hong became an actress, and before long a famous star; Xiao Chen, feeling unworthy of her, had let the contact fade away. That night, the more he remembered, the more restless he grew, and the night-shift man got up to make his rounds of the morgue. The morgue at night was cold and silent, and even Xiao Chen, usually so fearless, felt a creeping unease. Suddenly he seemed to see a streak of red deep in the corridor slip around a corner. “Who’s there!” he shouted, and gave chase — only to hear, from the far end of the corridor past that corner, a door open and footsteps hurry away. Xiao Chen ran to the corner: the side corridor was empty, but one of the rooms stood open, and inside it a mortuary drawer hung half pulled-out — in it lay Xiao Hong’s body. When day came, Xiao Chen told everyone the morgue was haunted and they should cremate Xiao Hong’s body soon. His colleagues all laughed at him; the boss gave him two days off to rest. But Xiao Chen refused to let it go, and that night he sneaked back into the funeral home behind the boss’s back. The next day, the police found Xiao Chen’s body in the cremation room. The strange smile on his face chilled everyone who saw it.
answer: Xiao Hong had died in an accident after becoming a famous star. A rich merchant had bribed the funeral home’s boss with a fortune to buy Xiao Hong’s body — to be ghost-married to the merchant’s son, dead before his time. That first night, the boss came to the morgue to swap Xiao Hong’s body out and smuggle the corpse away, and Xiao Chen’s patrol footsteps sounded in the corridor; the door and the hurrying footsteps Xiao Chen heard were the boss fleeing in panic. To get Xiao Chen out of the way, the boss simply gave Xiao Chen those days off. The next night the boss came again to make the swap — and walked straight into Xiao Chen, who had slipped back in. The boss offered to split the money with Xiao Chen; refused, the boss struck Xiao Chen with a blunt weapon. But Xiao Chen, out that night to “catch the ghost,” had brought a dagger to protect himself — and killed the boss instead. Mortally wounded, Xiao Chen lay on the floor, knowing there was little time left. In a haze, Xiao Chen seemed to see the red-clad figure appear before Xiao Chen once more, weeping as the figure asked: “Are you still willing to be with me?” Only then did Xiao Chen understand that the figure in the corridor that night had been Xiao Hong’s ghost. With his last strength, Xiao Chen dragged Xiao Hong’s body to the cremation room, so that Xiao Hong would never be given to a ghost marriage, and died there with a smile on his face.
hints: The sounds in the morgue and the red shadow did not necessarily come from the same being.
The boss meant to sell the dead star’s body for a ghost marriage.
The sounds were the boss smuggling the body out; the red shadow was her ghost; Xiao Chen gave his life to cremate the body and protect her.

title: Caught in the Frame
story: Faced with the corpse before me, I was vexed beyond words. But after wasting a great deal of time, I finally had a result I could be proud of — and I showed it all off. Then I saw the other man’s result, and the smile died on my face.
answer: I am an “underground reporter” working the gray zone, racing around every day to beat my rivals to a story. That day I happened to see a criminal bolt from a house, so I slipped inside to film — but the corpse’s position framed terribly. Impatient for my scoop, I moved the body, set the composition, and got a photograph I was satisfied with. When I showed the photograph off to the other man, he laid down a photo of me in the very act of moving the corpse — the mantis stalking the cicada, with the oriole right behind. My tampering with the crime scene had been caught dead-on camera, and now nothing I said could clear my name.
hints: Both men’s “results” were photographs.
To get a photograph he was satisfied with, me had tampered with the scene.
He moved the corpse to take his picture — and a rival photographed him moving it.

title: Ants on the Ceiling
story: On my second day in the apartment, I wiped out the ants on the floor. On the third day it rained and the bedroom ceiling leaked, so I called the landlord. At midnight I was woken again by dripping water, and when I looked up, the ants had all crawled onto the ceiling. Right then the landlord’s voice sounded outside the door: “Go ahead and open up. I’ve come to fix it.”
answer: The landlord had killed someone and hidden the body in the crawl space above the ceiling, then rented the place out to me in a hurry. At first I had only seen the ants swarming around a dropped snack on the floor, and thought wiping the ants out would be the end of it. Rain seeped into the cavity and began to drip, carrying fluids of decay with it, and the ants gathered again along the leaking crack. At midnight I followed the ants’ trail upward and saw, behind the loosened plaster, the exposed length of a human finger. I had already told the landlord where the leak was; the landlord knew something had gone wrong with his hiding place and hurried over to deal with it. Now the landlord is right outside the door.
hints: Where the ants reappeared matters more than how many there were.
Something is hidden above the ceiling, and the leaking water has passed through it.
The landlord hid the body in the crawl space; the repair call also told him his secret was coming out.

title: The Dancing Bystander
story: I danced, happily watching the companions in front of me die.
answer: I am a sunflower from the game Plants vs. Zombies. In that unreal world I am not a human being but a plant. In battle I sway my body with a smile on my face, “dancing,” happily watching the companions in front of me — plant after plant — being devoured by zombies and dying.
hints: me is not human.
It comes from a game where plants defend against zombies.
It is the ever-swaying, smiling sunflower of Plants vs. Zombies.

title: Your Delivery Is Here
story: “Ma’am, your delivery is here. Please open the door and take it.”Over the course of the day, that line sounded four times.The fourth time, I opened the door — and was never able to close it again.
answer: I was the killer who posed as a deliveryman to get inside. The first time, I used that line to trick a woman into opening her door. While I was at work, the real deliveryman arrived and said the same words a second time; I pulled the deliveryman in and killed the man too, taking the man’s phone and uniform. Following the next order on the deliveryman’s phone, I went to another home and knocked a third time with the same line. Neighbors near the first scene heard the commotion and called the police. The police found the dead deliveryman, learned from his orders where his next stop was, and came after me. When I heard the knock called out a fourth time, I assumed yet another real deliveryman had arrived — I opened the door and found the police already waiting for me.
hints: The four lines were spoken by people with different identities.
me posed as a deliveryman and later killed the real one.
Tracing the deliveryman’s orders from the first crime scene, the police caught the killer at the fourth knock.

title: Blank as Paper
story: At twenty I met her, pure as a blank sheet of paper. Two years later we married. At twenty-five I lost the love of my life and threw myself wholly into my work. At forty-five, as the project neared its end, an accident happened — and heaven took away the one I loved most, once again. Staring at the data before me, I felt a dark foreboding rise. When the test results came back, I went mad.
answer: At twenty I met her wandering the streets with nowhere to go: she seemed to have lost her memory, with no idea who she was or where she had come from. I kindly took her in; simple and good-hearted, she became a ray of light in my life, and we fell in love and married. At twenty-five my wife died in childbirth after giving me a daughter, and from then on I devoted myself single-mindedly to science. My daughter grew up to look more and more like her mother. At forty-five I built a working time machine, though the technology was still unstable. Just as I was preparing further safety tests, the accident happened — my daughter started the machine on her own and never came back; the transmission log showed her destination as twenty-five years in the past. Dark foreboding rose in me. I ran a DNA comparison between strands of my daughter’s hair and the lock of my wife’s hair I had kept for many years, and the match was exact: the amnesiac she had been back then was my own daughter, thrown back through time. I went mad.
hints: The moment the daughter vanished lines up with the moment the wife first appeared.
The wife had amnesia when they first met; the daughter stepped into a time machine.
Sent back twenty-five years, the daughter became the young wife her father met — and her own mother.

title: What About Tonight?
story: It was my first visit to my online boyfriend’s home, and we spent the whole afternoon playing games. One round got so intense I couldn’t help shouting — and he suddenly looked over at me with a smile: “This loud already? What about tonight?” I blushed and swore at him. That night, sure enough, no one came to disturb us.
answer: My online boyfriend was a killer who used first meetings to hunt for victims. That afternoon, while I shouted over the game, the boyfriend kept listening for any stir outside the door. No neighbor knocked, and the killer took this to mean that even if I cried for help that night, no one would bother to come. I had heard “This loud already? What about tonight?” as a flirtatious joke. That night the killer turned on me, and I truly began to scream for help. No footsteps ever came to the door.
