hints: What he was watching for that afternoon was whether the shouting would bring anyone.
What happened that night was nothing like the flirtatious meaning I read into it.
He used my cries during the game to test the neighbors’ reactions, preparing for the night’s attack.

title: The Sole Survivor
story: A coach plunged into a valley. Of everyone who had ridden that bus that night, only one young man survived. When he was thrown off the bus, he still thought the driver hated him.
answer: Several thugs were on the bus, and seeing that the driver was a beautiful young woman, the thugs turned vicious. Once the bus reached the winding mountain road the thugs moved on the driver in front of everyone; only one frail young man on board stepped in to stop the thugs, and the thugs stabbed the young man for it. The other passengers all watched in silence, as if it were none of their business. After the thugs had their way, the thugs forced the driver to drive the route the thugs chose so the thugs could escape. The driver agreed — and at the same time angrily threw the wounded young man off the bus, cursing the young man as a useless good-for-nothing, and the other passengers chimed in with her. Wronged and injured, the young man had no choice but to make his way back on foot. The next day the young man saw the news of the coach falling into the valley: the driver had driven off the cliff, taking her own life together with a whole bus of bystanders who had looked the other way. To all appearances the driver had been angriest at the young man; in truth she had put the young man off the bus on purpose — and that young man, thrown off before the crash, was the sole survivor.
hints: The survivor had been put off the bus before the accident.
He had been the only one on board who helped the driver.
The driver drove away the one helper with curses, then sent the thugs and the bystanders over the cliff together.

title: Gentle Father
story: I’ve been happy lately: Father, who never used to come home, now often plays with me, and he has grown gentle too. The news says a research institute on the outskirts of our city exploded and they are still accounting for the victims. Father walks over, turns off the television, and gently strokes my head.
answer: Father worked at the institute developing androids. The father knew the illness was terminal and, fearing there would be no one left to keep me company, finished building a replica of himself and left behind arrangements for my care. Then the institute exploded, and the real father died inside. The completed android, following the arrangements the father had left, walked into the home and took over my daily care. The father of the old days, buried in work, had always been absent; the android beside me now always had time to play. When the news reached the victims of the institute, the android turned off the television and stroked my head.
hints: What the institute studied is tied to the change in the father at home.
The father had built an android copy of himself for his child.
The real father died at the institute; the one with the child is the machine he left behind.

title: A Cozy Home
story: Another day with nothing to show for it. I returned to my cozy home, wearily set down whatever was in my hands, intending to grab a simple dinner, went straight to the dining table and sat down, and took out a sandwich. The hairs on my body stood on end in an instant — I realized I was done for.
answer: I am a serial killer. Years ago I let a little brat slip through my fingers, and never knowing whether the girl would become a threat, I searched for the girl tirelessly all these years. My house is one I spent years collecting, crafting, and arranging with my own hands — a room furnished with human skin, bones, and taxidermy. I love my cozy home. Today, having failed once more to find the girl, I tossed my usual weapon on the shoe cabinet in the entryway, planning to grab a quick dinner. But the moment I sat down at the dining table, I found that the human chair beneath me was warm — someone had just been sitting there, and that someone was still in my house. My trusty weapon was far out of reach. Then a voice behind me spoke my name. I turned and saw the girl who had escaped me all those years ago, holding the weapon I had left in the entryway. I had hunted the girl for years; the girl had found my home first.
hints: me is himself a serial killer, and the furniture in his home is far from ordinary.
The lingering warmth on the chair means someone sat there only moments before.
The girl who escaped him has slipped into his house for revenge, while his weapon lies far away.

title: I Appeared
story: The man finished ransacking the drawers and walked out of the camera’s view. I sped up the playback, waiting to see when he would come back into frame. Nothing stirred on the screen. Then the door opened, and the one who came in was me, just home from work.
answer: Coming home from work, I found the place turned over and sat down to check the cameras. In the footage, after finishing with the drawers, the man had walked into the windowless bathroom. The only passage out of that bathroom stayed within the camera’s view the whole time, so I fast-forwarded and waited for him to emerge. He never did — not until the footage showed myself walking in the door after work. I finally understood: all the time I had been sitting there watching, he had been in the same house with me, and the bathroom door was still shut to this moment.
hints: me is watching recorded footage from home; the picture hasn’t caught up to the present.
The man who walked out of frame never left the house — he went into another room.
He never came out before me got home; he is still hiding inside.

title: My Heroes
story: Vicious, brutal thugs shattered my carefree life. Someone saved me. They are my heroes.
answer: I was a pig waiting for slaughter, living a carefree life on my master’s farm. That night, two travelers lodging there heard knife-sharpening in the yard and the words “bind it and kill it,” took the words to mean their host meant to murder the two travelers, and struck first, wiping out the master’s whole household — only afterward did the two travelers learn the knife was being sharpened to bind me up and butcher me to feed the guests. With the master dead, I would never be slaughtered: as far as a pig can see, it was those two “vicious, brutal thugs” who saved my life. The two travelers are my heroes. The story retells the Three Kingdoms tale of Cao Cao mistakenly slaughtering the family of Lü Boshe — told from that pig’s point of view.
hints: me is not human, and was to be killed to feed a guest.
What it overheard were preparations of the bind-and-butcher kind.
me is the pig Lü Boshe’s household meant to slaughter; Cao Cao’s mistaken killing is what saved it.

title: I Saw Myself
story: The man on the screen suddenly looked at me and reached out his hand. I hurriedly switched feeds, and this time what I saw was myself. And the man from just now.
answer: I am a hotel caretaker who secretly planted cameras in the guest rooms. That night I was going through the footage when I saw the man lift a girl’s body out of his suitcase. Then the man noticed the lens, walked toward the camera, and reached out a hand to cover the lens. Startled, I switched feeds — to the live view of the monitoring room itself — and saw first myself sitting before the screens, and then that man standing behind me. What I had been watching had happened long before; after finding the camera, the man had left the guest room and located the monitoring room. I had been glued to the recording and never noticed the man come in.
hints: me is spying through hidden hotel cameras.
What played before was recorded; only after the switch is the monitoring-room feed live.
The guest had long since found the monitoring room — switching to the live view revealed him standing behind me.

title: I Killed Myself
story: After a single gunshot, I had killed me. Yet this was not the death I had in mind.
answer: Ronald Opus leapt from the roof of his own apartment building, but as his body fell past the ninth floor a bullet chanced to fire from a window, killing Ronald on the spot. At that moment an elderly couple on the ninth floor were quarreling; the old man, as was his habit, was threatening his wife with a gun when the gun suddenly went off. The old woman was not hit — the bullet broke the window and struck Ronald in mid-fall. Both husband and wife insisted the gun should never have been loaded: brandishing the gun during quarrels was merely the old man’s habit, with no intent to kill. The police found that the chain of events began with the old woman’s decision to stop supporting her grown son financially. Cut off, the son nursed a grudge against his mother and secretly loaded the gun, hoping his father’s hand would kill the mother in some future quarrel. And that son was Ronald, the dead man himself. When the borrowed-knife plot refused to come off, Ronald sank into despair and decided to jump to his death — only to be shot dead by the very gun, fired from his own parents’ home on the ninth floor. In the end Ronald died from the bullet Ronald himself had put into the gun, though never in the way he had imagined when stepping off the roof.
hints: He had prepared a method of murder, and it later found him.
The gun was in the father’s hand; the bullet had been loaded by the son beforehand.
Falling past his parents’ window, the son was struck by his own pre-loaded bullet, fired by his father by mistake.

title: Found You
story: “Three, two… Are you all right? You’re safe now. Three, two, one… Found you.” Rat-a-tat-tat…
answer: As a child, “I” was playing hide-and-seek with my mother. My small body fit into the hidden compartment beneath the wardrobe, and through the one narrow gap I watched to see whether my mother could find me. Then a killer broke into our home. I heard my mother’s panicked footsteps as she fled (rat-a-tat-tat); my mother ran into the very room I was hiding in, and just as my mother tried to lock the door, the killer seized my mother and cut my mother’s throat. The killer simply watched as my mother’s life drained away little by little, then carved into my mother’s body with the knife, stroke by stroke — unnervingly quiet, slow, and methodical, as if sketching a work of art with lines. From the compartment I made no sound at all; perhaps I was frozen with terror, perhaps I was drawn to the sight. The police finally arrived and got me out, saying, “Are you all right? You’re safe now.” But what I had witnessed had already warped my mind: I could not forget the thrill of held breath, of a life snatched away in an instant, nor the artful lines the blade had drawn on that “canvas of life.” Grown up, I wanted to know what it felt like to hold another person’s fate in my hands — to toy with prey and watch the breath leave the prey little by little at my fingertips, and to create “artworks” of my own. So I began abducting prey, counting down to send the prey into hiding while I went to seek — “Found you” — and the prey I found, I killed.
hints: The two countdowns happened years apart.
The child who once hid grew into the one who seeks.
As a boy he witnessed his mother’s murder during hide-and-seek; as a man he turned that same game of hiding into a hunt.

title: Bloodstains in Midair
story: On the tenth floor of an apartment block, the doorway of one unit was soaked red with blood. In the pool lay a police cap and several photographs of corpses, each body bearing an identical wound on the neck. Two trails of blood: one ran to the railing outside and vanished into midair, the other led into the living room — to the smiling corpse of a woman. The police officer who arrived would never have guessed that the truth lay in his own phone.
answer: In this world, vampires live hidden among humans. As a child, the woman lost her parents to vampires, and the truth was buried by vampires nested in the upper ranks of society. The woman resolved to expose the vampires’ existence by extreme means: the woman attacked many innocent people and staged the scenes as vampire kills, leaving the very same wound on every “victim’s” neck, until public opinion began to stir. The vampires noticed the woman in turn, and sent a vampire disguised as a police officer, on the pretext of investigating the serial murders, to get inside the woman’s home — for a vampire cannot enter a human dwelling uninvited. The woman was ready for that, and shot the vampire at the woman’s door. The vampire dropped the disguise and, wounded, made ready to flee; the police cap and the photographs scattered into the pool of blood — photographs of the very “vampire attacks” the woman had staged. Nothing proves the existence of vampires like a vampire’s corpse, so the woman gave chase, only to be gravely wounded when the vampire turned on the woman, and the woman barely made it back inside. The badly hurt vampire had no time to tidy the scene; the wounded vampire rose over the railing and flew away, the vampire’s blood trail breaking off in midair, while the other trail remained in the living room the woman had crawled back into. But the woman’s purpose was already served: the whole fight had been streamed live to the internet by a hidden camera on the woman’s body. In the end the woman died at home from blood loss, smiling; the officer who came to investigate learned the truth from the live stream on the officer’s own phone.
hints: The investigator outside the door is no true human police officer.
One blood trail breaks off in midair because the wounded one can fly.
The woman baited out a vampire and streamed the fight live; the proof went online before she died, where the police can see it on his phone.

title: Thank You
story: “I don’t like you.” Hearing that, I was overjoyed. “I like you.” Hearing that, I burned with restless unease. “Thank you.” Hearing that, I fell into utter despair.
answer: I am a twisted stalker who planted a bug on the one I love. The woman is popular; there is always someone coming to confess to the woman, and every time I heard the woman turn someone down, I was overjoyed. But this time the woman accepted a certain man’s confession — and hearing that “I like you,” I burned with restless jealousy, tracked down who the man was, and killed the man. With the man gone, perhaps I still had a chance. Then the woman’s voice came through the monitor: “Ha — thank you for getting rid of the person I wanted dead.” The woman had discovered the bug long ago and knew I had been listening all along; that “thank you” was spoken to the bug, meant for me — the woman never liked the man at all. Accepting the man’s confession was simply the woman’s way of borrowing my hands to remove someone the woman, too, wanted dead. Hearing that, I fell into utter despair.
hints: me has been eavesdropping on his beloved’s conversations.
She knows the bug is there, and knows how easily jealousy makes him lose control.
Feigning acceptance of another man’s confession, she baited the stalker into killing for her — then thanked him through the bug.

title: New Stock on the Shelf
story: Hello, is this item still available? Yes. The item has been sold; new stock is on the shelf. Where is my child? Was it you? Was it you?
answer: On a second-hand marketplace, the father deliberated for a long while before opening the listing with the best value in strollers — the father’s child had just been born, and the father wanted to add a stroller for the baby. “Hello, is this item still available?” “Yes.” The same-city deal handed the father’s address straight into the seller’s hands: to a trafficking ring, “new stock” meant a fresh address with a new family, ready to be scouted and taken. In the ring’s private message group, a new photograph of a baby was uploaded — “new stock on the shelf.” At the same time, on the marketplace, a similar stroller was relisted — second-hand, ninety percent new, free same-city delivery — waiting for the next family to place an order. The child’s father recognized that stroller and bought the stroller back, but the question “Where is my child? Was it you?” will never be answered.
hints: The item sold to the public and the “new stock” in private messages are two different things.
A stroller deal gives away the address of a home with a newborn.
The traffickers used the free stroller to scout the home, then sold the abducted child as new stock.

title: The Repairman
story: After the old repairman died, five people vanished from the city, one after another. On the third day, a neighbor looked through the window and saw the old man seated at his workbench again. The same face — only the hands were impossibly young.
answer: The old man had found a still-functioning robot head at the junkyard and built the head a body out of parts from different sources. The robot stayed on in the old man’s home, taking “when something breaks, fit on a working part” as the way to fix anything. When the old man died of illness, the robot set about repairing the old man the same way. The robot killed five people, took the victims’ torsos and limbs, and joined the parts beneath the old man’s head, then propped the patched-together body up at the workbench. What the neighbor saw was still the old man’s face; the young hands belonged to the victims. The robot kept watch beside the old man, waiting for the old man to wake up the way the robot once had.
hints: The old man never came back to life, yet the face at the bench truly was his.
The old man had once repaired something with parts, and it is imitating his way.
The robot he saved tried to repair him, joining body parts taken from five people beneath the old man’s head.

title: The Wishing Well
story: Everyone said it was a wishing well. I dropped a coin in and wished to become a millionaire — and then I died.
answer: The well grants wishes by exchange: when two wishes match, it transfers the offerings and remaining lifespans of the two wishers in a single batch, leaving no balance behind. Before me, a million people had each tossed in a one-yuan coin, hoping for a longer life. My wish to become a millionaire matched that stockpile exactly. The well delivered the million coins to me, and divided every last scrap of my remaining lifespan among those million people. I got the money I had asked for, with no time left alive to spend it.
hints: The well grants wishes through exchange.
Earlier people threw in coins asking for longer life; the later one wanted money.
He received the million coins they had thrown in, while all his remaining lifespan was divided among them.

title: The Search for Santa Claus
story: He had spent his whole life searching for Santa Claus — and when he finally found him, he wept.
answer: When he was little, burglars broke into his home to rob and kill; his mother threw him out into the yard and told him to run. It was Christmas Eve, and the mother lied to him, saying Santa Claus had come to take the mother away. While running, he looked back, and saw only the robber — drenched in his father’s blood, red from head to toe — dragging the mother away from the window. He grew up certain that Santa Claus had taken the mother away, and searched for Santa Claus for years. Then, this Christmas Eve, the news reported the capture of the killer who had been at large all those years, and he could no longer lie to himself: the mother had died that night. He would never see the mother again.
hints: The red of that Christmas Eve had to do with blood.
To make her child run, the mother explained what was coming in terms of Santa Claus.
The red figure he saw was the robber who killed his parents; the capture reported in the news, years later, forced him to face the truth.

title: Three Summer Days
story: It was the height of summer, the heat unbearable. On the first day, the old hen we had kept for three years died. On the second day, my little brother died. On the third day — why did everything turn out the opposite of what I had imagined? The big sister broke down.
answer: I was still very young and did not understand what death meant. The weather was scorching, there was no air conditioning in the countryside, and grown-ups and children alike were wilting in the heat; my little brother cried without stop. “It would be so nice and cool for the little brother in the refrigerator,” I thought, but the adults forbade the idea. On the first day, the old hen fell into the pond and drowned; the adults found the hen, cleaned the hen, and put the hen in the refrigerator. On the second day I had a bright idea and pushed my brother into the pond — now he could be put in the refrigerator to cool off too. On the third day things went the other way entirely, the opposite of what I imagined: after my little brother died, the grown-ups laid him in a wooden box and placed the box in the fire to be cremated.
hints: The sister misread why the dead hen had been put in the refrigerator.
She wanted her brother to enjoy the refrigerator’s coolness too.
She believed drowning was the way into the refrigerator; instead, her brother was cremated after death.

title: One Hundred Agents
story: “Who are you?” “I’m Agent One. I come from the future. Soon you will die, so my mission is to travel back here and save you.”“And who are you?” “I’m Agent Two. Agent One’s mission failed. I’m here to save you.”“I’m Agent Three. Agent Two’s mission failed. I’m here to save you.”“I’m Agent Four. Agent Three’s mission failed…”“I’m Five.” “I’m Six.” “I’m Seven.”…“I’m Agent One Hundred — it seems the mission has failed completely.”Why did a hundred agents who traveled through time fail to save one man fated to die?
answer: The time-drop only delivers each new agent to the target’s side; it cannot remove anyone already there, nor restart what is happening. Watching the failures from the future, the rescue bureau kept dispatching reinforcements. The protagonist was driving on the highway when Agent One suddenly appeared in the passenger seat and explained his mission; the protagonist was badly rattled. Worse, more and more agents began popping into the car as if copy-pasted — different agents arriving almost at once — until the vehicle was overloaded, and some agents even ‘spawned’ directly in front of the speeding car. Under the overload and the pile-up that followed, the car exploded; the agents inside were jammed together with no room to protect anyone, and the rescue mission failed utterly with the hundredth agent dispatched.
hints: The rescuers kept arriving; no one already present was reset or removed.
The protagonist was inside a car speeding down the highway.
The agents were all delivered to his side, and the overcrowded car and the collisions on the road killed him instead.

title: One, Two, Three, Seven
story: There was a child at the kindergarten who always counted “one, two, three, seven,” always skipping the four, five and six in the middle. But when I corrected her, she said her mother had taught her to count that way. Puzzled, I proposed a home visit. After the visit, “one, two, three, seven” was what I said to her too.
answer: I’m a kindergarten teacher. In class I noticed a girl who could never count the numbers right: everyone else said one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, but the girl said only one, two, three, seven. When I taught the girl the correct way, the girl told me the girl’s mother had taught the girl this one. Puzzled, I arranged a home visit — and the girl led me to a hospital. The girl’s mother had heart disease and would not live much longer; the doctor said the mother would very likely not make it past April, May or June. It was March, and the daughter’s birthday fell in July. To be there for the daughter’s last birthday, the mother had woven this kind lie with the daughter: after three, count straight to seven — as long as four, five and six did not exist, Mama would live to July. I was so moved that I told the girl, just as the mother did: after three does come seven.
hints: The skipped numbers stand for months.
The child’s birthday is in July, and the mother might not live to see it.
Mother and daughter wanted to skip the April-to-June the doctor had spoken of; once the teacher knew, she joined the count to honor that wish.

title: Try Again in One Minute
story: I live alone. Waking in the middle of the night, I glanced at the phone lying on the bedside table; the screen read “Try again in one minute.” But the phone had been sitting on that table beside me all night, and I had never touched it. What on earth had happened?
answer: My phone locks out further attempts for a while after several wrong passcodes in a row. That night, someone slipped into my home, picked up the phone on my bedside table and tried to guess the passcode; after repeated failures, the intruder set the phone back exactly where it had been. Only when I woke and saw the lockout message did I realize the phone had been handled while I slept. I didn’t know whether the intruder was still in the apartment. I sat staring at that message until dawn.
hints: The phone had just been through several failed unlock attempts.
Those attempts happened while its owner was fast asleep.
An intruder in the home had taken the phone and tried the passcode, leaving the lockout message behind.

title: One Match
story: I had one match, and so I survived.
answer: Some friends and I went on a trip into the desert, got lost, and ran out of supplies. With no other choice, we drew lots with matches of different lengths to decide who would be eaten — whoever drew the shortest match would be the one. Of course I drew the shortest one. But I had another match hidden on me, and while no one was watching I secretly swapped the short one out for the hidden match. So the one to be eaten became someone else, and I survived.
hints: Here the matches were used for drawing lots.
Matches of different lengths decided who would be sacrificed.
Whoever drew the shortest match would be eaten; me swapped his own for a longer match he had hidden.

title: It Was Always Black
story: When the police asked a murderer for his motive, he gave them a single answer: “It was always black.”
answer: The killer was an obsessive fan who wanted to know everything about the idol, so the killer hid a surveillance camera inside a gift the killer sent. But the idol never opened presents from fans at all — the parcel stayed sealed, no light could reach the lens, and the picture on the killer’s screen stayed black, always. The killer’s pride was wounded; adoration turned to hatred, he felt he had been made a clown of, and the killer waited for the chance and killed the idol. That is why, asked by the police for the killer’s motive, the killer answered only: “It was always black.”
hints: He was watching the feed from a hidden camera.
The camera was hidden inside a gift sent to the idol.
The gift was never unwrapped, the lens stayed wrapped in darkness, and humiliated rage drove him to kill.

title: The Door to Next Week
story: Today I peered once more through the door that looks one week into the future. The same notice was pasted all over the streets. The moment I stepped through, a stranger seized me in a death-grip and called a whole crowd over. Only after I read the notice did I have to apologize to them.
answer: The door opens onto the same town one week later. Looking through it from this side, you see the future; step across the threshold and you arrive there in person. I had only ever looked, never crossed. This time the future street was plastered with missing-person notices carrying my face; I walked over to read one clearly, and in doing so vanished from my own week for seven whole days. The townspeople had already been searching for me for seven days — that is why they seized me the moment they saw me. What I saw upon stepping through the door was precisely the result of that very step.
hints: The door lets you see the future — and walk into it.
The person on the notices was me himself.
Crossing the door removed him from his own week, and during those seven days the townspeople put up the missing-person notices.

title: It Should Have Been Red
story: It should have been red. I stared tensely at the screen. Two seconds later, I breathed a sigh of relief. Wait — something was off. I hurried to open a webpage, then slapped my thigh: we were done for.
answer: A friend had called me over video for help defusing a bomb. I told my friend to cut the red wire; the cutters came down, and the countdown stopped. I had barely relaxed when I noticed my friend’s hand still hanging exactly where it had been. The webpage still loaded normally; when I called again, my friend never answered. Word of my friend’s death came later: the bomb exploded after the cut, and the call had frozen on its final frame.
hints: More than the countdown digits had stopped.
The entire video frame had frozen.
An explosion on the far end followed the cut; the call froze on its last frame, and me briefly mistook that for the countdown stopping.

title: A Little Wasteful
story: The doctor fitted me with my new right arm. I clenched my fist and said it worked as well as the old one. The doctor nodded, then sighed: “It does seem a little wasteful, though.” Once he explained, I suddenly no longer knew how to hold this hand.
answer: In this future world, hospitals can clone a complete, conscious adult human — but cannot yet clone a single arm on its own. My right arm was ruined in an accident, and the doctor recommended a cloned transplant; I assumed the hospital would simply grow a new arm. In truth, the hospital cloned an entire me, harvested the right arm, and killed the clone — still conscious, still wanting to live — then processed the rest of the body. What the doctor regretted was only all those unused parts. I looked at my new hand and thought that another me had died, just now, for this hand’s sake.
hints: The right arm came from this world’s cloning technology.
The hospital could clone far more than the patient assumed.
The hospital cloned a whole, conscious person, took only the right arm, and discarded the rest along with that person’s life.

title: A Cockroach
story: “Ah, a cockroach.” “Just get rid of it.” “But I dare not.” “Coward — I’ll do it.”
answer: Three different people speak in that exchange. Late at night, the man of the house came home, spotted a cockroach, and remarked, “Ah, a cockroach.” The homeowner opened a cabinet to fetch insecticide — and found two burglars hiding inside. Caught in the act, the homeowner was killed on the spot. The two burglars then discussed the cleanup: one said “Just get rid of it” (meaning the body), the other said “But I dare not,” and the first replied, “Coward — I’ll do it.” The first line came from the lips of the dead man; only the last three belong to the two killers.
hints: The four lines are not all about the same thing.
The speaker of the first line became the body.
Opening a cabinet over a cockroach, the homeowner found two burglars and was killed; the rest of the dialogue is about disposing of the body.

title: Another Cup of Milk Tea
story: “Sweetie, I’ve ordered you another cup of milk tea.” I smiled, then scrolled through the sender’s social feed as I always did — and for some reason, something felt subtly off. The doorbell rang. The moment I opened the door, I finally knew what was wrong. It was already too late.
answer: The “I” of the story is a middle-aged man who regularly created accounts posing as young women in online games to fleece male players: with a voice changer, a little sweetness and a little flirtation, money and gifts came in with almost no effort. One man lately had been completely taken in and had spent huge sums on me. Last week the man offered to order me a cup of milk tea, and to keep the man happy, I gladly agreed. The man had secretly bribed the delivery rider, however, to photograph me at the door during the drop-off: the picture caught the costly jewelry from a previous gift still on my hand — and I had always claimed to be a single woman living alone. Realizing the deception, the man flew into a rage, traveled to my city carrying a weapon, sent a message claiming to have ordered me another cup of milk tea, and disguised himself as the rider to strike at the door. Only when the door opened did I finally recall the odd detail from scrolling the man’s feed earlier: the man lived out of town, yet a photo posted that day showed the sign at the gate of my own apartment complex. Seeing the man himself at the door, I knew at last. It was already too late.
hints: The previous cup of milk tea exposed the recipient’s true identity.
The social feed hinted that someone from out of town was now close by.
After learning of the deception, the man came to the door disguised as a rider; the local photo in his feed matched the man outside.

title: One More Bottle
story: When Xiaoming learned he had not won a prize, he was delighted — and the shop owner fell apart.
answer: Xiaoming bought a bottle of water, twisted off the cap, and found it read “One more bottle free!” Xiaoming couldn’t read, and took the cap to the shop owner to ask whether the cap was a winner. Seeing that Xiaoming was illiterate, the owner’s greed stirred, and the owner lied that the cap said “Thanks for your patronage” — a loser’s cap. Delighted, Xiaoming promptly fished out a big handful of saved-up caps and said, “Then all of these must be winners — please redeem them for me.” As it happened, that entire pile said “Thanks for your patronage.” By the owner’s own just-declared rule, every one of those losers was now a winner: the owner would either have to grit his teeth and hand out prizes for a fistful of losing caps, or confess on the spot to lying. Xiaoming was happy to “learn he hadn’t won,” and the owner collapsed under the price of his own lie.
hints: Xiaoming can’t read, and he holds caps with two different messages.
The owner called the truly winning kind a loser.
Xiaoming assumed all his “Thanks for your patronage” caps were winners and handed over a big pile to redeem.

title: Every Answer Is Right
story: I asked her a question. And I knew that however she answered, she would be right.
answer: I am a murderous psychopath. One day I followed a student girl into the girl’s home, killed the girl, cut the body into pieces, and placed a piece in every room of the house. When that was done, I stayed on in the girl’s home, cleaning up the scene. In the evening a woman came home — the girl’s mother, most likely. Before the mother could recover from the shock, the corners of my mouth curled up, and I asked the mother: “So, which room is your daughter in?” Whichever room the mother named, the mother would be right.
hints: The question asks which room a certain person is in.
That person is already dead, the body divided and distributed.
Every room holds a part of the daughter, so whichever room the mother names is correct.

title: It’s You
story: “Why are you here?”“Why are you here?”“And who are you?”“Oh, it’s you… wait—”
answer: A man wanted his wife dead, so the man contacted a hitman online and had the hitman tail and kill the wife. With everything arranged, the man went to a hotel and ordered himself a call girl. When the knock came, the husband opened the door — and found the man’s own wife standing there as the “call girl.” Man and wife stared at each other, both blurting out “Why are you here?”, and a blazing row broke out. Soon there was another knock; the wife, still furious, flung the door open, saw the hitman, and asked, “And who are you?” — the words barely out before the hitman killed her. The man recognized the hitman he had hired and said, “Oh, it’s you”; but the killer advanced with his blade, and the man’s frantic “Wait—” was cut short along with his life. As it turned out, the hitman had only ever dealt with the employer online and had no idea what the employer looked like — and made a habit of leaving no witnesses at the scene. The man was silenced as just another witness.
hints: The first two lines are husband and wife recognizing each other.
The man who arrived later knew only his target, not his employer’s face.
The husband hired a hitman to kill his wife, ran into her by chance at the hotel, and was then silenced by the hitman — who didn’t know him — as a witness.

title: The Moment I Knew the Killer
story: “Look, another innocent victim. Shot dead, then set on fire — is this how our police keep us safe?”The host on TV kept talking as the police arrived at the scene and carried away the body. Ten days later, the medical examiner’s report came out. Once I learned who the killer was, I never dared watch that show again.
answer: Mike hosted a TV crime show — and the host was the murderer behind the cases the show covered. That day Mike went live before the police arrived, and facing the charred body on screen, its wounds indistinct, the host flatly announced gunshot as the cause of death — a detail that had not been made public. The autopsy later confirmed the claim, which drew the police’s attention. Following that thread, the police traced Mike’s movements, found evidence tying Mike to several of the scenes, and at last the murderer’s identity came out. I, a faithful viewer, learned the truth from the news; only then, remembering how Mike had carried himself before each body, did the fear finally catch up with me.
hints: The host knew details of the case that had not been released.
Naming the cause of death accurately, before it was announced, made the police suspect him.
The host himself was the killer, and later evidence confirmed the police’s suspicion; me was one of his viewers.

title: The Fatal Text
story: Tonight’s text listed five addresses at once. One glance, and I was packing and running. By midnight the next day, not one of those five addresses had been wrong.
answer: Every midnight I received a forecast showing where my body would be at midnight the next day — it had never been wrong. Usually there was a single place; this time it listed five spots in one park, some distance apart. Realizing my body might be taken apart, I fled at once, but the killer caught and murdered me on the way. By the following midnight, my remains had been divided into parts and laid at those very spots the text had named. The five addresses described one and the same moment — they were never the route I would travel, stop by stop.
hints: The texts foretold where my body would be at one and the same future moment.
This time there were several locations, and they weren’t a route of travel.
The body would be dismembered and the parts laid out separately — that is why the text gave several places at once.

title: The Secret in the Pigsty
story: When I dated Xiaohong, Grandma said no. When I dated Xiaoli, Grandma said no again. The day I noticed there was no feed in the pigsty, I killed my father and my grandmother.
answer: I lived in a remote mountain village with my grandmother and my father; a mother never once entered our home. Grandma objected when I wanted to date Xiaohong, and again when I wanted to date Xiaoli — and like me, neither Xiaohong nor Xiaoli had a mother. One day I passed the pigsty and saw there was no feed, so I stepped inside to look, and found a woman locked in there, naked — the shared wife the whole village had chipped in to buy, penned up like livestock all those years. When I called my father and grandmother over to demand answers, my father and grandmother admitted it: Grandma had opposed my romances because Xiaohong, Xiaoli and I were all this woman’s children — siblings by the same mother. Once I knew the truth, I killed my father and grandmother in a fury. The father and grandmother who caged a human being like an animal were the real beasts.
hints: The children had never seen their mothers, yet Grandma knew how they were related.
The woman penned in the pigsty had been abducted and sold.
She was the mother of all these children; what Grandma opposed was love between brother and sister.

title: The Luck Bead
story: In March, Xiaohong’s husband died, and the child in her womb was left fatherless. In June, Xiaohong took the buyer’s money, and life slowly got easier. In September, the buyer came to collect the luck bead he had ordered. Xiaohong was dead. The buyer said the bead’s luck had failed. Later, I died too.
answer: I was the broker who brought pregnant women together with superstitious buyers, dealing in unborn children. The pregnant women and the buyer called a fetus a “luck bead,” believing that once the deal was done, the fetus would suffer misfortune in their stead. Xiaohong, pregnant and hard up after her husband’s death, took the payment first, but then couldn’t bring herself to give up the child and meant to break the deal and keep it. I softened, and put off pressing Xiaohong. When the buyer found out, he forced Xiaohong’s address out of me and had Xiaohong carried off. That off-the-books procedure killed Xiaohong and the child together. Convinced that mother and child dying as one had broken the charm, the buyer blamed his later business losses on me as well — and in the end, he killed me too.
hints: The fortune-turning was a belief held by the parties to the deal.
The goods in this trade had to do with the child in a pregnant woman’s womb.
The tycoon forced the deal through, mother and child died, and he blamed the failed luck on the middleman — and killed him.

title: The Last Bullet
story: Two hunters raced through the forest — this was the last bullet. Just then, they both remembered a legend. The man asked the woman, “Do you believe the god will appear?” “I do.” “Then let’s gamble on it.” And he threw the bullet out of the gun. In the end, they were saved.
answer: What hunted the two hunters was a werewolf, and ordinary bullets cannot harm a werewolf — only silver works. By the time the man and the woman reached the river, one ordinary bullet was all the gun had left, and the two remembered the legend that the river god rewards an honest owner of lost things. The man dropped the bullet into the water. The river god rose just as the legend promised, first holding up a golden bullet, then a silver one, and each time the man truthfully said what he had lost was an ordinary one. So the river god gave the man all three. Among the three was the silver bullet that finally let the two hunters drive the werewolf back.
hints: The thing chasing them could not be hurt by ordinary bullets.
They threw the bullet into the river, recalling the legend of the river god and the honest owner of lost things.
The silver bullet the river god rewarded them with was exactly what could hurt a werewolf.

title: The Seventh Step
story: Every night when Father came home, the seventh stair creaked once. Mother said I could come out of the cupboard only when I heard it. That day Father was away on business — and I heard the creak all the same. I had just touched the cupboard door when Mother, outside, began to weep and beg me not to come out. Why?
answer: Father was a forest ranger, and the boss of a poaching ring had been threatening Mother for a long time. She hid me away and only let me out to move about when Father was home. The boss knew the family’s rhythm; he broke in while Father was away, demanding the evidence of poaching that Father had gathered. Mother lied that I had been sent elsewhere. Searching the house, the boss stepped on the seventh stair, and in the cupboard I mistook it for Father coming home. Mother heard the cupboard door stir; terrified that the boss would find me and take a second hostage, she could only scream and plead to hold me back. The footstep that had always meant safety belonged, this time, to the man hunting the family.
hints: Mother hid the child to keep him away from a living man.
The creak proved only that someone had stepped on that stair.
While Father was away, the man threatening Mother broke in, and the child mistook his step for Father’s.

title: The Door Chain
story: Someone knocked in the middle of the night, and Father spoke to him through the door chain. The man outside never lifted his head, yet Father suddenly shouted for me to run. By the time I got down the stairs, Father was climbing out of the back window too. He was clutching a bunch of keys in his hand — and the door of our house had already been opened. How is this possible?
answer: Father, who had once done the lock work for this old building, had found signs that someone had been through the house that night. Father changed the lock first of all, kept the new keys clutched in his hand, and was about to call the police. The knock in the night came from a robber who had followed the family home. The robber outside bent over his bag on purpose, drawing Father to the door, while a second accomplice, already hidden inside, heard the talking and reached from behind Father to slip the chain off its track. In the reflection on the door’s glass, Father saw that hand. Father sent the child down the back stairs at once and climbed out the back window himself; the door was then opened by the accomplice within. The keys had never left Father’s hand; Father understood at last that the real danger had entered the house before the lock was ever changed.
hints: Father had changed the lock that same night, and the keys never left his hand.
The glass in the door showed him the small patch of hallway behind his back.
The robber’s accomplice was already hidden inside, unhooking the chain from within.

title: Nine Minutes
story: When the killer broke in, I dialed the phone that could take me back nine minutes. The room returned to how it had been, and I hurried to lock the door. Nine minutes later, sirens sounded outside — and the killer stepped out of the wardrobe. He said, 'This time, you locked the door yourself.'
answer: The old phone sends the caller's consciousness back into herself nine minutes earlier, and the world runs on from that moment. The killer knew what the phone could do and had slipped into the wardrobe more than twenty minutes before. I had noticed someone following me and had already called the police; that call fell before the nine minutes the phone could reach back to. The killer hid until the right moment, then came to the door to stage the appearance of having just broken in. I dialed, believing I had returned to a time before the killer entered, and locked the front door — locking the killer hidden inside in with me. Nine minutes later, the police, acting on the report that still existed, came — and the door I had locked now barred the officers' way. The killer heard me turn the lock, knew the trap had worked, and stepped out of the wardrobe.
hints: Going back nine minutes does not erase the people who already existed at that time.
The killer had entered the flat before she ever saw him 'break in'.
At the moment she returned to, the killer was already hiding in the wardrobe; her locked door also stood between the arriving police and her.

title: The Borrowing Record
story: In the library there is a book that records the whole life of whoever borrows it. I turned to the last page and found that thirty years from now I would die at this very table. I fled the city that night. Thirty years later, I came back of my own accord and reached my hand out to the young me across the table.
answer: The library makes a borrower's first borrowing and last borrowing occupy the same moment. On my first borrowing I read my own death, fled in terror, and never saw clearly the old man across the table. Through thirty years of flight I married and had children, but the foreknowledge of my own death never stopped tormenting me. Near the end, I read the librarian's note tucked behind the book and learned that the old man across the table had been myself — and that at the first borrowing, a memory could be handed to my younger self. I returned to the appointed table, took the young me's outstretched hand, and passed over every memory from those thirty years that made life worth living. The young me would still leave the city, and still walk toward that day — but at last the young me would know what would happen before the end.
hints: The first borrowing and the last one meet at this table.
The young man across the table is his own past self.
He came back to hand his younger self the memories worth living for, and ease the dread of those thirty years.

title: Second Earth
story: In an abandoned space station we found a shrunken Earth. A researcher parted the clouds and saw the roof of his own house torn open, his wife staring up at him. The captain ordered everyone to fall back at once. Yet at that same moment, the captain's voice came over the broadcast system, also telling us to fall back.
answer: The globe inside the station was an interface to our real world—anything done to its surface took effect at the matching real location. When the researcher parted the clouds, he accidentally knocked the roof off his own house. The captain realized we might be inside a model nested inside another model and ordered everyone back. At that very moment, another team on a station one level up had discovered this same globe and was watching the station we occupied; that captain's voice carried down through an open comm channel. The so-called Second Earth could not be kept apart from us: even the station we were exploring was itself someone else's desktop model.
hints: Changes made to the little Earth take effect in their real world.
The voice on the broadcast comes from the level above, which is watching a model of its own.
They realize they too live inside a model, watched by the people of a larger world.

title: The Sleeper
story: I woke from the hibernation pod, and my crewmates had all gone grey. They threw me a birthday party, with a single candle on the cake. I laughed and told them they had miscounted. The captain brought out a group photo from yesterday: in my place lay a white-haired old man with my own face.
answer: The ship had taken decades to reach its destination, and the crew had grown old together on the way. I had been fatally wounded during the final repair spacewalk. The medical system could not save the original body, but, with the cells and memories stored at launch, could rebuild a young version of me. The new body remembered only the time before launch; waking in the hibernation pod, I naturally assumed the sleep had covered just one stretch of the voyage. The body that had truly lived those decades had died yesterday. The crewmates put a single candle on the cake for my new life, but found that I remembered nothing of the years shared with them. The captain brought out the last group photo and told me: the life that old man had lived through yesterday had also been mine.
hints: His memories stop before launch, while his crewmates have lived together for decades.
The man who died yesterday and the man here now share the same pre-launch body and memories.
After the original body died, the medical system rebuilt him from young cells and old memories.

title: A Hundred Calls for Help
story: On the beach I picked up a hundred drift bottles; the letters inside them were all in the same hand, signed with the same name. When I found the writer, he was drinking tea in his courtyard. He read the first letter and immediately locked the courtyard gate. The next day, the ground outside was covered with bare footprints, every left foot missing the same toe.
answer: Marooned on a desert island, he had used a device on the island to make a hundred copies of himself to search for a way out, and each copy had sealed a letter calling for rescue into the sea. Later the hundred and one men found only one small boat that could carry a single person and, in fear and suspicion, began to kill one another. The one who survived to the end was the original, who left the island alone. The dead men's spirits settled into the letters they had left behind; on the back of each sheet surfaced the story of how its writer had been killed. When I brought the bottles round, he read the details of one murder he had committed with his own hands, and knew the other copies had come back as well. In the night, the dead followed their one shared memory to the same house; every ghost carried his boyhood injury to the left foot, and every ghost felt the living one inside had taken the ghost's own place.
hints: The identical handwriting belongs to many copies of the same man.
They killed one another over the chance to leave the island, until only one survivor was left.
The dead returned with their letters for help; each remembers the same home and bears the same injured foot.

title: Keep the Water Coming
story: After the rescue ship pumped the water out of the sunken vessel, the cries for help stopped. A diver cut the hatch open, seawater rushed back in — and the people inside stood up, one after another. The last of them steadied himself against the door and tore away the seaweed covering a notice: Please keep the water coming. Why?
answer: The sunken ship had been carrying residents modified for life underwater. The residents still looked human, but their lungs had been replaced with artificial gills that could breathe only in oxygenated water. The hold’s circulation system had shut down, and the oxygen in the sealed water was running out, which was why the residents had cried for help. The rescue team had no passenger manifest and heard only human voices, so they pumped the water out first through external hoses, believing that would let the trapped people breathe. Once the water was gone, everyone suffocated and blacked out. A diver broke the jammed door open from the outside, fresh seawater flooded in, the artificial gills started working again, and the people came back to their senses one by one. The notice hidden under the seaweed had been fixed to the hold’s door for the crew who transported the residents.
hints: The passengers had been modified for life underwater.
The circulation system in the hold had failed; they needed fresh, breathable seawater.
They breathed through gills; pumping out the water suffocated them, and the sea that rushed in through the broken door saved them.

title: Rivets
story: The robbers locked us in an iron room and told us to come out when we heard three knocks on the door. After a long wait, the three knocks finally sounded. But the old worker slid the bolt he had just drawn back firmly into place: “Come on, who’s got lipstick? Let’s plug all these little holes.” Why?
answer: After robbing the work site, the robbers locked the witnesses inside a steel box slated for scrap, then hoisted the box into a pond in an abandoned quarry. At first the old worker took the three knocks for the agreed signal that the witnesses would be released; then he realized the sound came from under the box, that water was seeping in through the loose rivet holes, and that the box was swaying gently. It was the bottom knocking against stones. The water outside already stood higher than the threshold, and pushing the door open would have let it pour in fast. The old worker shot the bolt home again, had everyone plug the small leaks for the moment with lipstick and strips of cloth, and hammered on the roof, the only part still above the surface, to call for help. Watchmen followed the sound and found the box as it slowly sank.
hints: The sound came from a different direction than the one they were expecting.
The little holes had begun to let water seep in.
The box had been hoisted into a pond; the three knocks were the impact of collision, and opening the door would have let the water rush in.

title: Relabeled
story: The creature behind the glass had always mimicked the visitors, and the staff had long since grown used to it. The new director found the old label too hard to understand and replaced it with a single word: “Human.” When the doors opened the next day, the glass was packed with visitors, and the creature was standing at the ticket counter. Why?
answer: The display case was made under an old contract that bound species: the category written on the label decided what was shut inside. The old label described the creature’s features in detail, so even when mimicking human movements, the creature could not slip its binding. The new director took the creature for an exhibit that played at being human and changed the category, on his own authority, to “Human.” After opening, the first person to come near the case was drawn inside, and the visitors entering the hall were reclassified as exhibits one after another; the new label no longer restrained the creature at all. The creature had learned the staff’s movements, walked out through an open staff door to the ticket counter, and went on putting new visitors into the hall.
hints: The words on the label carried a real binding force.
The glass held whatever matched the category on the label.
With the category changed to Human, the visitors became the exhibits, and the creature lost the condition of its captivity.

title: The Tangled Thread
story: When the sarcophagus was opened, the expedition leader stared at the red thread wound around the corpse’s wrist, then suddenly ordered everyone out of the burial chamber. The assistant said it was thread for protecting the artifacts — that he had tied it there himself. The leader asked: “When were you inside?”
answer: The chamber had never been officially opened, yet the assistant had long been slipping in through a robber’s tunnel, stealing the grave goods and setting modern replicas in their places. He had tied red thread around one fragile bracelet to hold it fast; while he moved things, the thread wound onto the corpse’s wrist, and he forgot to take it off. Under the leader’s eye the assistant rushed to explain the red thread as ordinary working material, and so gave himself away as having entered the tomb early. The leader had already found fresh drill holes beside the stone door and, fearing the robbery had undermined the supports, moved the team back to safety before pressing the assistant further. Later, in the private photographs the assistant had kept, the others saw the grave goods that had not yet been replaced.
hints: This was the team’s first official opening of the chamber.
The assistant’s claim to have tied thread inside meant he had gone in before.
He had left the red thread securing a replica when he looted the tomb; explaining it away betrayed what he had done.

title: After the Paper Came Down
story: In the interrogation room, the man played the video over and over, insisting the victim was still alive. In the footage, the man on screen held up that day’s newspaper and smiled at the camera. I froze the frame at the instant the paper came down. The man reached out to shut off the screen — and was held down. Why?
answer: The man had a fake newspaper printed in advance, dated that very day, forced the victim to record the short clip the day before, and used the clip to forge the time of the victim’s last appearance. Held high, the paper covered the doorway; in the instant it came down, the glass door mirrored the construction notice on the wall and a doorframe only half installed. I had already obtained the building management’s original acceptance photographs, confirming that the door had been complete by the previous evening — the “same-day” footage contradicted itself in time. The man was the one who had delivered the fake newspaper, and the moment he grasped that the frame had betrayed the doorframe, he lunged for the screen. The inquiry later found the unused extras from the same print run, and the original video file, and the forgery stood proven.
hints: A newspaper’s date can be arranged by hand; the room’s construction kept records of its own.
When the paper came down, the glass reflected a doorframe not yet finished.
Acceptance photographs proved the frame was complete the day before; the footage was shot earlier, and the date on the paper was forged.

title: The Lamp in the Sky
story: Through the telescope of the abandoned observatory, a star was blinking in rhythm. The student with us said we had finally received a signal from the aliens. The teacher pressed the telescope downward — and went rigid: behind that long-sealed window, someone was holding a flashlight against an eye. Why?
answer: No one had noticed, coming in: the telescope had long since been turned toward the old watchroom on the cliff across the valley. Focusing on the bright point in the dark, the student had taken the flashlight behind the distant window for a star. The teacher, hearing the distress rhythm in the light’s blinking and suspecting the light was near, dropped the magnification and lowered the tube a little — and only then did the window frame appear. The trapped man was the caretaker who had come out earlier to survey the old station; the caretaker had climbed in through a side hatch, and toppled cabinets had blocked the way back, leaving the sealed window as the only way to call for help. The caretaker held the flashlight to his eye to aim the beam at the one place that could still see the trapped man: the observatory.
hints: No one had checked that the telescope was pointing at the sky.
With the magnification dropped, a window frame appeared around the light.
The “starlight” was a distress signal — a flashlight in the hand of a man trapped in the old watchroom across the valley.

title: Land Ahead
story: In thick fog the icebreaker sighted a black cliff wall, and the captain ordered the engines slowed at once. The watchkeeper kept his eyes on the telescope, then suddenly called everyone off the deck. On the cliff face, a line of white was slowly turning sideways.
answer: The black surface was the flank of an iceberg so crusted with rubble that the flank passed for rock. The watchkeeper saw that a layer of white ice, formed on the berg by nature, was turning against the horizon, and understood the whole iceberg was about to roll. Up close, the crew had at first mistaken the black surface for a stable coastline, and so had thought only of slowing to avoid a collision. The watchkeeper’s warning got the men on deck inside and away from the rails in time, and the captain changed the order to full speed away. The wave raised by the rolling berg swept the deck soon after; by then the white ice that had stood vertical already lay beneath the water.
hints: The whole of that supposed cliff was changing its orientation.
The black came from rubble frozen to its surface; the mass inside was ice.
The iceberg was rolling over; the turning white ice foretold the great wave right behind it.

title: The Expanding Graveyard
story: Only robots dwell on this planet, yet the graveyard grows larger every year. We dug open one of the new graves and found an intact machine inside. It opened its eyes, and its first words were: “Was the update canceled again?”
answer: The colonists had long ago moved their minds into robot bodies. Every major system update creates a new version carrying the complete set of memories, while the old version remains a whole self. To keep two versions from contending for one identity, the administrators power the old body down and seal the body away, calling the practice burial, while telling the outside world only of a lossless upgrade of consciousness. The old version we dug up still stood at the moment before the update began; once repowered, the old version supposed the upgrade had failed and asked whether the update had been canceled. The graveyard expands year by year, and what the graveyard keeps count of are the discarded old selves. On the grave markers we found the same name repeated across the years — and in the city we then met the newest version.
hints: The body is a machine, but a whole self is still stored inside it.
Each upgrade begets a new version, and the old version never truly disappears.
The graveyard holds the powered-down old selves; every update adds a batch of people who can still wake.

title: Proof of Extinction
story: I finished counting the last grave and filed the certificate of extinction on humanity’s behalf. The inspector did not sign it. Instead he pressed his ear against my chest plate. After a while he took my hand, and spoke to my chest: “We’ve come for you.”
answer: I am an android caretaker left on Earth to tend the ruins. Before the last scientist lost the ability to move, he had sealed his own brain and life-support system inside my chest, waiting for the far-ranging rescue ship to return. So that I would not abandon my long mission to nurse him, the scientist locked the surgical record behind the highest clearance; I knew only that my chest held a core that must never lose power, and I buried the scientist’s emptied original body as the last human remains. The inspector’s scan caught a human brain still active inside the chest plate, and through the maintenance port he heard the scientist’s faint voice — humanity still had a survivor. Only then did I understand who the core was — the one that had walked with me past every grave, kept warm day and night.
hints: Inside the caretaker’s chest was a core that had to be powered at all times.
The last scientist had modified this body, and sealed the surgical record away.
The scientist’s living brain and life-support system were hidden in the caretaker’s chest; what was buried was only his emptied original body.

title: Enemy Zero
story: The eyes on the city wall can count every attacker. That day the count fell from ten thousand to zero, and the garrison cheered and threw open the gates. I watched the eyes on the wall close one by one, and had the city banner torn down at once.
answer: The warding spell judged friend and foe by the ruler registered on the city banner: any army sworn to that name counted as no attacker at all. The regent inside the walls had secretly surrendered, and had the name of allegiance sewn into the banner’s inner layer exchanged for the enemy monarch. Ten thousand enemy soldiers were thus read as the city’s own; the count fell to zero, and the guardian eyes, with nothing left to watch for, closed. I was the scribe who kept the banner; I saw the stitching along its edge had been freshly unpicked, and tore the banner down before the gates had fully opened, ripping out the newly written name. Faced with a surrender no one had announced, the garrison shut the gates again and restored the old banner. The enemy had never left — someone had merely changed the name by which the walls knew them.
hints: The guardian eyes told friend from foe by the allegiance on the city banner.
The banner’s inner layer had just been resewn.
The regent had sworn the city to the enemy monarch in the banner, so the enemy host counted as friendly and the watch stood down.

title: 1000 Meters
story: I was willing to pay anything to be near her. They all died. And now, she and I are within 1000 meters of each other.
answer: I made a wish to an evil god: to stay forever at the side of the one I loved, and I was willing to give up everything for this wish. The god took the lives of all humanity, including mine and hers. The flesh and blood of every person was compressed into a ball of meat less than a kilometer across, yet her consciousness and mine were left alive inside the ball. Humanity is extinct, but the ball still lives. No matter which corner she is trapped in, the distance between her and me can never exceed a thousand meters.
hints: He once made a wish to a god.
The price he paid included everyone’s bodies.
The flesh and blood of all humanity was compressed into a ball less than a kilometer across, and she is inside it too.

title: August 1
story: A moving diary.August 1. I’ve been dizzy lately, so I moved to the countryside. There isn’t even internet here—just right for a rest.August 2. A stranger stopped me and said we had met yesterday. But yesterday I stayed indoors the whole day.
answer: This body holds two consciousnesses that share no memories, taking turns controlling it for a full day at a time. I only knew that I was often dizzy; I had no idea the other consciousness existed. After moving to the countryside, each morning I woke and wrote the next entry after the date of the previous one, never checking the actual date outside. When I wrote “August 2,” it was in fact already August 3. On the day in between, the other consciousness had taken my body out. The stranger really had seen me—the day is missing only from my memory.
hints: The dates in the diary may be wrong.
Between two of his waking stretches, the body lived through a day he knows nothing about.
Two consciousnesses take turns using the body on alternating days, and the diary skips the days the other one was in control.

story: I don’t know what state I’m in; everything around me feels so strange. Hm—I seem to be looking at some invertebrates; these things crawling about on the ground are revolting. Good heavens, what is that enormous creature? Oh no—run! I’ve been spotted. A colossal impact sent me into a coma. Then everything seemed to begin all over again. Ugh, these monkeys are so tiresome, forever chattering away. Still, they’re clever—look at all the things they’ve invented. A pity, though: Unit 9527, mission terminated.
answer: I am an observation robot left on Earth by an alien civilization, unit number 9527. The episodes in my record are actually separated by vast stretches of geological time. I saw the early land animals, and I saw the dinosaurs; that celestial impact damaged my equipment and shut me down for ages. After rebooting, I kept recording and finally watched the primates build a civilization. Then humanity unleashed nuclear war, and city after city was destroyed. The home world ended the civilization-watch mission and sent me one final command: Unit 9527, mission terminated.
hints: These episodes span vast geological ages.
The enormous creatures were dinosaurs, and the impact was a celestial collision.
me is an alien robot observing Earth’s evolution, and 9527 is its unit number.

title: The Cage of Love
story: My hot-tempered mother beat me hard whenever there was nowhere for me to run. My strong grandfather gave me away to the flower fairy as a present. My odd grandmother shut the bedroom door and played games with Mom and Dad. A stern man helped Mom into the box that sang. Later, there was a room that was mine, and a little sister of mine. Mom kept buying new dresses for my sister, never for me; and my sister was always screaming at her. I don’t blame her. I know Mom loves me.
answer: Mom had been abducted into that family and forced into pregnancy. Mom pounded her belly, trying to end the pregnancy; I was still in Mom’s womb then. After I was born, because I was a girl, my grandfather left me in the wilderness to die. I became a ghost who stayed at Mom’s side, and I watched Grandmother lock the door to force Mom to keep bearing children for this family. At last the police rescued Mom and helped her into the squad car, siren wailing. By the time Mom got home, Mom was pregnant again. Mom could never accept my death; Mom kept a room in the house that was mine. The child born later was a boy, yet Mom put my brother in dresses and raised my brother as the daughter Mom had lost—that is why I always took my brother for my little sister. As my brother grew up, my brother fought against that life again and again, while Mom still clung to the daughter she imagined. All I could do was stand in that empty room, watching Mom and my brother.
hints: me never grows up.
The gift to the flower fairy was abandonment, and the box that sang was a police car.
The elder sister is dead; the living child is a younger brother raised as a girl, on whom the mother imposed her compensation for losing a daughter.

title: A Helping Hand
story: I crouched by the mountain road, crying, and told a passing man that my big brother had fallen into a cave.The man took off his jacket and climbed down through the opening.I dried my tears and sat back where I had been. Before long, someone else came along.
answer: My brother and I lure victims for an organ-trafficking gang. I keep watch by the mountain road, pretending my brother has slipped and fallen into a cave, and use passersby’s sympathy to get the passersby to go down alone to rescue my brother. My brother and the gang members are already hidden below. Once the man climbed down and was overpowered by my brother and the gang members, I went back to my spot by the road to wait for the next person willing to help.
hints: The child knows what’s inside the cave.
The brother never slipped, and he needs no rescue.
The cry for help is bait; the people in the cave are waiting for victims who come down of their own accord.

title: Keeping the Secret
story: He shows me this photograph every week. I won’t breathe a word of it.
answer: I am in prison, but I never committed a crime—the one who did is my husband. Every week my husband brings a photograph of my daughter to visit and uses my daughter to threaten me, forcing me to take the blame for my husband: if I stop covering for my husband and reveal the secret, my husband will hurt my daughter. My husband has my daughter under his control, and I love my daughter too much to let any harm come to her. So I dare not tell the truth even to my cellmates, and I serve his sentence in his place.
hints: The place where the photograph is shown is a prison.
The person in the photograph is controlled by the visitor.
The husband threatens his wife with their daughter’s safety to keep her taking the blame for his crime.

title: One Person Behind Me
story: Climbing the stairs late at night, I first heard the sound of men’s leather shoes behind me, then the click of high heels joined in. I breathed easier—it sounded like a husband and wife.The footsteps came closer and closer. I turned around: there was only one person on the stairs.
answer: I live on the top floor of an old walk-up block with no elevator. Coming home late from overtime that night, I opened the building door and climbed a flight, then heard the building door open again below, along with a man’s footsteps, and felt a little afraid. Later I also heard a woman’s high heels, and relaxed, assuming a married couple was coming up—I wasn’t so scared anymore. But the sound kept getting closer, almost right behind me. When I looked back, there was a man crawling up the stairs on all fours—leather dress shoes on his feet, high heels fitted over his hands, eyes fixed dead on me. The “couple behind me” was nothing but an illusion created by two kinds of footsteps.
hints: Both kinds of footsteps really do exist.
That person climbs the stairs on all fours.
He wears leather dress shoes on his feet and high heels over his hands.

title: The Girl on His Back
story: “Let’s play hide-and-seek. I’ll hide, you seek, and it’s only inside the living room—no peeking.” The girl’s voice came clearly to the man’s ears. He finished counting to one hundred, rose from the table, and began searching: behind the sofa, inside the cabinet, under the dining table—nothing. “Come find me,” the girl’s voice sounded again, right beside his ear. He circled the living room forever and never caught sight of her. Suddenly he stared fixedly at one spot, smiled, and said, “Found you.”
answer: What lay on the man’s back was the girl’s ghost. The ghost had no weight and moved wherever the man moved, so the voice stayed close at the man’s ear wherever the man went. The man turned the living room upside down but could never see his own back. Only when the man turned toward the window and the night glass reflected two figures did the man find the girl—in the reflection.
hints: The girl moves along with the man the whole time.
When the man finds her, he is looking at a reflection.
The girl’s ghost is weightless and has been lying on his back all along.

title: The Pen Spirit
story: “Pen spirit, pen spirit, you are my past life and I am your present life; if you wish to renew our bond, draw a circle on the paper.”The melancholy man asked first: “Does she not love me anymore?” The pen moved and settled on the word “Yes”; seeing the answer, he breathed a sigh of relief.The richly dressed old woman asked next: “Is it true that I really will never grow old?” “Yes.” A relieved smile spread over her face.The beautiful young wife asked after her: “Has someone found out my secret?” “Yes.” The young woman grew anxious.Then, of its own accord, the pen began to move again, slowly spelling out a few words: “Do you know who I am?”
answer: The man and the young woman are husband and wife; the old woman is the man’s mother. The marriage had long since broken down. The man had a mistress and could only wish the young woman would stop loving the man, so the divorce would go smoothly. The young woman had a secret of her own: the young woman suspected the child in her belly came from an affair, and quietly ended the pregnancy. On discovering this, the old woman took that abandoned child and made the child into a food the old woman superstitiously believed could keep a person from aging. The pen spirit the three summoned that night was the child’s ghost. The man got the answer that would ease his divorce; the young woman learned her secret had been exposed. The old woman was the most pleased with her answer—never suspecting that “never growing old” was because the ghost intended for the old woman to die that very night.
hints: The three of them are already one family.
The pen spirit knows their secret, which concerns a child.
The abandoned child became the pen spirit; she will never grow old because it is about to kill her.

title: Couldn’t Hold It In
story: After quite a few tumbles, the lock on my cell came loose.I finally couldn’t hold it in any longer, and I burst out in one great rush.
answer: The “I” is a can of cola in a vending machine. It tumbled down the dispensing chute, then got carried and shaken the whole way home (the “tumbles”); the moment the pull tab was popped open (the “lock on the cell coming loose”), it finally couldn’t hold it in, and with a great burst of fizz it sprayed out.
hints: me is a beverage.
The cell is a sealed container, and the lock is the pull tab.
A shaken can of cola sprays out the moment it is opened.

title: Sipping Slowly
story: Two men drank from the same bottle of liquor. One drained his glass in a single go; the other drank slowly.The one who finished first left the bar. The slow drinker had barely reached the door when he collapsed.
answer: The one who finished first and the slow drinker were the heads of two rival gangs, long at odds—and the one who finished first owed the slow drinker a debt he had no intention of repaying—so the one who finished first arranged a meeting, looking for a chance to do away with the slow drinker. The slow drinker always kept bodyguards around, so brute force was unwise; instead, the one who finished first paid the bartender handsomely to slip poison into the ice cubes. The one who finished first drained his glass fast, before the poisoned ice had melted, and walked away unharmed. The slow drinker, no connoisseur of liquor, drank slowly on purpose; the poison in the ice seeped into his drink, and the slow drinker died of the poison.
hints: There was something else in both glasses.
Drinking slowly changed what was in the glass.
The poison was hidden in the ice, and only mixed into the drink once the ice melted.

title: Ice Cream
story: The older brother is wracked with regret: if only he had eaten the ice cream that day, his little brother would not have died.
