answer: Mom had just bought a box of ice cream and put it in the chest freezer out in the storeroom, without shutting the lid. The little brother went to the storeroom to play; reaching for the ice cream, he lost his balance, tumbled into the freezer, and the lid fell shut—the little brother froze to death inside. Coming home from school, the older brother turned down Mom’s suggestion to “go to the storeroom and have some ice cream,” so no one found the little brother. Only at dinnertime did the family discover the little brother dead in the freezer. If the older brother had gone for the ice cream that day, the older brother would have found the little brother trapped inside, and the little brother might not have died.
hints: Eating the ice cream would have taken the older brother to open something.
The little brother was trapped in the freezer where the ice cream was kept.
By refusing to go get ice cream, the older brother missed the chance to find and rescue him.

title: Ice Water
story: A man walked into a restaurant and asked for a glass of ice water. The waiter pulled out a gun and aimed it at him. The man said “thank you” and left.
answer: The man had the hiccups and wanted a glass of ice water to stop them. The waiter saw what was bothering the man and pulled out a fake gun to give the man a fright—and the shock actually cured the man’s hiccups. Not knowing what had really happened, the man left, deeply grateful, with a word of thanks.
hints: He wanted the water to fix a small bodily nuisance.
A sudden fright happened to stop that nuisance.
The man had the hiccups, and after the waiter scared him with a fake gun, they stopped.

title: Terror in the Bathroom
story: After working overtime deep into the night, I hurried home and rushed straight into the bathroom, no time even to switch on the light.I had barely sat down when I shot back up, and without even stopping to fix my pants I bolted out of the house.
answer: I live alone and hadn’t been home all day. My toilet is an ordinary one with no heated seat, yet the seat still held the warmth of a human body. Terrified that someone had just used the bathroom and might still be hiding in the house, I fled at once. I didn’t stay to check, so I can’t be sure whether that person had already left.
hints: What frightened her was what she felt as she sat down.
She lives alone, and she had been away from home all day.
The unheated toilet seat was still warm, so she feared someone had just used it.

title: The Shipwreck Treasure
story: When he found that chest of gold, he decided to tell no one.The sea is so vast, yet he could never again part from that chest.When the last of his air ran out, the gold was still right in front of him.
answer: He was a deep-sea diver. Diving alone, the diver found a chest packed with gold inside an ancient shipwreck. Unwilling to share the treasure with anyone, the diver told none of his companions and tried to haul the chest up himself, misjudging the chest’s weight: as the diver strained on the rope, the rope entangled the diver. Trapped, unable to free himself or call for help, the diver suffocated to death in the water. The diver’s tank had held enough air to see the diver through, had the diver surfaced—but since the diver never came up, the oxygen simply ran out. No one knew where the diver was, and no one came to save the diver—and so the diver died there, for good, of his own greed.
hints: He is a diver.
He tried to bring the chest out of the wreck on his own.
As he hauled it, the rope entangled him; no one knew his location, and his air ran out.

title: Silence
story: The woman put away her knife, stepped over the blood on the floor, and flashed a V-sign at the camera.The screen went black. Lao Zhang gripped his phone, never daring to call the police.
answer: Lao Zhang is a drain-repair handyman. To satisfy his own twisted urges, Lao Zhang often used home repair visits to install tiny hidden cameras in women’s bathrooms. That day, while checking the secret footage, Lao Zhang watched the entire process of the woman—whose drains Lao Zhang had fixed that very morning—murdering someone in her bathroom. What terrified Lao Zhang even more was that after the killing the woman walked right up to the camera, bent down, grinned into the lens, held up a V-sign, and then smashed the camera: the woman had discovered the camera long ago. Lao Zhang didn’t know why the woman had killed someone in her bathroom, and Lao Zhang didn’t want to know. Lao Zhang meant to call the police, but for one thing the woman already knew who Lao Zhang was; for another, a police report would expose the camera Lao Zhang had secretly installed. So silence was Lao Zhang’s only choice.
hints: What Lao Zhang watched was camera footage from inside a private home.
That camera was one he had secretly installed.
The voyeur witnessed a murder but dared not report it: his own crime was exposed, and the killer knew who he was.

title: A Father’s Silent Love
story: The madam said the master had been away on business and hadn’t seen the young lady in ages—so the moment he returned, he took her out for a drive.Who knew the wind and rain that night would be so fierce? The car plunged into the sea.The police asked: “Are you certain it was the master and the young lady?” The driver said: “Absolutely. Please hurry and go save them.”The investigation found only one body in the car—the master’s.And the young lady had been unable to walk for five years already.
answer: Five years earlier, the young lady had lost the ability to walk and had lived away from home ever since. The master coveted the estate in the young lady’s name and wrote again and again to pressure the young lady; in despair the young lady took her own life, and the letters left behind were found by her best friend. Before the master could even break the news of the young lady’s death to the madam, the master stumbled onto the madam’s affair with the driver, and the madam and the driver locked the master away. The madam wanted the fortune too: the madam forged letters in the master’s name summoning the young lady home, planning to do away with father and daughter together. When the letters reached the best friend, the best friend was certain something was wrong, so the best friend went to the meeting in a wheelchair, posing as the young lady. Neither the madam nor the newly hired driver had ever seen the young lady as an adult, and the only one who could have exposed the imposture — the master — was locked away. The madam and the driver got the best friend and the unconscious master into the car; the driver sent the car into the sea, slipped out of it first, then played the witness of the accident and cried for help. The best friend was a good swimmer and freed herself once the car hit the water; when the master came to and tried to escape, the best friend thought of the letters that had driven the young lady to death and pushed the master back down into the car. After reaching shore, the best friend told the police her true identity and everything that had happened inside the car.
hints: The young lady’s physical condition is connected to someone’s escape from the car.
The real young lady was already dead before the drive ever happened.

The best friend went in her name to investigate, walked into the stepmother’s and the driver’s murder plot, survived the plunge into the sea, and took revenge on the father who had driven her friend to death.

title: The Promise
story: “I like you.” It was him, of all people. I was the last girl he would ever like — and he really did keep his word.
answer: He ran into me at the very moment he was confessing his love. Catching sight of him, I thought: he once said I was the last girl he would ever like — and he actually made it true. The person he was confessing to was a boy too: one boy saying “I like you” to another boy. What he said back then was true after all; he never lied to me. He said I was the last girl he would ever like, and I truly am the last girl he ever liked.
hints: The confession was not addressed to me.
me is his ex-girlfriend.
This time he fell in love with a man, so she is still the last girl he ever liked.

title: The Book of Hatreds
story: My great tome was finally finished, yet even turning its pages took effort.Later it was published in the lands of men, and it sold remarkably well.I had no choice but to take out another blank notebook.
answer: I am a grudge-bearing dwarf. Into my Book of Hatreds I wrote down every dwarf joke I ever heard, along with the name of whoever told it, intending to settle accounts one day. The entries piled up until the book grew too thick and heavy to lug about, and looking up a single enemy became a real labor. Worse still, humans got hold of the manuscript and had the jokes printed and published; the readership grew and grew, and so did the number of people mocking dwarves. To keep track of these new grudges, I had no choice but to open a fresh volume.
hints: What the author wrote down was originally meant for revenge.
Readers took it for a collection of jokes.
The dwarf recorded every word of mockery against himself; publication only created more mockers who now had to be recorded.

title: The Restroom I Couldn’t Leave
story: The footsteps faded. Bracing myself against the stall door, I stood up: “I can go out now.”Outside rose the sound of something being dragged. I shrank back inside at once: “No — I can’t.”At last, complete silence fell beyond the door. Then the person who had begged for help pressed close to the gap and asked, “You were there the whole time — why didn’t you open the door?”
answer: After I hid in that restroom, I heard someone being attacked outside; the person begging for help kept pounding on the door. Afraid the killer would discover me, I never dared make a sound. When the killer left to fetch tools, I mistook it for safety; when the killer returned and dragged the body, I could only keep hiding. The person who had begged for help, having died, became a vengeful ghost: the ghost then killed the killer and came to my stall. The ghost remembered that this door had stayed tightly shut while it was begging for help, so the ghost counted me among its enemies too. In the end the ghost passed through the stall door and killed me.
hints: Whether he could leave in the first two moments depended on whether the killer had gone.
The person who spoke at the end was already dead.
The victim’s vengeful ghost came back, killed the murderer, and then took revenge on the one who never opened the door.

title: Come Eat Hotpot
story: I invited my friends over for hotpot. The broth was fiery, and they ate with hisses and gasps. I claimed something urgent had come up and left the house. Once outside the door, I smiled, thoroughly pleased with myself.
answer: I had only just finished renovating the house, but I couldn’t bear to pay anyone to treat the indoor air pollution. I fell for an absurd claim: heat the place up until it is hot and steamy, then get people to breathe deeply inside, and they will draw the formaldehyde out of the house for you. So I lured my friends over for a brutally spicy hotpot and slipped out the door with an excuse. Listening to my friends panting between mouthfuls, I even congratulated myself on the money I had saved.
hints: The house had just been renovated.
The owner had fallen for a claim about treating indoor air pollution.
He treated his friends as tools to breathe the formaldehyde out of the house while he hid outside.

title: The Bed by the Window
story: There were two beds side by side in the hospital room, one by the window and one away from it, and mine was the one away from the window. One night, the patient by the window died; a day later, I died too.
answer: The patient by the window and I were both unable to get out of bed on our own, kept alive by machines, and the two of us had become friends in that room. The beds could not be swapped at will; only when the patient by the window died could I, in the bed away from the window, move to the window. I had sunk into despair and begun to think of ending my life. To keep me willing to live, the patient by the window told me every day, “The view outside is so beautiful” — in truth there was nothing outside but a wall; it was a lie told out of kindness. But I could not see the view myself, and little by little jealousy took root. Then one day the patient by the window suffered a sudden crisis and could not call the nurse himself; I, who could have pressed the call button for help, pretended not to hear — I wanted the bed by the window, wanted to see outside with my own eyes — and the patient by the window died. When I was finally moved to the bed by the window, I found nothing there but a wall, understood what the patient by the window had been doing for me, and killed myself in remorse.
hints: me had always wanted to move to the window side.
His roommate used to describe the beautiful view outside to him every day.
He deliberately let the chance to save him slip by to get the window bed, only to discover the view had been invented to keep his spirits up.

title: Under the Bed
story: During the holidays I was the only one left in the dormitory because of my part-time job. Late at night, I heard strange noises from downstairs and the clear sound of a door opening; terrified, I quickly hid under my own bed. The next day, I was found dead beneath it.
answer: A girl had fallen to her death from that dormitory building, and that night was exactly the seventh night after the girl’s death — the night when, as legend has it, the soul of the dead returns to the places it knew in life to look for a living substitute to take its place. Because the girl had died by falling, the returning spirit kept the posture of the girl’s death: upside down, head toward the ground. That night the spirit came back to the girl’s old dorm room in that inverted pose, and the instant the spirit’s dangling head swept through the doorway, the spirit’s eyes met mine through the narrow gap beneath the bed where I lay hidden. The sight was so unspeakably horrific that it frightened me to death on the spot.
hints: What came back that night was connected to an old story of the dormitory.
It kept the head-down posture of its fall.
The girl’s spirit returned upside down, head grazing the floor, and looked straight into the eyes of the person hidden under the bed.

title: Porcelain
story: One piece of porcelain after another shattered, and at last I discovered my younger brother’s secret.I told no one. I simply placed a new photograph on his desk.
answer: The porcelain my brother made was cursed: each piece was bound to the life of the person pictured in its design, and whenever a piece shattered, that person died. I first broke a vase by accident, and soon after learned that a colleague I detested had died. Once the coincidence had repeated itself, I discovered the custom design sheets in my brother’s room — every face on them belonged to someone who had quarreled with me. My brother was taking revenge for me. After I pieced it together, I did not stop my brother. Instead, I left a photograph of another enemy on my brother’s desk and waited for the next piece to come out of the kiln.
hints: Each shattered piece corresponds to one death in the real world.
Everyone my brother chose had crossed me at some point.
Porcelain is bound to human lives; once me learned the secret, he supplied the next target himself.

title: The Woman Who Fell to the Ground
story: The moment I stopped, she collapsed in front of me and could not get up.Yet as soon as the man nearby set off, she sprang to her feet and walked off, brisk as could be.
answer: I was riding my e-bike along normally when an old lady on a bicycle came straight at me, riding against the flow of traffic. I pulled over at once to let the old lady pass, but the old lady stopped right in front of me and slowly laid herself down on the ground — a staged-accident scam. So I simply went around the old lady and left. A man who had watched the whole thing now came over unhurried, scooped up the old lady’s bicycle, hopped on, and rode away. Seeing that, the old lady was instantly on her feet and striding after the man at full pace — the collapse was an act, but the bicycle being “walked off with” was a real emergency.
hints: Her injuries were faked.
The man nearby rode off on a bicycle.
While the scammer played injured, someone rode off with her bicycle, and she had to leap up and give chase.

title: The Woman in the Second-to-Last Row
story: There was a woman at the theater who always bought the left-hand seat of the second-to-last row. One day she did not come — and the actor cried at the curtain call.
answer: The woman was the actor’s mother. The mother was blind, yet came to every one of the son’s performances. The left seat of the second-to-last row sits close to the auxiliary speakers, and from there the mother could hear the actor’s voice clearly. That afternoon, the actor had received word of the mother’s death, and still the actor carried the show through to the end. At the curtain call, the lights fell on the seat where the actor had grown used to seeing someone sit, and the actor finally could not hold back the tears.
hints: The woman was one of the actor’s family.
She was blind; she chose that seat to hear the voice clearly.
His mother died that very day; the actor had already received the news, and only wept at the curtain call when he saw the empty seat.

title: Waiting for the Moonlight
story: “The moon is so beautiful tonight.” He said it, gazing at the moon.He lowered his head and added, “It must be your first time seeing it from this angle.”Her eyes were open, and she never answered.
answer: He and she climbed the mountain to enjoy the moon every autumn, and this year went as always — but this time she asked to break up. In the heat of the quarrel he killed her by accident. As he buried the body, the moonlight happened to fall into the pit and light up her eyes, which had never closed in death. Gazing at that pair of eyes filled with moonlight, he let out his fond remark — it was her first time watching the moon while lying down.
hints: They were lovers who climbed the mountain together every year to watch the moon.
This time she asked to break up, and the quarrel ended in a death.
When he spoke, she was lying in the pit he had dug, eyes open toward the sky.

title: The Elevator
story: I got into the elevator to head down to school; before I could press a button, it started going up.When the doors opened, I lunged straight for the close-door button.A bloodied hand reached in.
answer: A girl upstairs had been attacked. The girl fled to the elevator and pressed the call button, and was then killed by the attacker — which is why the elevator rose to the girl’s floor. I was on my way to school; before I could press the ground-floor button inside the car, I was carried up to the scene. When the doors opened, I saw the girl lying in a pool of blood and a man dragging the body. I rushed to close the doors, but the man had already spotted me; the man forced a bloodied hand into the gap, squeezed into the elevator, and killed me, the witness.
hints: The elevator went up because someone upstairs had pressed the call button first.
The person who pressed it was under attack and trying to escape by elevator.
When the doors opened, the victim was already dead and the killer was still on the scene; I had become a witness.

title: Taking Out the Trash
story: Mom has to go into the hospital. I was scared. So every day I raced to be the one who took out the trash.
answer: I once asked my mother where I had come from, and my mother told me, “You were picked out of the trash bin.” I believed it completely. Then one day Mom told me I would soon have a little brother or sister. I was afraid Mom would stop loving me once the baby came, and I figured Mom must be going to the trash bin to pick up the baby — so as long as I took out the trash every single day, Mom and Dad would never have the chance to go to the bin and bring my little sibling home, and I would not lose my parents’ love.
hints: “I” is a small child, worried about the family gaining another kid.
Mom once said I was picked out of the trash bin, and the child believed it all along.
I raced to take out the trash so my parents would have no chance to “pick up” a little sibling from the bin.

title: Thud, Thud, Thud
story: The burglar had only just slipped into a bedroom when he heard a heavy “thud… thud” coming up the stairs, one knock at a time.He ducked under the bed at once.The door opened, and a face skimmed along the floor, passing by the bed.
answer: The burglar had broken into a murderer’s house. The sounds on the stairs came from a corpse: the killer held the corpse by the ankles and hauled the body backward up the steps, the corpse’s head striking every stair on the way up. As the killer dragged the corpse into the bedroom, the dead man’s head tilted toward the space beneath the bed, and the dead man’s unclosed eyes came level with the burglar’s. Only then did the burglar realize whose home he had hidden in, and was too frightened to make a sound.
hints: The sound on the stairs came from something being dragged.
The resident coming home was dragging a corpse upstairs.
The corpse’s head skimmed the floor, landing right at eye level with the burglar under the bed.

title: Who Laughed
story: I came home and told my wife a joke.She didn’t laugh at all — but I heard laughter.That night, the police took me away.
answer: My joke failed to make my wife laugh, but the joke cracked up Lao Wang, who was hiding in the wardrobe. In a rage I killed both my wife and Lao Wang, and the police came for me.
hints: There was someone else in the house I had not seen.
The laughter came from the wardrobe; the man hiding there was having an affair with my wife.
I discovered their affair, killed them both, and that is why the police took me away.

title: Building a Snowman
story: I killed my little sister, and the next year my sister appeared again.
answer: Last winter, my little sister dragged me out to build a snowman, then complained that the snowman I made looked ugly. In a fit of anger I shoved my little sister; my sister’s head struck a rock, and my sister stopped breathing. I hid my sister’s body inside the snowman, rebuilt the snowman, and was even pleased with how the snowman turned out this time. By early spring of the following year, the snowman in the yard slowly melted, and my sister’s body came to light.
hints: When my sister appeared again, it was already early spring of the following year.
Her body had been in the yard all along; the winter had kept it hidden.
I had hidden her inside the snowman; once the snow melted, she came to light.

title: A Loving Couple
story: Xiaoming and his mistress plotted a murder.After his wife “rose from the dead,” he loved her more than ever.The wife was thoroughly satisfied too: she had gotten the marriage she wanted, and she had eliminated her rival with her own hands.
answer: Xiaoming meant to kill his wife, destroy the corpse’s face, and then have his mistress undergo surgery to look like the wife and take over the wife’s identity. The wife discovered the plan ahead of time and turned the plan around: the wife killed the mistress and destroyed the dead woman’s face, so that Xiaoming would take the body for his wife. The wife then posed as the mistress and told Xiaoming she would go through with the surgery as agreed and come back as his wife. Xiaoming believed the real wife was dead and that the woman before him was the mistress who had successfully replaced the wife, so Xiaoming loved the wife without reservation. The wife knew exactly whom Xiaoming was loving, and the wife accepted that devotion all the same: the rival was dead, and both the marriage and Xiaoming stayed with the wife.
hints: Xiaoming had always intended for his mistress to take over his wife’s identity.
The dead woman’s face had been destroyed, so Xiaoming misidentified her.
The dead woman was the mistress; the wife pretended to be “the mistress surgically remade into the wife” and returned to her husband’s side.

title: Burning the Mountain
story: The mountain caught fire, and more and more people came rushing.I watched the pile of empty water bottles rising at my feet, and I smiled.
answer: I made my living collecting empty bottles to sell. Hardly anyone ever came up the mountain, so I set my mind on the firefighting crowds: whenever the mountain burned, people would rush over; with more people around, busy for longer, the crowds would drink the water and perhaps leave more empty bottles behind. I set the fire deliberately, for the sake of those bottles, and waited at the scene to gather the bottles. Watching the rescuers leave their empty water bottles behind, I thought only of how much money the bottles would fetch, and I smiled.
hints: What I cared about was the bottles left over once the water was drunk.
I lived off collecting and selling empty bottles, and I figured a fire would bring more bottles for me to pick up.
I set the fire on purpose, for no reason other than to draw more people here and have them leave their water bottles.

title: Herding Sheep
story: The police asked me to identify a headless female corpse, and I shook my head.Beside me, my mother-in-law said: “My daughter is doing just fine — she’s herding sheep on the back hill.”Hearing that, I smiled.
answer: Every time my wife went back to her family home, my wife would meet her old flame. My mother-in-law had opposed that relationship in its day and, out of guilt, had long covered for the wife and the old flame, telling outsiders her daughter was herding sheep on the back hill. After I found out about the affair, I killed my wife and dumped her body in the river. When the police asked me to identify the corpse, I deliberately denied that the body was my wife. My mother-in-law had no idea her daughter was already dead and kept covering for the daughter the way the mother-in-law always had. Hearing that familiar lie, I realized that this time, without knowing it, the mother-in-law was covering up my wife’s disappearance for me — and I smiled.
hints: The mother-in-law had not laid eyes on her daughter herding sheep that day.
She had used that same line for years to cover for her daughter’s meetings with her old flame.
The daughter had been killed by her husband; the mother-in-law reused her old lie and unknowingly helped the murderer.

title: The Enemy from the Sky
story: In the primordial age, we could only hide beneath the feet of the colossal beasts. Only after our ancestors watched the beasts wage their great war and learned to absorb spiritual energy did our clan slowly grow mighty.Generations later, our forebears finally ascended to the immortal realm. All we received in return was a single line: “Ascension is a trap — the enemy comes from the sky!”The message cut off at once. The clan chief said a great calamity was coming, and that we must guard the last spark of our kind.
answer: This clan that calls itself “the human tribe” is a species of intelligent mutant insects living on a wasted earth. The colossal beasts are humans; the beasts’ great war is a nuclear war; the spiritual energy is radiation, which these insects can harness. The insects multiplied across the postwar surface, contending with other mutated animals for territory. Some humans lived aboard orbital ships, hoping to find a way to reclaim the surface, so the humans sent collection devices down that carried the insects up for study. The swarm called the journey — rising into the sky and entering a ship — “ascension,” believing the forebears had arrived in the immortal realm. One forebear sent back the warning just before being dissected, and contact was lost. More collection devices will fall from the sky again, and that is the world-ending calamity the clan chief spoke of.
hints: The “colossal beasts,” the “spiritual energy,” and the “immortal realm” are simply this clan’s names for what it has seen.
The beasts’ great war was a nuclear war, and this species survives by harnessing radiation.
They are intelligent mutant insects; the so-called ascension is being collected by humans for study aboard the orbital ships.

title: Who Do You Choose?
story: Mom and Dad asked me yet again: “Who are you going to live with?”I could not bear to give up either of them, so I came up with a fair solution.Afterwards, they finally stopped forcing me to choose.
answer: Mom and Dad were heading for divorce, and every quarrel ended with them pressing me to choose whom to live with. I could not bear to lose either side, and the relentless questioning wore me down until I took “both of them can have me” to mean splitting myself into two halves. I acted on that thought and hurt myself badly, and in the end I could not be saved. Mom and Dad lost me, and there was no custody left to fight over.
hints: The parents are divorcing, and their fights are over which of them the child will live with.
The child took “each side gets a share of me” as a way to settle it.
He tried to split himself in half and gravely injured himself; in the end, both parents lost him.

title: Sharing Hobbies
story: I got to talking about hobbies with someone I had only just met. He went first, and what I heard left me speechless.When my turn came, he cut in: “I know. You were playing last night, too.”Suddenly I no longer felt like continuing the conversation.
answer: He said his hobby was stalking people. I took the remark for an uncomfortable joke in poor taste. When I said that I liked playing video games in my free time, he immediately said he knew, and brought up the fact that I had been gaming at home the night before. We had only just met, and I had never posted anything about my life online. Only then did I understand: his hobby had long since been practiced on me.
hints: His hobby intrudes on other people’s private lives.
The hobby he named first was stalking people; I took it as a joke at the time.
He had been stalking me all along, which is how he knew I was gaming at home last night.

title: Senior Year
story: In my final year of high school, I did something wrong, thought it had gone unnoticed, and counted myself lucky that I could keep going to school.At a class reunion years later, I apologized to my teacher.After I heard his reply, I cried.
answer: In my final year, my family could not afford the full tuition, so I slipped counterfeit bills into the money I handed to my teacher. No one ever pursued the matter, and I assumed the teacher had not noticed. In fact, the teacher had seen the counterfeit bills from the start; so that I could stay in school, the teacher quietly made up the shortfall from his own salary. Years later a classmate brought the matter up, and at the reunion I apologized to my teacher. The teacher said: “You wanted to stay in school back then, so I just made up the tuition for you.” Only then did I learn that my clean escape in those years had rested on my teacher keeping my secret all along.
hints: The wrong act had to do with paying tuition, and the family was in hardship at the time.
I slipped counterfeit bills into the tuition money, thinking my teacher had not noticed.
The teacher did notice; he quietly covered the shortfall with his own salary so that I could keep studying.

title: The Confession
story: Trapped in an elevator, the husband wanted to leave his wife one last “I love you.”He blurted it out to his phone in a panic, and the message was sent.When his wife read it, she shot back: “If you love him, then go to him!”
answer: Trapped in the elevator and fearing something might happen, the husband used voice input to text his wife. Flustered, the husband said: “Tell my wife I love her.” But in spoken Chinese, “her” and “him” are the exact same word — tā — and the phone’s transcription picked the male one, turning “I love her” into “I love him.” The husband sent the text without checking the message. The wife had no idea the husband was trapped; all the wife saw was her husband suddenly sending words that read like an admission of loving another man, and the wife angrily replied. The husband had meant to confess his love, and the identical-sounding pronoun turned the confession into a misunderstanding.
hints: What the wife read was written text; what the husband had produced was spoken sound.
He sent the message by voice input and did not check the text in his panic.
In spoken Chinese “her” and “him” sound identical; “I love her” was transcribed as “I love him,” and the wife thought her husband loved someone else.

title: Shine My Shoes
story: He ducked into an alley, pulled off his jacket, and walked back out unhurried.The police ran right past him.He stopped at the curb: “Give my shoes a shine.”The shoe-shiner looked up at him: “He’s the one.”
answer: He was the jewel-store robber. Spotted by the security guard during the robbery, the robber killed the guard and bolted into the alley to change his outfit. The robber’s shoes had hidden lifts inside; with the jacket swapped, the appearance and height the witnesses had noted no longer matched him before the witnesses, and the pursuing officers ran past without recognizing the robber. Yet he could never bring himself to give up that specially made pair of leather shoes. The guard’s family watched the surveillance footage over and over, memorizing the shoes’ distinctive seam pattern and their old repair marks, then set up nearby posing as a shoe-shiner to wait. The day he sat down for a shine, the family member saw the same telltale features up close, recognized the suspect, and immediately alerted the police; the follow-up investigation confirmed the robber’s identity.
hints: He was evading pursuit: he changed his jacket in the alley but never changed his shoes.
The clue the shoe-shiner knew came from surveillance footage of a murder at a jewelry store.
The shoe-shiner is a relative of the slain guard, waiting specifically for that pair of leather shoes with their distinctive repair marks to appear again.

title: Stay Close to the Grown-ups
story: Mom said that crossing the road is safe as long as you follow a grown-up.There was no traffic light that day, so I walked close behind a man.He didn’t stop, and neither did I. Neither of us ever reached the other side.
answer: I had just started first grade. My parents were busy with work and had me walk to school by myself. Mom instructed me that at intersections without traffic lights, I should cross together with a grown-up. I always believed that grown-ups judged the safety first. But the man that day had already resolved to end his life; the man was carrying a suicide note and walked deliberately into the onrushing traffic. Knowing nothing of the man’s intent, I kept following right behind the man, and the man and I were both killed in the accident. The following that used to reassure me had led me straight into a danger a grown-up had chosen for himself.
hints: The child assumed every grown-up crossing the road was judging whether it was safe.
That man was carrying a suicide note, and his purpose was entirely different from the child’s.
The man walked into the traffic on purpose to end his life; the child, not knowing, followed him and died in the same accident.

title: The Bus
story: I stood by the handrail of the bus. The cabin was cold, and a stench of rot hung in the air, never dispersing.One after another, they came toward me, and not one of them looked at me.Then someone stepped into the very spot where I was standing.
answer: I had already died on that bus. The killer dismembered my body and hid the corpse in a secret compartment beneath the floor, and the bus kept running its route every day as usual. My ghost stayed on board, and at first I even took myself for an ordinary passenger. The passengers could not see me and walked straight through my body — which is why a passenger could stand directly in my spot. The stench in the cabin came from the corpse under the floor that no one had found. The driver assumed a dead rat was hidden somewhere in the bus and never tracked down the source; what I kept smelling was my own body.
hints: The passengers cannot see me, and they can stand in the very spot I occupy.
I am already dead; my ghost remains on this bus that still runs its route.
The smell comes from the corpse hidden in the compartment beneath the bus floor — my own remains.

title: The Lonely Old Man
story: A neighbor brought over a bag of fish, saying they were no longer fresh and might as well be fed to the cats.A few days later, the old man was found dead beside his dining table, his body no longer whole.The cats he had taken in were still alive, and the doors and windows had been shut tight the whole time.
answer: The old man lived on a tight budget and had taken in many stray cats. The neighbor resented the cats’ noise and smell, so the neighbor poisoned the fish, hoping the old man’s own hands would do the work of killing the cats. But the old man could not bear to waste fish that still looked fresh; the old man cooked and ate the fish himself and died at home of the poison before giving any to the cats. Locked inside with no one to feed the cats, the starving cats eventually gnawed at the old man’s remains — which is why the body was found mutilated. The neighbor who delivered the fish had targeted the cats; in the end, that same neighbor killed the man who had sheltered the cats.
hints: The neighbors had hoped the bag of fish would be eaten by the cats.
The fish were poisoned, but the old man could not bear to give them to the cats and ate them himself.
After the old man died, the cats were shut in with nothing to eat and gnawed at his remains.

title: Stay Away from Water
story: He once nearly drowned, and from then on he dared not go near even the edge of the water.Later, he took a job on a farm far from any river or lake.In the end, he was “drowned” in a dry barn.
answer: Because he feared water, he took farm work that had nothing to do with water — and the accident happened in the grain bin. The bin was being unloaded, the grain streaming out from the bottom. He sank into the flowing grain, could not free himself, was buried completely, and died of suffocation. It was grain that pulled him under; water had nothing to do with the death.
hints: The word “drowned” is in quotation marks because there was no water at the scene.
The farm he worked on stored large amounts of grain.
The grain being unloaded swallowed and buried him; he died because he could not breathe.

title: The Applause
story: In a fit of anger he left his girlfriend in the wilderness, then turned back to pick her up, believing they had made up.A few claps of applause sounded in the car, and he never managed to drive it home.When the car was found, he was dead in the driver’s seat, his face frozen in terror.
answer: He had left his girlfriend on a desolate roadside and driven off alone. While his girlfriend waited, she was murdered, and her ghost stayed right where she had died. Regretting it, he drove back, saw his girlfriend standing there, assumed she was safe and sound, and let her into the car. Partway along, a ghostly figure stepped out to flag the car down, beckoning with gestures the reverse of a living person’s. He sped past and told her that the ghosts around here beckoned and clapped in ways opposite to the living. She smiled and said, “You really do know a lot.” Then she brought the backs of her hands together and slowly clapped. Only then did he realize that the woman he had picked up was a ghost too. The girlfriend’s ghost killed him; afterward, all anyone found was him and the car parked by the roadside.
hints: Before he turned back, his girlfriend had already been murdered in the wilderness.
In this story, ghosts make gestures with their hands turned the opposite way from the living.
The girlfriend clapped with the backs of her hands facing each other, and that was how he knew the person beside him was already dead.

title: The Contact
story: I had finally escaped the prison, and lay in the dark waiting for the man who was to meet me.I struck a match and recognized the person lying beside me.No one would ever come for me again.
answer: I had bribed a guard who handled the prison’s burials, and we agreed that the next time an inmate died, I would secretly climb into the coffin and be carried out with the body; once the coffin was buried, the guard would come and dig me up. Then one day came news that someone had died. Without asking who the deceased was, I slipped into the coffin being prepared for removal. After the coffin was buried, I struck a match and found that the corpse beside me was the very guard who had promised to save me. The guard was dead. No one outside knew of my plan, and no one knew there was a living man inside the coffin. In the end I died trapped in the coffin.
hints: The escape plan made use of the prison’s arrangements for burying its dead.
I hid inside the coffin and waited for the bribed guard to dig me out after the burial.
The body the matchlight revealed was that very guard — my only contact was already dead.

title: The Host’s Note
story: He folded a note and put it in his pocket.It read:“You are the host. They are the players.Answer only yes or no, give away as little as possible, and lie when necessary.They will attack you. Hold it in, do not strike back. Time is limited; hold out.Do not let them guess the answer to the soup, or you will never get out.”
answer: He was a criminal suspect, and the note was coded coaching from his accomplices on how to handle an interrogation. “Host” meant the suspect being questioned; “players” meant the police pressing the suspect for details of the case; “the soup’s answer” meant the true account of the crime. Giving away little and lying were the accomplices’ tactics for concealing the facts, and “attack” referred to the questioning and pressure from the police. The suspect meant to stall the interrogation, betting that the police would never gather enough evidence and that the suspect would eventually be released. The note dressed a scheme of denial in the language of turtle soup; if the truth about the crime came out, his hope of walking free would collapse.
hints: The turtle-soup roles on the note are metaphors for a different question-and-answer scenario.
He hoped the questioners would never get to the truth, so that he could walk away.
He is the suspect; the “players” are the police interrogating him, and “the soup’s answer” is what really happened in the crime.

title: The Wi-Fi at Her Best Friend’s Place
story: It was my first time going with my wife to visit her best friend’s home.Yet after we came back, my wife was determined to divorce me.
answer: My wife took me to her best friend’s home for the first time, and saw my phone automatically connect to the Wi-Fi there. I had told my wife before that I had never been, but I had once been having an affair with the best friend and had come here alone many times, and my phone had saved the network’s password. The auto-connect made my wife start to doubt that claim of a “first visit.” When my wife pressed me, I admitted the affair; back home, my wife asked for a divorce.
hints: During the visit, my wife noticed that my phone had automatically connected to the home’s wireless network.
The phone had the network’s password saved, even though I had claimed I had never been there.
The connection aroused her suspicion, and when she pressed me I admitted the affair with her best friend.

title: The Cough
story: Xiaobai had been making coughing sounds nonstop these past few days, and its owner was coughing too.He took Xiaobai to the hospital.After examining Xiaobai, the doctor said Xiaobai was perfectly healthy.
answer: Xiaobai is a parrot. When the owner fell ill and coughed without stop, Xiaobai learned to copy the sound. Thinking the bird was sick, the owner took Xiaobai to a pet hospital, and after the checkup the doctor told the owner: Xiaobai is perfectly healthy — the bird is only imitating the sounds it hears.
hints: Xiaobai and the owner are two different beings.
Xiaobai can imitate sounds its owner makes.
Xiaobai is a parrot that learned its sick owner’s cough; it is not sick itself.

title: Still Alive
story: I am a doctor, seeing patients day after day. That day, a patient walked in and froze the moment he saw me: “How are you still alive?”
answer: I am a doctor who removes hemorrhoids. Once, the Tang Monk came to me to have a hemorrhoid cut away. After the Tang Monk left, I ate the piece of flesh that had been removed — it was the flesh of the Tang Monk (the monk Tang Sanzang of legend, whose flesh grants immortality to whoever eats it) — and from then on I could not die. Several hundred years later, the Tang Monk came back to have another hemorrhoid removed, saw that I was still alive, and asked in astonishment: “Don’t tell me you ate my hemorrhoid?”
hints: This patient’s previous visit to the doctor was several hundred years ago.
The doctor once cut a small piece of flesh from him and secretly ate it.
The patient is the Tang Monk; the doctor ate the Tang Monk’s flesh cut away in surgery, and so became immortal.

title: The Ocean-View Apartment
story: In one ocean-view tower, fifteen households were hit by murders within a single month, and every victim lived on the sea-facing side.The police had not caught the killer, yet the killings suddenly stopped.Later, a girl moved into the building, wheeling her father in his hospital bed.
answer: The girl and her father had lived in an old house across the way, and when the tower went up, the building blocked the father and daughter’s view of the sea. The father promised that one day father and daughter would move into that tower, and the father worked himself to the bone for four years, only to collapse from illness with savings still nowhere near enough. So the girl began killing the residents on the tower’s sea-facing side. The string of murders kept buyers away, and one of the stricken apartments was put up for sale in a hurry at a steep discount, finally dropping within reach of the father’s savings. The girl bought the apartment and stopped killing. The girl wheeled her father to the window and drew back the curtain: “Dad, look.” The father finally saw the sea, never knowing that his daughter had killed fifteen people for that window.
hints: The direction the victims’ apartments faced is connected to the girl who later moved into the building.
The girl and her father used to live across the way; the tower had blocked their sea view, and they could not afford an apartment in it.
She used the string of murders to make the apartments hard to sell; after buying one at a deep discount, she stopped killing.

title: The Noisy Neighbor
story: My neighbor was making noise again, and I could not play my clarinet, so I went to knock on his fruit-shaped house.His pet went “meow” and slowly crawled back inside.He came out, and looking at the countless little holes all over his body, I got even more annoyed.
answer: I am Squidward, and the neighbor is SpongeBob. We live in Bikini Bottom; SpongeBob’s house is a pineapple under the sea, and the neighbor’s pet is Gary, a snail that meows like a cat. SpongeBob’s body is covered in holes to begin with, and in my irritation at the noise, the sight of those holes annoyed me all the more.
hints: The story takes place in a cartoon world, and the shape of the house is an important clue.
The neighbor lives in a pineapple under the sea, and his pet is a snail that goes “meow.”
The one playing the clarinet is Squidward; the neighbor who comes to the door is SpongeBob.

title: The Chosen Day
story: My family sold me into a rich and powerful household. After I became pregnant, they chose the day the child would be born.On that day, before I was full term, I was taken away to give birth, then told the baby was gone.Yet my gravely ill father-in-law had a whole banquet table laid out.
answer: The father-in-law was dying and believed a folk remedy: that a baby carrying the father-in-law’s own bloodline and born at a designated hour could serve as a “medicine primer” — the guiding ingredient of a folk prescription — and extend the old man’s life. The father-in-law had the household buy a woman to bear the son’s child, and arranged the delivery date in advance. In my eighth month, the family forced me into labor, took the baby away, and told me the baby had been stillborn. The banquet celebrated the family’s finally getting the medicine primer. I quietly looked into the matter and learned that my child had been used to satisfy the old man’s superstitious hope — that buying me and scheduling the birth had all been for this — and I broke down completely.
hints: The delivery date was set by the household in advance; whether the baby was full term had nothing to do with it.
The father-in-law believed that to extend his life he needed an infant of his own bloodline, born at a designated hour.
They bought me to bear a child, forced an early delivery, lied that it was stillborn, and used the baby as the medicine primer of a folk remedy.

title: Good Boy
story: Late at night, a stranger slipped into the house. I remembered what my owners had taught me: “Be a good boy.”I held it in and did not make a single sound.Later, the news reported the murder of the family; the killer’s whereabouts remain unknown.
answer: I am a dog. Like many dogs I was on guard, barking whenever anyone came to the house. But my owners hated that, had had enough of the days when I barked loudly at the courier, the mail carrier, even the owners’ friends, and trained me to hold back the urge to bark. This time, I was jolted awake while sleeping in the backyard and saw a stranger sneaking into my owners’ home in the dead of night. I never let out a single bark. I was a good boy, and I watched with my own eyes as the stranger slaughtered my owners one by one. That is how the killer walked free, and to this day no one knows the killer’s whereabouts.
hints: “Good boy” was what my owners said to me over and over during training.
I am a dog, and my owners had repeatedly stopped me from barking at visitors.
When the intruder came, I stayed silent as I had been trained, and my owners lost their one chance of a warning.

title: The Good Samaritan
story: A kind-hearted man caught the person who had stolen our things and told me and the girl beside me to come along to the police station.The girl had had things stolen too, so I followed them.After we turned into a deserted alley, the girl suddenly blocked my way.
answer: The “kind-hearted man,” the thief, and the girl were all one gang of human traffickers. The gang staged a theft first, then one of the traffickers stepped in to catch the thief, while the girl posed as another victim and went along with me, steering me toward a place under the gang’s control. When the girl blocked my path, the kind-hearted man and the thief dropped the act as well. Realizing I had been tricked, I fought back and tried to run, and the traffickers killed me. The rescuer, the suspect, and the other victim were all roles in the same trap.
hints: The girl beside me had not really had anything stolen.
The kind-hearted man, the thief, and the girl all knew one another and were putting on a show together.
They were human traffickers who used the catch-the-thief-and-go-to-the-police pretext to lead me somewhere deserted, and they killed me when I fought back.

title: Domestic Harmony
story: Everyone in the village envied me: a son and a daughter, a loving couple, a devoted daughter-in-law, a successful son-in-law. This New Year, only my daughter came home to see me, her eyes brimming with tears. When the neighbors came round with New Year greetings and asked what had happened, I told them: my daughter-in-law is tied up at the cold-storage facility with no time to come home; my son is busy running around taking care of her; my son-in-law has gone far away to make big money; and my daughter and her husband are so devoted that, unable to see him over the New Year, she misses him and cries every day.
answer: The son-in-law tried to force himself on the daughter-in-law; when the daughter-in-law fought back, the son-in-law killed the daughter-in-law and hid the body in the cold-storage room. On learning the truth, my son gathered evidence everywhere and hired a lawyer to bring the killer to justice. My daughter came to me in tears, begging me to talk my son into dropping the case and sparing the son-in-law. I had always prized the appearance of a harmonious family above all; terrified that the scandal would get out, I took my daughter’s side and ended up estranged from my son. In the end the son-in-law went to prison, my son stopped coming home, and this New Year only my daughter came, weeping and pleading. Even then I would not admit the truth to the neighbors: my daughter-in-law in the cold storage is already dead; my son’s running around is a fight to win justice for the daughter-in-law; my son-in-law’s “going far away” is a prison cell; and my daughter’s tears fall because I could not make my son spare the son-in-law. I had dressed each family member’s fate up in a flattering story.
hints: What I told the villagers hid what had really happened to every member of the family.
The daughter-in-law was murdered by the son-in-law and her body hidden in the cold storage; the son is fighting to win her justice.
My daughter begged me to shield her husband and I fell out with my son; even after the son-in-law was jailed, I kept papering over the scandal with talk of family harmony.

title: Tragedy by the River
story: Lao Wang threw something out by the river, and the dog bounded eagerly after it.Moments later, Lao Wang was running for his life, shouting at the dog: “Stay away!”They both died by the river.
answer: Lao Wang often went blast fishing at the river alone, and this time brought along the dog, who loved to fetch whatever he threw. Lao Wang hurled an already-lit explosive far out, and the dog, thinking he wanted to play again, ran over, picked up the charge in its mouth, and raced back toward Lao Wang. The moment Lao Wang made out what was in the dog’s mouth, he fled, but the dog kept chasing after him. The explosive went off, and neither Lao Wang nor the dog survived.
hints: The dog was trained to love fetching back whatever its master threw.
Lao Wang was blast fishing at the river; what he threw was an already-lit explosive.
The dog carried the explosive back and kept chasing him, and when it blew, neither of them could get clear in time.

title: The Black Cat
story: I killed my neighbor.As the police led me out, the black cat that often came begging for food stood at the door with something in its mouth.I suddenly understood that I had been wrong.
answer: I live on the second floor and often saw a black cat down below. My work kept sending me on business trips, so I could only feed the cat now and then.That day I came home from a trip and found several dead mice scattered across my balcony. My first thought was of the neighbor I was always clashing with — I assumed he had thrown the mice over on purpose. In a fury I stormed into the neighbor’s home to confront him, lost control, and struck him, and went on until the sirens sounded.As I was being led out, I saw that black cat again. The cat held a mouse in its mouth and watched me quietly. Only in that moment did I understand: those mice had been caught by the cat.I had gotten it wrong — and I had killed my neighbor.
hints: I had clashed with my neighbor over several dead mice that turned up on my balcony.
I assumed the neighbor had thrown the mice over on purpose; in fact, the black cat often accepted food from me.
What the cat carried in its mouth was a mouse; the mice on the balcony had been brought by it too, and because of them I killed my neighbor by mistake.

title: The Black Giant
story: A sharp, acrid smell filled my nostrils. Outside the window, a black giant was pressed flat against the glass, watching me. But I felt no fear.
answer: I am a dog, alone in the villa, waiting for my master to come home. My master had been murdered out there, and the killer hung the master’s body outside our window. In the night, that body — far taller than I am — stood against the light from inside the house, leaving only a huge black outline. As time passed, the corpse began to reek of decay, but I could still catch my master’s familiar scent in the corpse. Not understanding that my master was dead, I stayed by the window the whole time and never took that black shape for a stranger.
hints: The “giant” is huge only relative to me’s own height.
me is a dog, home alone waiting for its master, and it recognized a familiar scent.
What hung outside the window was its master’s body after he was murdered; the dog still believed its master had come home.

title: The Red Dress
story: On my birthday, I put on the red dress that had arrived at the shop that very day and sat down to a candlelit dinner with my husband. He lit the candles on the cake and said to me: “Make a wish.” I lowered my head and made my wish. Half a minute later, I said to him: you are having an affair.
answer: I am a fashion designer, and the dress I wore to dinner was the red one delivered to the shop that same day, not yet put on display. Some time before, I had sewn a sample of the dress myself, kept at home, with a unique mark of mine on the hem. While making my wish I merely narrowed my eyes — and saw my husband open a new message: in the photo, a woman was wearing the same red dress, in the bedroom of my home. The mark on the hem showed the woman was wearing the sample from our house. I confronted my husband on the spot, and my husband admitted bringing the woman home and giving the woman the sample to wear. That charge of cheating came from the photo I saw by candlelight.
hints: While making my wish, I kept my eyes narrowed and was secretly watching my husband’s phone.
I designed the red dress, and a sample with a unique mark was kept at home.
The woman in the photo was wearing that sample in my bedroom; my husband then admitted the affair.

title: She Chose Me
story: I put on my older sister’s red dress.Sure enough, Mom chose me.After that, my sister never came back.
answer: My sister and I are twins who look almost exactly alike. My sister was the gentle one; Mom favored my sister and always bought my sister pretty red dresses. I suggested we swap clothes, and my sister took it for a game to see whether Mom could tell us apart. On a walk by the river I roughhoused with my sister on purpose so that we both fell into the water. Panicking, Mom went by the red dress, swam first to the daughter Mom took for my sister, and pulled me out. My real sister was never rescued and drowned. With that one dress, I made Mom choose me at the moment of life and death.
hints: The red dress usually belonged to my sister, and Mom was used to telling the twins apart by it.
After the two of us swapped clothes, we fell into the river together.
Mom meant to save the sister she favored, but went by the dress and saved the wrong girl — the younger sister who had swapped the clothes on purpose.

title: The Newlyweds on Stage
story: After their honeymoon, the newlyweds were set out on the same table.The crowd below the stage gathered around, laughing as they watched. The two were within arm’s reach of each other, yet they could not embrace.Someone called out a price, and one of them was about to be carried off.
answer: The couple was kidnapped while traveling and mutilated so badly that both lost their limbs. The kidnappers put the two of them each into a neighboring vase with only the head showing, as exhibits for an underground show and trade. The crowd below was watching and bidding. The couple could see each other but had no way to reach out and touch. At the auction to come, they might well be sold separately, and neither knew whether they would ever see each other again.
hints: They were kidnapped, and the crowd watching them is bidding to buy them.
Each of them is sealed inside a container with only the head exposed.
They lost their limbs and are being displayed in neighboring vases, unable to embrace, and they may be sold apart.

title: The Makeup Artist
story: I made good money with makeup, though most of it came from another line of business.That day, while I was moving one of my “clients,” I broke his face.The family did not press me about the wound; they simply called the police.
answer: I am a mortuary makeup artist. On the side, I secretly sold corpses, then painted up a life-size paper figure to pass for the deceased and laid the figure in the coffin as a stand-in. With clothing covering the paper body, the family believed during the brief farewell that their loved one’s body was still there, and I pocketed the extra money. This time, while moving the paper figure, I tore the figure’s face open. The ceremony had already begun, and there was no time to make another stand-in, so I tried to bluff my way through. The family saw the paper inside the tear, realized the coffin held none of their loved one’s body, and called the police, exposing the corpse-selling.
hints: My regular job is applying makeup to the dead for funerals.
The extra income comes from secretly selling corpses, so I have to put a substitute in the coffin.
The substitute is a made-up paper figure; the torn face exposed the paper, and that is how the family found out the body had been sold.

title: The Evil Eye in the Painting
story: A woman reporter checked into a small inn in a remote village and took the wall across from her bed for a portrait of a man.The man in the painting had no right arm, and his eyes stayed fixed on her.The next day she begged the innkeeper for help in terror, but he said with satisfaction: “Now that’s normal.”
answer: In this remote village cut off from the outside world, everyone was born with only a left arm, so people with two whole arms were seen as diseased. What the woman reporter took for a painting was in fact a window in a dim corner, and a man was standing outside the window, watching her. The man had fallen for her, yet believed her extra right arm was a sickness that had to be removed. That night the man broke into her room, attacked her, and took her right arm off by force. When she begged the innkeeper for help, the innkeeper could not understand her fear at all; the innkeeper thought she had finally become the same as everyone else in the village and had been cured.
hints: What she took for a portrait is a window, and the man has been standing outside it all along.
The villagers are born with only a left arm and regard two whole arms as abnormal.
Acting on that twisted belief, the man harmed her, and the innkeeper takes the loss of her right arm as a cure.

title: His “Child”
story: My husband’s belly swelled a little more each day, while he grew thinner and thinner.I laid my hand on it and said with a smile: “The baby just moved again.”Now, at last, he must understand how I suffered back then.
answer: When I was pregnant, my husband betrayed me. In those days I lost the child, and I laid all the pain and hatred on him. For revenge, I gave him a severe parasitic infection and kept him locked to the bed, forbidding any doctor. As his belly bloated and his body wasted away, I called the roundworms inside him my “child” and treated the stirrings of his sick abdomen as the baby’s kicks, feeding him every day, dreaming that this would force him to feel exactly what I had endured. My husband was never pregnant; I was torturing him with disease.
hints: The loved one is a man, and the “child” and “fetal movement” are names me forces onto the situation.
His swollen belly and wasting body come from a severe parasitic infection, and he is kept away from doctors.
After losing her child, me takes revenge on her husband, calls the roundworms her baby, and imagines she is making him experience pregnancy.

title: The Bus in the Middle of Nowhere
story: I fought with my boyfriend the whole ride, until the driver put me off the bus.After dark, the bus came back, and I finally breathed a sigh of relief.The door opened, and the woman driver stepped down: “That was quite the cursing earlier. Go on, keep cursing.”
answer: I had discovered over the phone that my boyfriend was cheating, and I furiously cursed my boyfriend and the other woman; my crying and shouting got on the driver’s nerves. After passengers complained, the driver put me off at the next stop. I was too swallowed up in grief to notice, and only after nightfall did I see how remote the place was; by then my phone was dead too. From my call, the driver had recognized my boyfriend: the woman I was cursing was the driver herself. The driver finished the shift, then drove the bus back alone to the spot where the driver had dropped me. Thinking the driver had come to my rescue, I let my guard down. The driver stepped off, revealed who the driver really was, led me out into the wild, and killed me.
hints: The driver overheard my phone call, in which I confronted my boyfriend and cursed another woman.
The call let her recognize who my boyfriend was, which is why she came back for me alone.
The woman driver is the one my boyfriend cheated with; after putting me off the bus, she came back alone to kill me.

title: Regained Sight
story: That day, the disaster struck, and I went blind along with every other person on Earth.Two years later, my sight suddenly came back.Just as I was about to share the news with everyone, I saw that sentence, and I clamped my hand hard over my mouth.
answer: The disaster left everyone blind. The new government that rose afterward was run by blind people, who wrote blindness into law as the normal state. Over the two years, some people’s sight gradually returned, but the new government feared the newly sighted would hold more information and shake the new government’s control, so the government secretly arrested and imprisoned the newly sighted as heretics. Those who escaped could not warn others openly; the escapees could only write on walls and doorways: “Do not tell them you can see.” The still-blind would never notice the words, but the newly sighted would read the words. I saw the warning just as I was about to announce my recovery, and that is why I covered my mouth at once and went on pretending to be blind.
hints: After the disaster, the definition of “normal” was rewritten.
People who regain their sight may be secretly taken away by the new government; the writing on the wall is a warning left by escapees.
The sentence is “Do not tell them you can see,” and I must keep playing blind.

title: The Sound in the Subtitles
story: He stared at the movie’s subtitles with full attention.After one line appeared, a flood of old memories came back to him, and he slowly shrank down into his seat.The movie was not over yet, but he already wanted to leave.
answer: He had been deaf since childhood and had always assumed that passing gas was a bodily change only he could feel. This movie played with captions for the deaf. In one scene, a character passed gas, a person beside the character turned to look, and the caption noted “(fart sound).” He had passed gas in his own seat just before, and only now did he understand that the movement he felt might also make a sound. He remembered all the times people around him had looked over after he did it, and the embarrassment left him wanting nothing but to get out of there. The caption was describing a sound in the movie, yet it taught him something he had missed for years.
hints: Besides dialogue, the captions also describe sounds in the movie.
Deaf since childhood, he sees a sound cue and realizes a certain bodily event of his could have been heard by others.
The caption reads “(fart sound)”; he realizes his years of passing gas in public may have come with sound, and the embarrassment overwhelms him.

title: Calling Daddy
story: The little girl refused to call him Daddy, and the man got angry. After a while, the girl did call out “Daddy.” This time, the man was terrified.
answer: The man had always wanted to be a father. On Father’s Day the man lured a girl who had wandered off alone into a back alley and forced the girl to call the man Daddy. The girl never made a sound, and when the man’s anger boiled over, the man decided the girl must be unable to speak, so the man meant to take the girl home and keep the girl caged as his daughter. On the way, the girl caught sight of the real father out searching for the girl and suddenly screamed “Daddy!” The real father heard the cry and recognized both his own daughter and the stranger leading the girl away. Only then did the man realize the girl had simply been staying silent before, and that the girl’s one cry had just given the man away to the person coming to save the girl.
hints: The two cries of “Daddy” are meant for two different men.
The man with the girl is her kidnapper, and he wrongly believes she cannot speak.
The girl’s later cry is for her real father, who is out looking for her, and that cry exposes the kidnapper.

title: Murder on the Death Anniversary
story: On the first anniversary of my son’s death, three people came who truly mourned him. Not one of them had ever met my son while he lived; they only came to “know” him after he died. And on this very anniversary, I killed all three with my own hands.
answer: Before dying, my son asked to donate his organs and tissue, saying this way my son could stay behind in another form. Once I consented, my son’s skin, lungs, and liver each went to save a different person. The recipients reached out to me themselves and came to mourn my son on the first anniversary of my son’s death. That day, I saw the one carrying my son’s skin had tattoos, the young man carrying my son’s lungs was smoking, and the one carrying my son’s liver was on the phone arranging drinks. I read every bit of it as a betrayal of my son’s dying wish, and I treated the recipients’ bodies as something that still belonged to my son and was mine to police for my son. The recipients had come out of genuine grief, yet that rage and that possessiveness drove me to kill all three.
hints: They were saved by my son’s donations and came of their own will to honor the donor who helped them.
My son’s skin, lungs, and liver each went to a different person.
Seeing the tattoos, the smoking, and the drinking plans, I decided they were squandering my son’s last gift and killed them in fury.

title: Calling in a Parent
story: The school asked for my parents, so I brought along a “Dad.”But the instant the teacher saw him, he gave the two of us a scolding together.
answer: I did not dare tell my parents the school had called my parents in, so I found an old man on the street and paid him to play my father and walk with me into the office. The teacher recognized him at a glance, because he was the teacher’s own father. He had helped me lie to his own child, and I was exposed on the spot; the two of us took the scolding together.
hints: The “Dad” I brought is someone hired to pose as a parent.
The teacher already knows this old man.
The old man is the teacher’s own father; the fake parent walked straight into his own child.

title: Thanks at the Funeral
story: He finished his last dangerous mission, and his superior pushed a case of payment across to him.The next day, word spread that he had been assassinated.At the funeral, a mourner nobody recognized passed by the superior and said in a low voice: “I cannot thank you enough.”
answer: He was an undercover agent inside a criminal organization. After the final operation, there were still people who remembered his old identity, so his superior staged a fake assassination and funeral, letting the world believe he was dead so he could leave with a new identity. The unrecognized mourner was the undercover agent himself, with a changed face. He had come to attend his own funeral and to thank the superior who had arranged the way out. The case of money was his pay for the mission, and the news of the death was his final protection.
hints: The assassination is only the story spread to the public, and the funeral was staged as well.
The man who finished the mission is an undercover agent whose old identity must disappear from the world.
The unrecognized mourner is the man himself, presumed dead with a changed face, thanking at his own funeral the superior who engineered his escape.

title: Before Breakfast
story: An old man living alone got up in the morning and died of poison before he could eat breakfast.Nothing wrong was found in his food or his drinking water.In the end, the police carried off one thing he still had on him.
answer: Every night the old man took out the dentures and soaked the dentures in the glass beside the bed, and every morning the old man put the dentures back in. The killer knew the habit, slipped into the old man’s room the night before, and left poison on the dentures. When the old man put the dentures in, the residue got into the old man’s mouth; the old man swallowed the residue with saliva, and the poison killed the old man. The old man had not yet eaten breakfast, so testing the food and the drinking water found no source. In the end it was on the dentures the old man was still wearing that the police found the poison residue.
hints: Something poisonous got into his mouth, but he never ate or drank it.
Every morning the old man puts back in something he took out for the night.
The killer left poison on his dentures; putting them in brought the residue into contact with his mouth, he swallowed it, and the poison took him.

title: The Spy Nurse
story: The badly wounded general made it back to camp but never walked out of the operating room alive.The nurse knew he was dead, yet she ran to the door and cried desperately for help, shouting the same words over and over.
answer: The nurse was a spy for the enemy. During the surgery the nurse killed the doctor and stalled the treatment until the badly wounded general died. Then the spy ran to the doorway calling for help, trying to make everyone believe the nurse had just fought off the doctor who was murdering the general. The nurse’s repeated shouting also carried a code phrase agreed on beforehand; the accomplices still hidden in the camp knew the moment the accomplices heard the phrase that the general was dead. The spy was building a cover story and delivering the report in one breath; even if the nurse was exposed and seized at once, the message had already reached the spy’s comrades.
hints: Among the people her cries are meant for is one who agreed on a code phrase with her beforehand.
The nurse is a spy who killed the doctor to stall the general’s treatment.
The words she keeps shouting work both as a call for help after a supposed struggle and as word to her accomplices that the general is dead.

title: Bringing a Blade to an Invitation
story: I bought a treasured sword, and when a powerful lord heard of it, he summoned me to bring it and show him.A servant led me into a great hall. I looked up, saw the four characters on the plaque, and knew it was already too late to walk away.The lord appeared, roaring for me to be bound: I had brought the sword, he said, to kill him.
answer: I am Lin Chong, from the classic Chinese novel Water Margin. Gao Qiu’s adopted son lusted after my wife, so Gao Qiu schemed to ruin me. Gao Qiu first had the treasured sword sold to me, then sent word for me to bring the sword to the residence to compare blades. The two ushers walked me into the Hall of the White Tiger, a restricted chamber where military affairs were weighed and no one might enter uninvited. Only when I saw the plaque did I realize something was wrong, and just as I turned to leave, Gao Qiu appeared, denied ever having summoned me, and accused me of entering armed to assassinate Gao Qiu. The fact that I had walked in with a sword became the evidence planted in advance, and in the end I was branded with the crime and exiled to Cangzhou.
hints: The story comes from a classic Chinese novel, and the lord and the ushers set the trap together.
I was lured into carrying a weapon into a military hall where no one may enter uninvited.
I am Lin Chong; the plaque reads Hall of the White Tiger, and Gao Qiu uses it to frame me for coming armed to kill him.

title: Come to Light
story: He hid me under the bed in the hotel room, picked up my phone, and copied my voice to tell my husband I was safe.I watched him perform and whispered softly in his ear: “Don’t be afraid. I will stay with you always.”A few days later, he came back with the police.
answer: He and I each had a family, and we were meeting secretly at the hotel. My lover had gambling debts, so he killed me, packed my body into a black bag and hid the body under the bed, then used my phone to transfer away my money and impersonated me, sending my family word that I was safe. My ghost never left him; day and night I kept whispering in his ear that I would stay with him always. He had staged the whole act to bury my death, but found there was no escaping the voice of the dead, and in the end the fear broke him: he turned himself in to the police and told them where the body was. When the officers lifted the bedboard they found me, and even after he was taken away, I still walked at his side.
hints: He uses my phone to impersonate me, hiding the fact that I can no longer tell my family I am safe myself.
He killed his secret lover for money and hid her body under the bed.
I am now the ghost who follows him, whispering until he turns himself in, and afterward I still do not leave him.

title: The Naked Man Outside Town
story: At first light, a man woke up naked on the outskirts of town with no memory of the night before.Following the tracks from the scene of a murder, the police found him and took him away.After they questioned him, they let him go.
answer: The man was a werewolf. On the night of a full moon the man turned into a wolf, and after returning to human form the man had no memory of anything from the time as a wolf. That night, after the change, the man attacked passersby, the man’s clothes were torn apart in the transformation, and at dawn the man woke naked. The police found victims mauled by a large wild beast and followed the wolf’s tracks to the spot where the man woke, which put the man under suspicion. But the man’s human body had no claws, and there was nothing to prove the man had done the killing himself. The police did not know werewolves existed, so they never linked the two forms; all they could do was let the man in front of them go.
hints: The wounds and tracks at the murder scene look like the work of a large wild beast.
He turns into a werewolf on full-moon nights and keeps no memory of it once he is human again.
The police find him in human form but, not knowing the rules of the change, cannot prove he is the attacker who left the wolf tracks.

title: Pride
story: I looked at my father’s head hanging on the wall, then at the body on the floor. This day had finally come. At this moment, surely he must be proud of me.
answer: I am a deer. My father was killed by a hunter and made into a trophy, my father's head mounted on the wall. I found that hunter and killed the hunter with my antlers; the body on the floor is the hunter's. I have avenged my father, and at this moment, my father must be proud of me.
hints: The head on the wall is a hunting trophy left by a hunter.
