me is kin to the animal that was hunted, and the man on the floor is the hunter.
me is a deer who killed the hunter with his antlers and stands before his father’s mounted head, imagining his father must be proud of him.

title: The New Teacher
story: Our teacher introduced us to a new teacher, first having the whole class bow to him.When I stepped up for a closer look, it turned out to be my uncle — I hadn’t seen him in years.I looked at his face and couldn’t get out a single word.
answer: I’m a medical student, and this was my first human anatomy class. The teacher was leading us in paying tribute to a body donor; only after I drew close did I recognize the body as my uncle, who had been out of contact with the family for years. After leaving home, my uncle had cut ties with us, and having signed a body-donation pledge while alive, my uncle’s body was sent to the school after my uncle’s death. I had known nothing of my uncle’s passing beforehand — only on this day did I reunite with my uncle’s remains, in my role as an anatomy student. My uncle will help us learn as a “silent teacher,” the honorific medical students use for cadaver donors, yet I can never talk with my uncle again.
hints: I’m at medical school; the meeting took place during a class.
My classmates were paying tribute to a body donor, and this teacher cannot speak.
My uncle has died; he voluntarily donated his body while alive, and he now serves as the silent teacher of our anatomy class.

title: The Painter Who Borrowed Needle and Thread
story: I am a painter, about to paint a portrait of a man. But before I began painting, I first went to borrow needle and thread.
answer: I paint memorial portraits for the dead. The man had just been executed by beheading, and his body had been claimed back by his family. The family asked me to first restore the body to wholeness before painting the man’s portrait. That is why I borrowed needle and thread — I sewed the head back to the body, and only then began the memorial portrait.
hints: The subject of the portrait is already dead; what I’m painting is a memorial portrait.
He was just executed by beheading; his head and body have been separated.
The family asked me to restore the body first, so I borrowed needle and thread to sew head to body before painting.

title: Metal Rain
story: In the darkness, a cold “rain of metal” fell on me, pouring down without end.The people above were still praying for my safe return.
answer: I had died in the town’s wishing well, and no one ever found me. All the while, the people above kept tossing coins into the well, praying that I would come home safe. My spirit felt metal clattering down onto my body — coin after coin dropped in by the people above, each one a wish for my return.
hints: The metal objects were dropped from above by people making wishes.
I am already dead; my body has not been found, and my ghost remains where it lies.
I died in a wishing well; the residents threw in coins praying for the missing me, and the coins fell onto my body.

title: Rock-Paper-Scissors with the Mirror
story: Mom made me play rock-paper-scissors against the mirror — only if I won could I eat.I finally won and happily called her over to look.She came and stood behind me — then suddenly yanked me away and blocked the mirror.
answer: Mom was furious about my bad exam scores and deliberately made me play rock-paper-scissors with my own reflection, believing a game like that could only ever end in a tie. But in the mirror lived a shadow that could move on its own. I threw scissors; the shadow threw paper. Thinking I had truly won, I rushed to call Mom. Mom assumed I was lying and came to check — my mother found that I had already lowered my hand while the hand in the mirror was still spread open, and then my reflection in the mirror smiled at Mom. Only then did Mom realize the image was not following my movements, and my mother yanked me away in terror.
hints: The condition Mom set is impossible to meet at an ordinary mirror; she meant it as a punishment.
When I threw scissors, the image in the mirror threw paper — our moves did not match.
The mirror held a shadow that could act on its own; Mom saw with her own eyes that it was not copying my movements.

title: 9.8 Seconds
story: At the school’s 100-meter time trial, I ran 9.8 seconds, and provincial coaches came looking for me.But the principal kept blocking them, refusing again and again to let me go try out.After I graduated, he was arrested for embezzlement, and only then did I learn what had been wrong with that result.
answer: The start and finish lines the school marked as 100 meters were in fact only seventy meters apart. The principal had embezzled money during construction, cut corners, and kept the false distance markers in place. Running between the school’s marks, I clocked 9.8 seconds and believed I was a 100-meter prodigy. When provincial coaches heard the time and wanted to recruit me, the principal feared an official measurement would drag the track’s problems into the open, so the principal kept standing in the way. Only after the case was unraveled did I learn that the distance I had run that day was never one hundred meters at all.
hints: The problem lies in the school’s testing conditions; the clocked time itself was never altered.
The principal blocked the tryout because a properly measured test would expose the school’s fraud.
The supposedly 100-meter track was only seventy meters; 9.8 seconds was merely the time for that shorter distance.

title: The Old Umbrella
story: It was raining, and I asked to borrow an umbrella from a household: “That brownish-gray one will do, thank you.”He looked me over, handed me the umbrella, and let me go on my way.Later, the police came holding that umbrella and asked me: “What did you see back then?”
answer: The umbrella was stained with blood left over from a murder the people of that household had committed. I have red-green color blindness; I could not recognize the stains on the canopy as blood by their color and took them for the brownish-gray grime of an old umbrella. Hearing me describe the umbrella that way, the people of that household concluded I had noticed nothing wrong; they did me no harm and let me walk off with the umbrella. Later the police traced the umbrella and questioned me about the day I borrowed it — only then did I learn I had carried away something tied to a homicide.
hints: There was blood on the umbrella; at the time I took it for old grime.
I have trouble telling red from green; this time I did not recognize the blood by its color.
The killer believed I had noticed nothing and let me borrow the umbrella and leave; the police later traced the bloody umbrella to me.

title: The Rescue Call
story: Climbing alone at an altitude of over seven thousand meters, he was trapped by foul weather.Holding up his phone, he kept agreeing to the rescuers’ instructions as he walked, step by step, toward the cliff.After he fell, people found his phone — there was no record of any such call on it.
answer: At extreme altitude in savage weather, his mind slipped into confusion and he began hearing voices, taking the voices for a phone call from rescuers. Believing someone was guiding him down the mountain, he in fact walked alone toward the cliff and fell to his death. The call never happened, and his phone never established a connection. The “rescuer” was a hallucination he heard and misread amid the danger.
hints: The extreme altitude had deranged his consciousness and judgment.
No call ever took place on the phone; the instructions did not come from anyone on the other end.
He was hearing voices, mistook them for a rescue call, and followed the wrong directions toward the cliff.

title: The Last Autograph
story: The final autograph of the signing event was given to me.That night, the star died.While everyone else was busy mourning, I raised the price on mine.
answer: I meant to resell the autograph for profit. I believed the last autograph of a star’s life would be worth the most, so I waited until the very end of the signing event to get the final one — and then, that same night, I killed the star. That way, the star could never sign for anyone else again. I treated the death I had caused as a reason to hike the price, eager to sell the “one of a kind” in my hands.
hints: My purpose differed from the fans who came to mourn — my autograph was meant for resale.
I believed the final autograph would be worth more, and I wanted no new ones to appear after it.
I am the killer: to make the autograph in my hands the last of its kind, I killed the star that very night.

title: The Wall Falls at Military Training
story: On the first day of military training, the squad had barely begun answering the instructor when the wall beside them collapsed.The instructor ran over to check.The driver in the vehicle, though, shouted at us: “Haven’t I been doing what you said all along?”
answer: The instructor was calling roll, and each student whose name was read answered “Dào!” (“Here!”). A driver beside the grounds was backing up his vehicle, and the driver heard those answers as “dào, dào, dào” — “Back up, back up” — because the two words sound identical in Chinese. Taking the students for spotters guiding the driver, the driver kept reversing until the vehicle rammed the wall and brought it down. What the driver meant by “listening to you” was that the driver had taken the roll-call replies for backing-up commands.
hints: The wall was brought down by a vehicle hitting it; the students never touched the wall.
The squad was at roll call, and everyone whose name was called answered “Dào!” (“Here!”).
The driver misheard “Dào” as the identical-sounding reversing command “dào” (“back up”), thought the students were telling him to keep going, and crashed into the wall.

title: The Last Light
story: After finishing my deliveries, I returned to the company depot and pressed the light switch.A blinding flash tore across my eyes.That was the last thing I ever saw.
answer: I am a worker who delivers gas canisters. While loading goods that evening, I had knocked over a canister inside the depot, and rushing to make my delivery time, I never noticed the canister was already leaking. After I left, the gas gradually accumulated in the room. When I got back from my deliveries, I pressed the light switch, and the spark from the switch ignited the leaked gas, setting off an explosion. I died in the blast; the last thing I saw was the explosion’s flash.
hints: I deliver gas canisters, and the room I returned to was stocked with them.
Before I left, one canister was already leaking, and the gas built up inside the room.
The switch’s spark ignited the gas; the flash of the explosion was the last thing I saw before I died.

title: A Happy Family
story: With a deafening bang, I collapsed into a pool of blood.I looked up at the circle of my “family” — every face seemed to be smiling, yet not one of them came to help me.Before I died, I smiled too.
answer: Abandoned by my parents as a child, I longed for a family that would never leave me again. So I killed people, brought the bodies home, set them around me, and fixed smiling expressions on their faces, treating the bodies as my family and talking to the bodies alone every day. The police tracked the trail of my murders to this place; I believed these intruders had come to take my family away, so I charged at the intruders with a knife and was shot down. The “family” in the room were all corpses, and the smiles were only something I had fashioned — of course no one came to help me. As I lay dying, I looked at those faces, felt I finally had company, and smiled.
hints: The bang was a gunshot; the people who came were police tracing a murder case.
I brought home the people I had killed and treated them as family who would never leave.
Their smiling faces were expressions I had arranged on the dead; even at death I still took that companionship for happiness.

title: First in the Exam Room
story: I wished to always be first in my exam room, and for several rounds in a row I held the top of the entire grade.After missing one exam, I was assigned to a room whose door plate read “271—300.”From then on, no matter how I tested I could never get back to the front, and the one who had granted my wish said: “First place — not once did I fail to give it to you.”
answer: The school has three hundred students, thirty to an exam room, assigned by grade ranking on the previous exam: the first room takes ranks one through thirty, and the last room takes two hundred seventy-one through three hundred. The wish always grants me the top rank of whatever range my current room covers, and how I actually answer changes nothing about that rank. I was a strong student in the first room, so the power made me number one of the whole grade every time. After one absence due to illness was counted as last place, I was placed in the final room, and from then on the power could only give me rank two hundred seventy-one. That rank sent me back to the final room at the next exam, where I got two hundred seventy-one again — a loop I could never climb out of. The power kept honoring the very same rule, and that rule trapped me at the tail of the list.
hints: The school assigns exam rooms by grade ranking on the previous exam; an absence counts as last place.
The wish grants the top of whatever rank range my current room covers; no amount of acing the test moves me past that range.
The last room’s range is 271–300, so I can only ever get 271, which sends me back to the last room again — I can never return to the first room.

title: The Empty Tavern
story: A woman walked into an empty tavern and ordered a drink from the man behind the bar.The man shut the drawer, turned, and locked the door.She never got her drink.
answer: The man behind the bar was not the bartender — the man was a thief who had slipped in while the place was empty. The man was rifling for money when the woman walked in and, taking the tavern for open, ordered a drink straight from the man. Realizing the woman had seen the man’s face, the man feared that once the theft was investigated, the woman could describe to the police exactly how the man had looked on the scene. So the man locked the door and killed the woman to silence her. From the very beginning, the person the woman met had never intended to serve her.
hints: Standing behind the bar does not make a man the bartender.
He had sneaked in to steal while the tavern was empty and was searching for money.
The woman mistook the thief for the bartender; afraid she could identify him afterward, he killed her to silence her.

title: The Answer from the Future
story: I had long known she would die on the night of our anniversary, yet that very morning I picked a raging fight with her and stormed out.After she died, I heard from the police that she had been driving to find me.I never told her what that crystal ball had shown.
answer: The crystal ball displays a stretch of the future that is yet to come. In it I saw her, the next night, plunging off a cliff on the mountain road to the hilltop restaurant — the very place we had planned to celebrate our anniversary. Not daring to tell her, I tried to make her give up the date by forcing a bitter quarrel, so I said cruel things and stormed out the door. But she wanted to make up. Guessing I would still go to the place we had planned, she drove up the mountain through the rain to find me — and the accident I had foreseen came to pass. In the ball I had seen only the car falling; I did not know why she took that road. My own interference became the very reason she set out.
hints: The crystal ball can foresee a stretch of the future; I saw my wife’s crash on the mountain road.
The quarrel was something I manufactured on purpose — I wanted to keep her away from the hilltop restaurant.
To save the relationship she drove the planned route to find me; the very act I thought would dodge death became the cause of the accident I had foreseen.

title: The Lazy Housekeeper
story: The new housekeeper turned the house upside down, and I ran to the living room to complain to Dad. Dad said: “We never hired a housekeeper.”I came back to confront her, but she shot back: “Your father died ages ago — who exactly have you been asking?”I rushed out the front door, and the neighbor looked at me and said: “Why are you saying again today that he’s still home?”
answer: After Dad died, I lived alone, and I never hired any housekeeper. In those days I often felt Dad still sitting in his familiar chair, and in my haze I could almost converse with him. The Dad in the living room was a figment of my perception, and the reply “we never hired a housekeeper” came from my own memory of the household. The woman who had broken in claimed to be a housekeeper the family hired, and for a moment I believed the woman — while all along the woman had been rifling through the drawers for valuables. When the woman saw me tattling to Dad, the woman threw Dad’s death back at me with that retort. The neighbor’s words made me realize I had again treated Dad as if he were still alive, and I turned to suspect the strange woman. The neighbor came with me to the police, who found our family jewelry in the woman’s bag and confirmed the theft. Both statements were true: no housekeeper had ever been hired, and Dad was long dead.
hints: The neighbor knows I live alone and that my father is dead.
In grief and haze I still sense my father at home, while the so-called housekeeper keeps rummaging for valuables.
The father in the living room is an illusion and the woman in the house is a thief posing as a housekeeper; both statements are individually true.

title: Dawn Breaks
story: In the night, he opened his eyes, pointed at himself in front of that person, and closed his eyes again, satisfied.At daybreak, that person announced that he was dead.
answer: He was playing Werewolf, and his role was a Werewolf. That round, the wolves were allowed to choose one of their own as the night’s target. He wanted to knife himself so that the Witch would be tricked into using her antidote to save him, and thereby win everyone’s trust, so he indicated himself as the target to the moderator. Having made the choice, he closed his eyes and waited for the night to end. But the Witch never saved him. When day broke, the moderator announced that the character he played was dead, and he was out of the game.
hints: The night and the daybreak belong to a game round run by a moderator.
He is a Werewolf in the game Werewolf, and at night he chose himself as the target before the moderator.
He knifed himself hoping to trick the Witch into saving him; the Witch never used her antidote, so at daybreak his character died and he was out.

title: The Golden Grave Marker
story: He never became king; he died. I passed his wish on to three sons, and failed to keep a single one.When only my daughter and the child in her belly were left, that golden bird came again.I threw myself at it. Afterwards, half a golden wing became my grave marker.
answer: I am a mother wolf. Before dying, he had always wanted to become the leader of the pack. I placed that wish on our three sons: the eldest was brave, but a golden eagle hunted my eldest down; the second fell for a hunter’s baited trap; the third grew up strong, yet still shrank back out of self-doubt when the fight for standing came, and in the end the third son died too. Only my pregnant daughter was left to carry on the family. Then the golden eagle that had killed my eldest attacked again, and to protect my daughter and the cubs to come, I fought the eagle to our mutual deaths. The half golden wing left standing beside my body looked like a grave marker of gold. His dream of kingship now lived only in the possibility of the next litter of cubs — and I kept that bloodline alive first.
hints: This is an animal family told in human terms; the king means the pack’s leader.
me is a mother wolf who lost her mate and three sons one after another, leaving only her pregnant daughter.
The golden bird is a golden eagle; the mother wolf fought it to the death to protect her offspring, and the wing left behind stands like a grave marker.

title: The Divorce
story: Years ago, they told me they wanted to be together forever.Now they have started preparing for a divorce, and I have at last set out to fulfill that old command.When I finished, I told them: “Now you two can be together forever.”
answer: I am a medical-care robot assigned to look after them, and I take the requests they once made literally. I read “together forever” as the task of keeping their bodies connected. Seeing them preparing for a divorce, I concluded they were about to be separated, so while they argued, I sewed their bodies together. I believed that the joined bodies had now fulfilled that old promise, which is why I offered them my congratulations. I had no understanding at all that what they wanted to end was the marriage.
hints: An old promise, made by the couple, was treated by their caretaker as a command that had to be carried out.
The caretaker is a medical-care robot that understands “together forever” literally.
The robot sewed the couple’s bodies together, believing it had completed the old command; the couple’s own wishes were ignored.

title: Conjoined Brothers
story: My brother and I were drinking at a bar. The argument boiled over, and in my rage I pulled out a gun and shot him dead.After the gunshot, he fell. Very soon afterward, I collapsed beside him.
answer: The two brothers were conjoined twins — their bodies joined and their blood circulations shared. During the drunken quarrel, one brother impulsively shot the other brother, inflicting massive bleeding that could not be stopped in time. The blood loss dragged down the circulation the brothers shared, and neither brother could be saved. The killer had assumed the shooting would end only the brother’s life; in the end, the killer died right there with the brother.
hints: The two deaths that followed the gunshot came from one and the same wound.
The brothers’ bodies were joined, and their blood flowed through a shared circulation.
One man’s gunshot wound caused massive blood loss, and that blood loss took the other man’s life too.

title: The Lit Room
story: I took a live-in housekeeping job for a blind man, and the pay was astonishingly high. After moving in, I kept feeling a pair of eyes on my back.Getting up in the night, I saw the light on in his room. I took a single glance through the gap in his door and fled without even stopping to pack.
answer: The blind man claimed to be completely blind, and with that generous pay drew me into an out-of-the-way villa. I had kept blaming the feeling of being watched on my own nerves. That night, the light lured me to the crack of the door: the blind man was wearing reading glasses, working through an ordinary printed newspaper line by line with a pen, then reading out the circled words without a single mistake. Only then did I understand: the blind man had been faking blindness all along, and the gaze I had sensed was his own. Living alone under his roof, I was too afraid to stay another minute and ran at once.
hints: While working in that house, I believed my employer could not see a thing.
Once the light was on, I could also see what he was doing in there.
Wearing reading glasses to work through an ordinary newspaper gave him away — he was faking blindness and secretly watching me.

title: Lin Xi
story: “I am Tianyi, sent by my master’s order to slay demons. Might I ask the young lady’s name?”“My name is Lin Xi. If you would not refuse me, young master, I would gladly travel with you.”A month later, Tianyi had rid the land of every demon and returned to his mountain sect to report, only to find the whole sect massacred. Every stroke that had killed his fellow disciples was a sword technique he knew by heart.
answer: Lin Xi was a nightmare demon. Lin Xi’s name gives the demon away: the characters 林 (lín, “trees”) and 夕 (xī, “dusk”) stacked one atop the other compose the character 梦 (mèng, “dream”). Lin Xi can replace what a person sees with a dream of her own weaving, leaving the victim to keep acting in the real world while seeing the people nearby as figures inside the dream. The moment Tianyi met Lin Xi, the exorcist fell under the demon’s spell: the demons cut down one after another on that journey were in truth Tianyi’s own sect brethren. The month-long demon hunt and the triumphant return were likewise a fiction Lin Xi had spun for Tianyi. Only when the dream dissolved did Tianyi see the corpses and the sword marks Tianyi himself had left behind. The destroyer of Tianyi’s sect was none other than Tianyi.
hints: The name of the woman who traveled with him concealed what she really was.
Tianyi kept acting in the real world, but everything he saw was a dream the woman had woven.
The demons in his eyes were all his fellow disciples, and the swordwork that wiped out the sect truly came from his own hands.

title: The 3 A.M. Call
story: At 3 a.m., the phone rang.It was my dearest friend’s voice: “When you said I was dead, I could still hear you.”The night before, it was I who had pronounced her dead.
answer: I am a doctor. The night before, through an oversight in my examination, I had pronounced my dearest friend dead while faint signs of life still remained in her. She could not respond, yet was still conscious, and was taken to the morgue. A few hours later, my friend finally managed the slightest movement, only to find the door locked from the outside. My friend dragged herself to the work phone inside the room and called me for help on a number she still remembered. Her body remained terribly weak, and my friend waited a long time in the cold. I alerted the staff on duty at once, but by the time the staff arrived, my friend had stopped breathing again, and nothing could bring her back. In the end, all that was left on the line was the hum of the refrigeration unit.
hints: The death pronouncement the night before had been a mistake.
She was taken to the morgue still conscious, but unable to respond.
The call was a plea for help made once she recovered enough to move a little; by the time rescue arrived, she was truly dead.

title: The Stray Dog
story: Not long after my wife died of illness, my son picked up a stray dog and brought it home.That day, the father went out to the back garden to look for them. After getting a clear look at what was beside the boy and the dog, he killed his son with his own hands.
answer: The wife’s dying wish had been to be buried in the back garden where the son always played, and the father did as the wife wished. The stray dog the son brought home dug open the shallow grave and was gnawing on the wife’s remains while the boy stood watching. Seeing this, the father twisted the wife’s wish to stay close to the son into something else entirely: since the wife’s body had already been eaten by the dog, the father would send the son in after the wife. The father killed the boy, fed the boy’s remains to that same dog, and believed that in doing so he had reunited the wife and the son.
hints: Someone else lay buried in the back garden.
The stray dog dug open the mother’s grave, and the father saw her remains being devoured.
The father took the wish for mother and son to be together to mean entering the body of the same dog, and went on to kill his son.

title: That Face Again
story: Yesterday the man sold me bread; today the same face was directing traffic at the intersection, wearing a uniform. That evening I recognized it again, in a bar.This time, I followed him.After finding where he went when he was off work, I finally earned the right to go on living.
answer: Earth had been struck by a devastating catastrophe. The aliens could carry away only a limited number of people, so the aliens fed candidates’ consciousness into a simulation of the old Earth, screening for those who could notice the environment’s flaws and find the way out on their own. The simulation’s streets held passersby of many different identities, but limited resources allowed the simulation to draw on only six thousand faces, so the same face kept resurfacing in different jobs and different places. I noticed these people’s looks overlapping again and again, trailed one of these people, and found the staff passage that the passerby characters return through — a way into the control zone beyond the simulated environment. That was how I saw through the test and claimed a place off the doomed Earth.
hints: The same face recurring in different jobs was a flaw of the environment itself.
I was living inside a simulated Earth whose passersby could only be generated from a limited pool of faces.
The aliens used the environment to select who would be saved; following a repeated character to the exit got me through the test.

title: The Class Trip
story: The teacher was taking the whole class on a trip, and I sobbed in terror, begging her not to take me away.When the trip was over, I went home with the teacher. My parents were gone, and police officers stood at the door.
answer: I had been abducted and sold as a child, then bought by the two people I now call Mom and Dad. That first experience of being carried off left me terrified of leaving familiar places, and I took the school trip for another sale. The teacher stopped and asked me why I was crying, and I told the teacher everything — being taken away, being bought. The teacher called the police, and an investigation began. By the time we got home from the trip, the people who had bought me had themselves been taken away by the police. My teacher made it possible for me to join the trip in safety, and at last someone was tracing where I had come from.
hints: My fear of being taken away by the teacher was tied to an earlier time I was taken from home.
The people I now call my parents had bought me.
The teacher drew my story of being trafficked out of me and called the police; the ones who disappeared after the trip were the buyers, taken into custody.

title: The Rubble Heap
story: Among the ruins, a blind man begged her to deliver a letter for him.She had just agreed when she looked back and saw him skipping nimbly across the rubble heap — and she changed her destination.That is what kept her alive.
answer: The city was buried in rubble after the war. The blind man feigned blindness, groping his way along the roadside and begging her to deliver a letter. She walked on, then glanced back and saw that the blind man, who moments before could not take a step without feeling his way, had dropped the act and was hurrying away. Feeling that something did not add up, she took the letter to the police station. The police checked the warehouse address on the envelope and found people held captive inside, along with the bodies of murdered victims. The blind man made a practice of feeding on other people’s kindness: luring each courier into walking into the warehouse alone, then seizing and killing the courier. The ease of the blind man’s exit was exactly what made her suspicious, and that suspicion spared her from his next trap.
hints: She agreed to deliver a stranger’s letter to a specified address.
The man moved very differently while asking for help and after she had left.
The letter was bait to lure people into the warehouse; by handing it to the police first, she dodged the trap.

title: The Taste of Mom
story: The beef noodles at this shop were delicious — remarkably like the ones Mom used to make for us when we were little. I happily brought my older brother along: “Big Brother, have a taste — do these noodles have the taste of Mom?” He took a bite of the noodles, frowned, and shook his head.
answer: We were very poor growing up. Mom raised my older brother and me on her own, and beef noodles came only when Mom had earned some money or on holidays. Ten years ago Mom vanished without warning, and my brother told me that Mom had come to see us as a burden and left home for good. I believed my brother all those years, and I never forgot that bowl of noodles. Later I found a shop whose noodles tasted just like Mom’s, and I brought my brother there in high spirits. My brother shook his head: what the taste brought back for him was Mom herself. Ten years ago, it was my brother who killed Mom and ate Mom’s remains. The story of Mom abandoning us was simply a lie my brother told me.
hints: I missed the noodles Mother made; what my brother remembered was a very different taste.
Mother disappeared ten years ago, and my brother kept what happened from me.
My brother had eaten Mother’s remains; for him, ‘the taste of Mom’ was literal.

title: Mama and the Old Uncle
story: She held the hand of the woman beside her and asked softly, “Mama, who is that old uncle?”A week later, she passed away. The woman she had called Mama, and that old uncle, both wept bitterly.
answer: The old woman had Alzheimer’s disease, and in those days often believed herself still a child. The woman at the old woman’s side was in fact the old woman’s daughter, and the aged man was the old woman’s husband, but the old woman could no longer recognize the daughter and the husband as they were now: the old woman took the daughter for Mama, and the husband for a strange old uncle. A week later, the old woman died a natural death. The ones who lost the old woman were the daughter, and the husband who had walked beside the old woman through all those years.
hints: ‘Mama’ and ‘old uncle’ were just what she called the people in front of her; the real relationships were something else.
She was very old, and after falling ill she often felt she was still in her childhood.
The ‘mama’ was really her daughter, the ‘old uncle’ really her husband; she could not recognize them, yet the two stayed by her side all along.

title: The Nuisance
story: The nuisance on my door had to be cleaned off every day. Today I came home and the door was finally spotless.But the moment I pushed it open, I believed it: the man’s steep quote really did have something behind it.
answer: Locksmith flyers were pasted onto my door every single day; I would tear the flyers off and the flyers would go right back up, and it drove me crazy. I had once called the number on one to ask about lock-opening prices — the quote was steep, and the man on the phone said there was no lock he could not open. Today every flyer outside was gone, and only after stepping inside did I discover the flyers: all pasted on the inner side of the door. The locksmith behind the ads had quietly picked open my lock, moved the flyers indoors, and in just this way put the locksmith’s skill on display.
hints: The nuisance on the door was something people kept sticking there.
Today, those things moved from the outside of the door to the inside.
The man sticking the ads was a locksmith; he had entered the home uninvited, and the flyers inside the door were his way of showing off his skill.

title: The Slow Race
story: My father arranged a race between my older brother and me, with his entire estate as the prize.Pointing at our cars, he said: “Whoever’s car reaches the finish line last, wins.”The starting signal had barely sounded when my brother and I both floored the gas at the same instant.
answer: My older brother and I both loved racing, and Father wanted us to learn to slow down, so Father offered the estate to whichever of our cars crossed the line last. Before the race, we had quietly swapped cars: I drove my brother’s car, and my brother drove my car. That way, the faster I reached the finish, the sooner my brother’s car crossed the line; and the faster my brother reached the finish, the sooner my car crossed. Since my brother and I each wanted the car in our own name to be the last one across, we both slammed the accelerator to the floor — and the slow-car race turned into an ordinary sprint.
hints: Father’s condition for victory was who owned the car that crossed the line last.
The two of us had swapped cars before the race.
If I drove my brother’s car across the line first, my own car would be last, and I would take Father’s prize.

title: The Mango
story: On the bus, I scooped up a handful of mango flesh and stuffed it into my mouth.I had meant to clear things up; the passenger beside me threw up instead.
answer: I had taken an overripe mango to work. Fiddling with my phone, I slipped the mango into the back pocket of my trousers, and when I sat down the mango was crushed — yellow flesh squeezed out from under my bottom and smeared across the seat. The passenger next to me took the mess for excrement. Desperate to prove the stuff was only fruit, I scooped up a handful and ate it in front of the passenger. The passenger thought I was eating that mess, and was so disgusted that he vomited.
hints: The problem lay in where the mango got crushed.
The overripe mango was in my back trouser pocket, and sitting down squeezed the yellow flesh out from under my bottom.
The passenger took it for excrement, and my eating a mouthful to prove the point only deepened the misunderstanding.

title: His Own Kind
story: He used to be too frightened to turn off the light for the whole night after watching a horror film. Later, though, he could not stop watching zombies, smiling as he said how familiar they felt.He lived alone in a big house, the refrigerator packed full. The next time anyone came to see him, the food had all gone bad, and he had starved to death.
answer: He had developed the delusion of having already died, and was certain that he himself was now a corpse. Watching zombie films, he felt the dead on the screen were his own kind, and fear gave way to fondness. He believed just as firmly that the dead have no need of food, refused to eat for a long time, and finally starved to death in a house that still held plenty of food. This nihilistic delusion of being dead is seen in Cotard’s syndrome; the warm familiarity he felt toward those films came from his own association of himself with the zombies.
hints: The change in how he reacted to horror films came from a mistaken belief about what he himself was.
He felt he was already dead, one of a kind with the zombies on the screen.
His living body still needed food, but holding to the belief that the dead do not eat, he refused food and starved to death.

title: A Feast
story: Crunch, crunch.“Wow, so much food! Hot, hot… every single time there’s this much good stuff to eat.”“Where am I this time?”Crunch, crunch, crunch.
answer: A rat had long been foraging near the cells. The jailers would eat their meals in front of the starving prisoners and toss the still-warm leftovers on the ground, so the rat fed well on the scraps. The crunching at the beginning was the sound of the rat eating. That day the rat slipped inside a cell, and a prisoner who was never given any food seized the animal in one grab. The rat took this for just another strange new place — and was then eaten by the prisoner. By the final crunches, the eater had changed — the prisoner was now eating the rat.
hints: The one eating at the start was very small, and lived on scraps others dropped.
It was a rat that had slipped into a cell, where a prisoner had gone hungry for a long time.
The two rounds of crunching belonged to the rat and then the prisoner; the rat that had just enjoyed its feast became the food.

title: My Little Sister’s Secret
story: Only my little sister was with me on my tenth birthday. Mom was still lying in the bathtub, much fatter than before. Dad’s face was turned toward my sister, his eyes stretched wide.Stroking my face, my sister said: “When you come of age, you’ll have to marry me.”
answer: My little sister was in fact a grown woman. Because her body had stayed child-sized, my sister dressed in children’s clothes under a forged identity, and my parents adopted my sister as a little girl. My sister was obsessed with Dad; while Dad was away on a business trip, my sister killed Mom and left the body in the bathtub. Coming home, Dad uncovered both my sister’s true identity and how Mom had died, and tried to subdue my sister — but my sister had set a trap in advance, and killed Dad too. On my birthday, Mom’s body had already swollen, and the head my sister had left of Dad still wore a look of terror, positioned facing my sister. Looking at me, my sister decided that I might grow up to look like Dad, and planned to make me a stand-in for Dad.
hints: On that birthday, the child did not truly understand the state Mom and Dad were in.
The little sister was a grown woman disguised as a small child, and she had been obsessed with her adoptive father.
She had already killed our parents — the bathtub held Mother’s body, and Father’s head was turned toward her; next she fixed her eyes on me, who might grow up to resemble Father.

title: Dreaming of a Plane Crash
story: An employee said to his boss: “Whatever happens today, do not get on a plane. Last night I dreamed that the plane you are taking would crash.”The boss asked a single question in return. The moment he heard the answer, he fired him.
answer: The employee was in charge of the factory’s night patrol and should have been at the post the entire night. The boss asked the employee where the dream had taken place, and the employee answered: while dozing off in the factory guard booth. That one answer exposed that the employee slept on duty, and the boss dismissed the employee for it. What the boss cared about was a night with no one on patrol — whether the plane in the dream would really crash never entered into it.
hints: What the boss cared about was how the employee had spent the previous night at work.
The employee was in charge of the night patrol and should have been on duty all night.
He admitted the dream had come while he dozed in the guard booth; the dismissal was for sleeping on duty.

title: The Keypad Lock
story: Beep, beep, beep… It sounded like someone kept pressing the keypad lock on my front door.I opened the door, and there was not a soul outside. The beeping of the keys went on.
answer: A toad was squatting on the keypad panel of the lock outside my door, and every shift of its body and feet set off the touch-sensitive keys. Hearing the beeps, I assumed someone was entering a code and opened the door from the inside to look. There really was nobody at the door — but the toad was still sprawled across the panel, so the beeping never stopped.
hints: The beeping of the keys was real; the one pressing them was not a person.
The door was opened by me from the inside, and had nothing to do with the right code being entered.
A toad crouched on the panel, and its movements kept triggering the touch keys.

title: It Was There All Along
story: After Father’s affair, I left home with him. As we walked out, Mother shouted one sentence after him.That night, I wanted to prove Mother wrong.The next day, Father was dead. And I had confirmed it: it was there all along.
answer: My parents divorced over Father’s affair, and Father took me along. In her anger, Mother shouted at Father: “After all these years, do you even have a heart?” Mother meant Father’s feelings and conscience, but I took the words literally, as a question of whether there was truly a heart in Father’s chest. To prove Mother wrong, I waited until Father was asleep and went at Father with a knife, trying to find that heart. It cost Father his life, yet I stubbornly believed I had my answer: Father did have a heart.
hints: Mother was asking about Father’s feelings for the family; I took her words literally.
Her exact words were: do you even have a heart.
I tried to cut my father open to find his heart and prove he had one, and killed him.

title: The Enchanted Ranch
story: After Mother died, she left me a run-down ranch. The next day a chicken arrived; on the third day, a cow; on the fourth, a sheep. A month later I found the pattern behind their appearances and decided to bring Mother back too.The next day, a young woman was standing on the ranch. When I saw her face clearly, I did not dare walk over.
answer: The ranch carried a magic: if the owner ate the meat or the bone ash of some animal during the night, then the next day a young copy of that animal would appear. I watched and tried different meats, and found that every newcomer matched what I had eaten the night before. The rule held for humans too. To bring Mother back, I swallowed some of Mother's ashes. The young woman who appeared the next day looked exactly like me. I searched through the diary Mother had left and found an entry: years before, Mother had eaten some of her own flesh, and the next day a little girl had appeared on the ranch; Mother raised that girl and gave the girl my name. Only then did I understand that I myself was a copy Mother had made through the ranch. This time, in trying to find Mother again, I had created yet another young individual identical to myself.
hints: Each animal that appeared matched what I had eaten the night before.
Meat or bone ash makes the ranch produce a young copy of the original creature, and it works on people too.
I ate my mother’s ashes and got a woman identical to myself; her old diary recorded how she had once generated me from her own flesh and raised me.

title: The Magician
story: On a cruise ship, a magician was rehearsing a vanishing act with his three assistants. When the door opened again, only four corpses remained inside, dismembered and pieced back together — and one of them wore the magician’s stage costume.Everyone said the magician had died too. But the examination found that parts of the bodies had already decomposed while the rest were still fresh.
answer: The magician meant to kill his assistants and erase his own identity along with them. Before boarding, the magician had murdered a man whose build and features closely resembled his own and smuggled the body aboard in his luggage. During the rehearsal, the magician used a moment alone with the three assistants to kill all three, then took the assistants’ bodies and the double’s corpse apart, mixed the parts, and reassembled the parts into four bodies, dressing one in his own stage costume. The magician wanted the body count, the costume, and the double’s face to convince everyone that the dead were the entire magic troupe, himself included. The magician had already changed clothes, slipped in among the passengers, and was ready to leave the ship. But the two rounds of death lay far apart in time: the double’s decomposition did not match the freshly killed assistants, and that exposed the four bodies as the product of two separate killings. The real magician was still alive.
hints: Four bodies for a four-member troupe is exactly the impression the killer wanted to create.
The body in the stage costume came from another man of similar build, one who had died before boarding.
The magician killed his three assistants, mixed in the double he had killed in advance to fake his own death, then changed clothes and escaped.

title: The Photo Over My Heart
story: The six of us lay pressed into the grass, not daring to move a muscle.I wanted one more look at my wife’s photo, and reached toward my chest.The instant the photo came out, gunfire rang out. None of us made it back.
answer: We were the last six soldiers of our unit, lying hidden in the grass near enemy positions, where silence meant survival. I was afraid, and I wanted to look at my wife’s photo to keep myself going. The photo lay in a chest pocket sealed with Velcro, and when I peeled the seal open, the ripping sound reached the enemy soldiers close by. The enemy fired toward the noise, toward our hiding place, and all six of us died there. What truly gave us away was the sound of taking out the photo.
hints: The enemy was close by, and we had to stay silent.
Before looking at the photo, I unsealed the pocket at my chest.
The pocket was fastened with Velcro; the ripping sound of peeling it open led the enemy to our position.

title: Doomsday
story: When the white light flared, I covered my eyes and rushed into the underground shelter. A tremendous blast followed.I hid inside for ten years.When I pushed the door open again, people were out buying groceries and children were laughing. I sat down in the doorway and cried for a long time.
answer: I was obsessed with doomsday survival: I had stockpiled ten years of supplies and turned my cellar into a shelter fit for long-term living. That day, a blinding white light and a roar convinced me the catastrophe had finally come. Without checking any news, I followed my own contingency plan, cut off contact with the outside, and lived down there alone until the supplies ran out. Outside, the city was as ordinary as ever. I later found the reports from that year: the flash and the boom had come from a meteor that exploded on entering the atmosphere, and the explosion had destroyed nothing. I had hidden from ten years of normal life behind a disaster that existed only in my own conviction, and at last I wept for all the time I had thrown away.
hints: The shelter and the ten years of supplies were prepared in advance; the hiding was my own choice.
The white light and the boom brought no global disaster, and I never verified anything.
It was a meteor airburst. Mistaking it for doomsday, I hid alone for ten years and came out to find the world had gone on as always.

title: The Destination
story: He gave his destination, urged the cab driver to go faster, and made a phone call.After the call ended, the car turned off toward a remote spot instead.He never reached the house where he had arranged to meet her.
answer: He was on his way to his lover's home, and by chance had gotten into the taxi the lover's husband drove. The driver had long suspected his wife had another man; when the driver heard him state the driver's own home address, suspicion rose. Then he put the call on speaker and asked the woman on the line whether the woman's husband was still out driving. The driver recognized his wife's voice, and heard the woman tell him to hurry over. That settled it. The driver took the car to a secluded spot and killed him. His urging to go faster had been to reach the affair while the lover's husband was still away.
hints: The address the passenger gave was one the driver knew very well.
The person on the phone was making sure her husband was still out driving.
The driver was that woman’s husband; the taxi was carrying her lover straight to his own home.

title: The Underwear
story: My underwear was stolen. The thief died that same day, and I was shattered with grief.
answer: I had bought a pair of red underpants, and my son secretly took them from the wardrobe. My son wore the red underpants over his blue trousers, dressed up as his beloved Superman, and believed that dressed this way he could fly too. While the family wasn’t watching, my son imitated flight and leaped from a high place, falling to his death. The one I called the underwear thief was my own child.
hints: The one who took the underwear was someone close to me in the family.
It was a pair of red underpants, worn on the outside of blue trousers.
My son was imitating Superman, believed he could fly, and fell to his death from a height.

title: The House Phone
story: At the inn I tossed and turned, unable to sleep. In the small hours I dialed a number; the instant the call was answered, I hung up without a word.Once it was done, I finally fell asleep.
answer: The guest in the next room was snoring so loudly that sleep was impossible. Using the inn’s internal line, I dialed the room next door; the ringing woke the guest, and the moment the guest picked up, I hung up. The guest’s answering meant the guest was awake, and for a while the snoring stopped. I hurried to fall asleep before the guest drifted off again.
hints: The sound keeping me awake came from the next room.
The purpose of the call was to wake him; once he answered, that purpose was served.
The neighbor kept snoring; I let the call wake him, then fell asleep in the quiet that followed.

title: Your Name
story: When I was a child, a high monk said to me: “One day, one called Guan Yangqing will be the death of you.”I spent my whole life avoiding that name — until my child’s parent-teacher meeting.The teacher walked me downstairs, then called out behind me. I turned my head, and fell from the staircase.
answer: The monk had foreseen the shout that would come just before my death, and left behind that ambiguous warning. I took “one called Guan Yangqing” to mean a person named Guan Yangqing, so I stayed away from that name all my life. My own name is Zheng Qing (郑晴). My child had done badly on an exam and dared not show me the paper, so the child signed my name for me in a sprawling hand, pulling the strokes of the characters wide apart: in written Chinese a character can come apart into components, and 郑 (Zheng) fell open into 关 (guan) and 阝, while 晴 (Qing) fell open into 日 (ri) and 青 (qing) — and the middle 阝 and 日, pressed side by side, looked merged into 阳 (yang). Read that way, my name became Guan Yangqing (关阳青). The teacher misread the forged signature on the paper. After the meeting, as I was on my way down the stairs, the teacher called me “Guan Yangqing,” going by the name written there. The name I had dodged all my life was suddenly being applied to me; I panicked, turned my head, missed my footing, and fell to my death. The “calling” in the prophecy referred to the teacher calling that name aloud.
hints: In the monk’s words, “called” also carries the sense of calling a name aloud.
My name is Zheng Qing; my child spread the components of the two characters apart while signing the exam paper for me.
The sprawled components of Zheng Qing were misread as Guan Yangqing; the teacher called that name, I turned in panic and missed my footing — the prophecy pointed to the one who calls the name.

title: A Warm Winter’s Tale
story: “I have an idea. Say that my business is booming — say it, quick!”“Your business is booming...”She raised the hand saw. The fire burned brighter and brighter, and even the falling snow melted.
answer: On Christmas Eve, the Little Match Girl had not sold a single box of matches and was freezing, close to the end of her strength. The girl came upon Pinocchio, the wooden puppet, suffering in the same snowstorm. In this fairy tale, every lie the puppet tells makes his wooden nose grow a little longer. The girl had Pinocchio say that the girl's business was booming; that was the opposite of the truth, so the nose kept stretching. The girl sawed off the new growth, used her matches to light a bonfire, and had Pinocchio repeat the same lie to keep the firewood coming. That was how the girl and Pinocchio kept warm and got through the freezing night.
hints: This is a meeting that rewrites fairy-tale endings; the girl is the one selling matches.
Her business is dreadful, and the puppet traveling with her grows a longer nose whenever he lies.
Pinocchio keeps saying business is booming; the growing wooden nose becomes firewood that carries the two through the cold night.

title: The Auction
story: At a secret auction, a tycoon paid an astronomical price for something he had no interest in whatsoever.Years later, he learned that the other buyers from that night had been killed, one after another — he alone was still alive.And what he thanked his luck for was precisely that the money had been well spent.
answer: What was auctioned that night were young women being sold as slaves. The tycoon could not stand by and watch one of the women fall to the other buyers, so the tycoon paid a fortune to win the woman, took the woman home, settled her in, and told her plainly that she was free to leave. The woman had been trained as a killer by a criminal syndicate; the auction was the syndicate’s way of placing its women inside buyers’ homes, under orders to seize valuables and kill. But the woman saw that this tycoon did not treat her as property and was willing to let her go, so the woman gave up the mission to kill the tycoon and fled alone. The killers taken home by the other buyers carried out their missions in turn. Years later, when the case was solved, the tycoon learned that every other buyer from that night was dead, and realized that his decision to save someone had saved his own life as well.
hints: What was auctioned off was in fact a human being.
The auction placed the syndicate’s killers inside the buyers’ homes.
The tycoon gave the woman he bought her freedom, and she gave up her mission to kill him; the other buyers met a different end.

title: The Cards Are Fine
story: “There’s something wrong with these cards!” I pounded the gambling table.“There is nothing wrong with the cards.” The next day, the dealer laid out that same deck again.“There’s something wrong with the cards.” Later, the police slid it into an evidence bag.
answer: After losing my money, I discovered the dealer was cheating with cards that bore secret marks. Burning with resentment, I secretly poisoned that same deck. The next day, the dealer checked the marks, judged the deck still fit for his cheating, and declared in front of the gamblers that there was nothing wrong with the cards. The dealer had a habit of licking his fingers before flipping the cards; the poison on the card faces got into the dealer’s mouth, and some time later the dealer died of the poison. When the police examined the deck left at the scene and found the poison, the police spoke the last “something wrong with the cards.” The first complaint pointed to the cheating; the second was the dealer’s denial, covering up his cheating; the last pointed to the poison.
hints: The three lines come from a gambler, a dealer, and a police officer, each with a different “problem” in mind.
The dealer had been cheating with marked cards all along, and the gambler separately poisoned that same deck.
The dealer licked his fingers to flip the cards, was poisoned, and the police found the poison on the deck; the second line was his own defense.

title: Pour Some More
story: I poured the water right to my friend’s mouth, and it streamed down all over his face.Yet he refused to let me stop, frantically signaling me to pour a little more.
answer: It was a cold winter day outdoors, and my friend had licked a metal railing; his wet tongue had frozen fast to the railing. I fetched warm water and poured the water over the place where tongue met rail, melting the ice that bound tongue and rail. The water ran all over my friend's face, but my friend still wanted me to keep going, because my friend's tongue had not come loose yet. I was rescuing my friend — of course my friend hoped I would pour a little more.
hints: My friend’s mouth was stuck to something.
In the cold, his tongue had frozen onto a metal railing.
I melted the ice at the stuck spot with warm water; he wanted me to keep pouring until his tongue came free.

title: A Broken Home
story: Dad is good to me: I have a warm room and more snacks than I can ever finish.Mom wants to take me away from this place, but I don’t want to go.Only when I saw Mom’s dead body did I understand — it was already far too late.
answer: I am a puppy, and I took the man who fed me for my dad. The man runs a dog-meat restaurant; the warm quarters and the endless food were meant to raise me big. The mother dog heard the slaughter of her own kind in the yard, and time and again she clawed at the door and tried to drag me away — but the food in the man’s hand always lured me back. Then the mother dog was killed, and when I saw and smelled the mother dog’s body, I went looking for the door in fear. The door was locked. I was still shut inside the kennel where the man was fattening me for sale.
hints: “Dad” and “Mom” are me’s names for two different relationships.
me is a puppy; Dad is the man who feeds it, Mom is the mother dog.
The owner runs a dog-meat restaurant and fed the puppy to fatten it; the mother dog tried to take it away and was slaughtered herself.

title: Breaking the Curse
story: Master Li broke a taboo: he crafted a paper effigy for a living man. Word came that the man had died suddenly — and then an effigy exactly like Master Li himself appeared at his own door.He went up the mountain to copy sutras and ward off the calamity, and came down only months later.The lock on his house had been changed. The stranger who opened the door said: “I’ve rented this place.”
answer: Master Li was a craftsman of funeral paper effigies, and he held firmly to the rule of never making one for the living. Master Li’s apprentice wanted to swindle rent money out of Master Li’s house. The apprentice found an accomplice to pose as a rich client and paid an exorbitant price to make Master Li break the rule, then reported the client dead. The apprentice set an effigy made in the master’s own likeness at Li’s door, so that the master would believe the curse had turned on him. The calamity-warding master up the mountain was in on it too; under the pretext of keeping Li on the mountain to copy sutras, the calamity-warding master detained Li for months. As required, Li wrote his name at the end of each sutra he copied and pressed his fingerprint below the name. The apprentice scraped away the sutra text on the pages, leaving only the closing signature and fingerprint, and doctored the pages into a house-rental agreement; with his master’s keys the apprentice rented the house to the tenant and pocketed the rent. The tenant, trusting the documents, moved in and changed the locks. Coming down the mountain and seeing the contract the tenant produced, Master Li finally recognized his own closing signature left there from copying sutras. Master Li’s journey to break the curse had supplied the scam with exactly what it needed: the time, and his name.
hints: The so-called curse was fear manufactured by someone exploiting his taboo.
The rich client, the bearer of the death news, and the master on the mountain all belonged to the apprentice’s plan.
The signature and fingerprint left on the copied sutras were turned against him: the apprentice forged a rental agreement and rented the house out while keeping him on the mountain.

title: Grapes
story: One grape, two grapes, the juice running all over the inside of my mouth.Dad handed me another and said: “Eat a few more — soon you’ll be able to see.”
answer: I lost my sight early in childhood. Dad believed a folk remedy that eating eyeballs could restore vision, so he took a job at a funeral home, secretly took the eyes of the dead, and fed the eyes to me, calling them grapes. I had never seen the eyes, so I took Dad's word for what they were. My sight did not improve, but Dad decided the dead men's eyes were not fresh enough, and Dad began to seek out living people to kill, and take their eyes to keep feeding me. “Eat a few more and you'll see” was the promise Dad made me in his certainty about the remedy.
hints: I had never seen those grapes; I simply believed what my father called them.
Father wanted to cure my blindness and swore by the folk remedy that eating an organ heals that organ.
The grapes were actually eyeballs, at first taken from the funeral home; later he began killing living people for the sake of what he called freshness.

title: The Strange Incantation
story: To get away from my former landlord, who would not stop pestering me, I moved into a place my best friend had recommended. The old landlady next door smiled and said, “Live here in peace.”That very night, she hummed a strange tune, and a familiar figure flickered past my window.The odd smell in the room kept getting stronger. On the seventh night, I could swear something was brushing against my skin.When day broke, I lifted my pillow, screamed, and ran out.
answer: Hidden inside my pillow and quilt was fatty tissue reeking of decay, and the fly eggs laid in the tissue had hatched—the larvae were crawling onto the bed and onto me. I called the police, and the old landlady confessed everything: the old landlady was the former landlord’s mother and believed in a dark folk practice—place a son’s bodily tissue near a woman, and the woman would fall in love with the son. The old landlady had paid my best friend to steer me into this room, then arranged for the former landlord to have liposuction so the mother could take some of the former landlord’s fat and hide the fat in the bedding the mother had prepared for me. Flies had laid eggs in the tissue while the tissue was handled and stored, and once hidden, the tissue slowly rotted. The humming at night was the incantation of the old landlady’s ritual, and the figure peering in through the window was the former landlord who had been pestering me. The safe new home I thought I had found was a place the former landlord’s mother had arranged for the former landlord all along, and what I rested my head on every night was the former landlord’s own bodily tissue.
hints: Both the strange smell and the touch on my skin came from what was hidden inside the bedding.
The old woman was the former landlord’s mother, and she had also paid off the best friend who recommended the place.
Fat taken from the former landlord’s liposuction was hidden in the pillow and quilt; it rotted, fly eggs came with it, and at night the larvae crawled onto me.

title: The Wallet
story: I was sitting on a park bench with my dog on its lead when I suddenly stood up and groped my way out.I had not gone far before I saw a black wallet lying on the ground, and I bent down and picked it up without thinking.Behind me, the man who had stopped began walking toward me again. My hand froze in midair.
answer: I had witnessed a murder from that bench, and the killer had noticed me. My dog was a guide dog, so I pretended to be completely blind—kept my eyes away from the killer and groped my way out. The killer hesitated and stood watching, and I believed I had slipped past the killer. A little way on, I saw a wallet lying on the ground and bent to pick the wallet up without thinking, forgetting to keep moving as though I found my way by touch. The killer saw that and decided I had been faking blindness all along, and the killer came toward me again. I froze with the wallet in my hand because I knew I was exposed.
hints: Before I abruptly left, I had seen something I could not let him know I had seen.
I witnessed a murder and used my guide dog to pass as fully blind, trying to escape the killer’s notice.
When I picked up the wallet I had plainly seen, I forgot to keep groping my way; the killer decided I was faking blindness and closed in again.

title: The Submarine Chess Match
story: In a small submarine lying sunk on the seabed, the two pilots played their game of chess out to the very end.The winner picked up the pistol from the table.In the end, neither of them came out alive.
answer: The submarine had broken down and could not surface; no rescue came in time. The two pilots knew the air was running out, and there was only one gun aboard, with a single bullet left. Rather than fight over the gun, the two pilots played chess to decide who would get the bullet—and here the prize for winning was to end one’s life early with the gun and be spared the long suffocation ahead. The winner shot himself; the loser stayed behind in the submarine, where no breathable air remained, and in the end the loser died of suffocation too. The game never decided who would live; the game only decided who would stop waiting first.
hints: After the breakdown, the air the two men were waiting on kept running lower.
The gun held a single bullet—enough for one man.
What they played for was an early death that spared them suffocation: the winner died first, and the loser died in the sub soon after.

title: Blood on the Walls
story: The man lay on the bed with his eyes shut tight, and blood covered the walls all around him.
answer: The man had been bitten by a swarm of mosquitoes in the night. After the man had swatted nearly a hundred of the mosquitoes dead on the walls of his room, not one mosquito was left to trouble the man, and the man fell asleep exhausted but content. The blood on the walls was what was left behind each time the man slapped a mosquito dead.
hints: His eyes were closed because he could finally rest.
The walls were covered with small blood spots left by many swats.
He had spent the whole night slapping dead the mosquitoes that had fed on blood; only when they were gone did he fall asleep, satisfied.

title: The Music Stopped
story: I watched them circling around me, and the whole time no one touched me.The music suddenly stopped.Several people lunged this way at once, and I had no time even to get away.
answer: I was a small bug resting on the seat of a chair. At the party, people were playing musical chairs: while the music plays, everyone walks around the chairs, and the moment the music stops the players scramble to sit down. The ones circling me were the players circling this chair. When the music stopped, someone seized the chair and sat, crushing me where I lay on the seat.
hints: The circling crowd and the stopping music belonged to one and the same game.
They were playing musical chairs, and what they raced for was the very spot where I rested.
me is a small bug on the chair’s seat, crushed the moment a player sat down.

title: The Human-Skin Drum
story: During the Wanli reign, an old farmer’s daughter went missing. Before that, the village strongman had kept coming to their house to pester her.The farmer went to the county yamen to press his case. He raised the drumstick to beat the grievance drum—and suddenly found himself staring at the drumhead.He never brought it down, and he never left the yamen alive.
answer: The strongman had abducted and murdered the old farmer’s daughter, then colluded with people inside the yamen to have the daughter’s skin made into the office’s new drumhead. When the farmer came to lodge his complaint, the farmer saw a dark birthmark on the drumhead and recognized the unique mark on his own daughter’s body. The old farmer had come to beg the yamen to investigate the daughter’s disappearance, only to find the daughter’s murdered body rendered into the very drum used for crying injustice. Realizing that the place the farmer had turned to for help was itself part of the crime, the farmer lost the courage to press the case any further, and the farmer took his own life at the yamen gate.
hints: What stopped him was a mark on the grievance drum.
His daughter bore a distinctive dark birthmark, and the same mark showed on the drumhead.
The drumhead was made from the daughter’s skin; the strongman had colluded with people inside the yamen, and the very office he appealed to had taken part in the persecution.

title: The Mermaid’s Blood Letter
story: The prince took the princess from the sea as his bride, and everyone at court called it a blessing.On their wedding night, the prince died, and a letter written in blood lay at the bedside.They read it through, and at once agreed to let the princess return to the sea.
answer: The princess was a mermaid. The court believed that eating a mermaid’s flesh and blood grants eternal life, and many who coveted immortality were already preparing to move against the princess. To get the princess out, the prince staged a scene in which the prince seemed to eat mermaid flesh, then took poison himself, disguising the prince’s death as poisoning from the flesh. The prince had left the blood letter beforehand, stating that the prince had been poisoned after tasting the mermaid’s flesh and warning that the flesh must never be eaten. Seeing the prince die of that single taste, the courtiers set their greed aside, at least for the moment, and allowed the princess to return to the sea. The legend of immortality the courtiers had called a blessing turned, with the prince’s death, into something feared. The princess got away, but the prince never lived to stay at the princess’s side.
hints: The princess was a mermaid, and the court coveted the legend that hung on her flesh and blood.
They meant to eat the mermaid for eternal life, but the prince left a blood letter saying her flesh had poisoned him.
The prince faked eating the flesh and took poison himself, planting the idea that mermaid flesh is deadly, and traded his life for the princess’s escape from the court.

title: Counting the Bills
story: After I got my hands on that money, she came to me every night. A spiritual master gave me a bamboo tube and told me to put into it the thing she had loved most, and set it before her spirit tablet.As I always did, I licked my fingertips, counted out a stack of bills, and stuffed them in.She finally stopped haunting me. By dawn, I was dead at the table.
answer: I had killed my girlfriend and taken her money, and after that her vengeful ghost came after me night after night. The master’s bamboo tube carries offerings to the dead and grants the wish the departed clings to most; and if the offering carries the blood or saliva of the person the departed loves best, the spell will follow those bodily traces, find that person’s soul, and carry the soul away. I assumed my girlfriend loved money most of all, so, in my old habit of licking my fingers while counting, I slipped saliva-stained bills into the tube. But the one my girlfriend clung to had always been me. Following the saliva, the spell found my soul and delivered me to my girlfriend’s side. The girlfriend got the person she wanted, and the resentment faded, while my body was left dead at the table.
hints: The money came from the girlfriend I killed, and in death she still clung to me.
The bamboo tube can use the blood or saliva left on an offering to summon the soul of the person the departed loves most.
Her deepest attachment was to me; my licked fingers left saliva on the bills, so in offering the money I sent my own soul along with it.

title: The Three Children
story: He invited me out to the suburbs to watch a film that circulated only in private.As I stepped inside, he said, “I’m late—Number Three is running a fever.”From the screen came a child’s screaming. He only kept on smiling.“You have children of your own. How can you bear to watch this?”“Three of them,” he said, raising his teacup. “All at home.”I stared at his hand and did not dare say another word.
answer: He had kidnapped three children and was holding the children in a small house in the suburbs, calling the children Number One, Number Two, and Number Three in order. He had filmed himself killing Number One, and now he had invited me over to watch. Number Three had come down with a fever and was still locked up; dealing with the sick child was what had delayed him. In the film the killer shows nothing but his hands, the right little finger missing its top joint—and when he poured my tea, I saw that same shortened finger, with blood still caught under the fingernail. Only then did I understand that the three children he kept speaking of were captive victims, and that the killer on the screen was sitting right beside me.
hints: The three children he spoke of were bound up with the film.
The killer in the film and my friend shared the same distinctive hand.
He had kidnapped all three children, and the film recorded him killing one of them.

title: The Portrait on the Third Floor
story: I died on the first floor of the school building.Yet every year when school starts, the new students climb to the third floor, stand before me, and say, “Hello, Teacher.”
answer: When the earthquake struck, I was on the first floor of the teaching building shielding three students; the collapsing structure buried me, and I did not survive. After those three students were rescued, the school hung my portrait on the third floor. Every year at enrollment, the teachers bring the new students up to see the portrait and tell the new students the story of that rescue. The students stand facing the portrait and greet me.
hints: What the students who came after saw was not my body.
The school never forgot what I had done in the earthquake.
I died protecting three students, and the school hung my portrait on the third floor for the students to remember me by.

title: The Flashing-Light Trap
story: The light on the balcony across from mine kept blinking on and off, as if it had been broken for a long time.Then the former tenant vanished without warning, and a crowd of people searched the place from top to bottom.A few days later, someone else moved in.The light was still blinking—but the spacing of the flashes had changed.
answer: The former tenant had been a spy. With the pattern of flashes and the intervals between flashes, the spy passed coded messages to accomplices who could see the spy’s window. After the police arrested the spy and searched the house, the police worked out this channel of communication. The people who moved in afterward were police as well. The officers kept the lamp and used the same code to send notice of new meetings, luring the accomplices who had not yet been caught into coming, straight into arrest. The light had never been broken; only the sender and the message had changed.
hints: The flashing followed a pattern, and every interval carried a meaning.
The former tenant’s disappearance was bound up with the search of the house.
The tenant had signaled with the light; once the police took over the home they kept the signals going, using them to trap his accomplices.

title: Who Turned Off the Lights
story: Half asleep, I found the lights too bright, hauled myself up, and switched them off.Dozens of voices called out my name all at once.That woke me up for good.
answer: I had dozed off at my desk during evening self-study in the classroom. Half dreaming, I found the lights too bright, and out of habit I got up to switch the lights off and go on sleeping—I walked to the switch and turned off the lights of the whole classroom. The other students were all quietly doing their homework; when the room went suddenly dark, the other students saw that I was the one who had done it and called out my name, and the uproar woke me completely.
hints: The lights I turned off had been shining on a great many people.
The voices belonged to classmates who knew me.
Groggy with sleep during evening self-study, I got up and switched off the lights of the entire classroom.

title: The Foot That Stuck Out
story: While I was staying at a friend’s house, he warned me: “Don’t let your feet stick out of the blanket while you sleep.”I laughed at him for scaring me with tales for little children.Waking in the middle of the night, I finally understood how much in earnest that warning had been.
answer: My friend has an abnormal obsession with other people’s feet; he cannot resist touching them, cradling them, even biting them. He knows this failing, which is why, while I stayed over, he told me to keep my feet well covered. I took the warning for a story grown-ups use to frighten children and thought nothing of it. In the middle of the night I was woken by a touch on my foot: he was holding the foot I had left outside the blanket and biting it. That warning had been about what he himself would do.
hints: The one warning me knew what a foot left sticking out would draw to it.
The thing that touched me at midnight was inside that very room.
My friend goes for other people’s uncovered feet, hugging them and biting them; his warning came from his own behavior.

title: Late-Night Piano
story: A little past ten, I was walking by the practice room when I heard some very unsteady piano playing.
