The same passage went wrong twice, then fell silent for a long while.The next day, the famous pianist was found dead in that practice room.When he died, I had not yet reached the practice room door.
answer: A composer who worked behind the scenes for the orchestra had long had his works taken by the pianist and passed off as the pianist’s own. That night the composer caught the pianist stealing the composer’s new score, ready to publish the score under the pianist’s own name. The two fought, and the composer killed the pianist. Just then, my footsteps sounded from outside the door. The composer hid the body under the piano, sat down on the bench, and played, wanting me to believe the man in the practice room was still alive. The composer could play, but fresh from killing a man and terrified of being caught, his hands kept slipping. Afterwards the composer left the room. The playing I heard came from the murderer; the pianist was already dead by then.
hints: The death and the playing happened in the same room, but two different people did them.
The playing was meant for whoever was passing outside the door.
The killer hid the body and played the piano himself to cover up the death; his nerves made the playing falter again and again.

title: Three Birthdays
story: I am almost forty.Today they wished me a happy twenty-fifth birthday; tomorrow someone will celebrate my twenty-third; the day after, my twenty-fourth.I already have another name ready for tomorrow, when I go for cake.
answer: I work at a nursing home. Several residents with Alzheimer’s have mistaken me for their own sons and are living in memories of their sons’ younger years. Their families rarely visit, so I sit with the residents, talk over the old days, and celebrate the birthdays of the sons each resident remembers. Three days in a row, different residents wanted to celebrate their son’s birthday, at ages twenty-five, twenty-three, and twenty-four. I answer to whatever name each resident remembers, and accept each resident’s birthday wishes.
hints: Those ages belong to different people; the celebrants have mistaken me for them.
The celebrants are all elderly residents of the same facility.
Nursing home residents take a staff member for their own sons as they were in youth, and he celebrates each of their birthdays with them.

title: Birthday Applause
story: My friends threw me a birthday party.I blew out the candles and heard a burst of applause.Laughing, I said I wanted to hug them one by one.When the last one’s turn came, my hand found the cake knife.
answer: I was born blind. A year ago we were stranded in the wild and ran out of food. My friends proposed that each of us give up a hand and share the meat, so we could hold out until rescue came. I believed my friends and lost a hand; the others all kept both hands, simply lying to me that the others had done the same. After the rescue, my friends always touched me with only one hand, and I never suspected a thing. On my birthday night my friends forgot the lie and clapped without thinking. The sound made me doubt, but applause alone could prove nothing. Under cover of the hugs, I took hold of my friends’ wrists and felt both sides of each: every friend had two sound hands. I finally knew that back then, only I had been sacrificed. Then I picked up the cake knife and turned the knife on my friends.
hints: I cannot see them, and I once went through a deadly ordeal together with them.
We all claimed to have paid the same bodily price to stay alive.
I was made to lose a hand while their hands stayed whole; the applause planted my doubt, and the touch during the hugs proved the lie.

title: Go to Sleep
story: I am so sleepy I can barely keep my eyes open.That man stays beside me, saying gently, “Go to sleep.”Yet I fight with everything I have to stay awake. If I go on standing here, I will not last much longer.
answer: That man kidnapped me; he takes pleasure in tormenting people. He left me on a narrow plank suspended in the air, a rope around my neck. I must keep my balance to stay alive: the moment I fall asleep and lose my footing, I will drop and the rope will strangle me. He waits close by, deliberately urging me to sleep, waiting to watch me give out. I am desperately sleepy, but I do not dare let myself lose consciousness.
hints: I cannot sit or lie down; I must keep my balance.
The man keeping me company wants something dangerous to happen once I fall asleep.
I am trapped on a plank suspended in midair with a rope around my neck—doze off, slip, and it will strangle me.

title: Insomnia
story: After the divorce, I could never fall asleep.Last night I went to see him, and I slept straight through to dawn.When I opened my eyes, the sheets were soaked in red.
answer: During the marriage I was used to sleeping with my head on his arm, and after the divorce I could never adapt to sleeping alone. I went to see him, attacked him, cut off the arm I had always used as a pillow, and brought the arm home. That night I slept on the arm, and when I woke, the sheets had been soaked red with blood. I had my familiar feeling back; he was left gravely harmed.
hints: After seeing him again, I brought back something that used to help me sleep.
The red is blood, and it has to do with what I brought back.
I cut off my ex-husband’s arm and took it home to keep using as a pillow.

title: Separated
story: At a gas station, I keyed a stranger’s car.The owner grabbed me and insisted on calling the police.I turned my head and called out, “Daddy.”He looked at me, turned, and ran.Later, some strangers took me away—and that was how I finally got to go home.
answer: The person traveling with me was a child trafficker who made me pose as his daughter. I was afraid that if I simply cried for help, he would drag me away again, so at the gas station, while he was inside buying things, I scratched up a car outside the shop so that its owner would seize me and insist on calling the police. At the mention of the police, he feared the police would check our identities; he abandoned me and fled. Calling him “Daddy” kept my cover intact, since he could not very well announce in public that I had nothing to do with him. The strangers who came were police officers. I told the officers how I had been abducted, and with the officers’ help I finally reached my family.
hints: Keying the car was my way of making sure someone held me there and called the police.
The name I called that man came from the role he had ordered me to play.
He was a trafficker who fled rather than let the police find out who he was; the officers taking me away were saving me.

title: Disappointment
story: “You have disappointed me too deeply. I am never coming back.”I wrote the sentence over and over, and the wastebasket filled with crumpled paper.Not one sheet could be shown to anyone.And she can never correct my handwriting now.
answer: I had killed her and wanted to forge a letter in her hand, so that relatives, friends, and the police would believe she had simply given up on the marriage and left of her own accord. Using samples of her old writing, I practiced imitating her handwriting, writing that sentence again and again. Every attempt still showed differences, and I could not get the signature right. I crumpled up the failures and grew more frantic with every sheet. She was already dead, so I could never have her write, in her own hand, the letter meant to cover up the death.
hints: The crumpled sheets were practice for a letter meant to be shown to others.
I wanted people to believe that another person had left of her own accord.
I killed my wife and was practicing forging her departure letter, but I could not imitate her handwriting well enough.

title: The Twelve Zodiac Animals Go Abroad
story: The twelve of us had agreed to travel abroad together.Beep—cleared. One companion after another passed through security.When my turn came, the screen first read “camel,” then changed to “deer,” then spilled out a long list of names.An officer stopped me: “You may take only your own belongings out of the country.”I looked at my own body and wept.
answer: This is a fairy-tale world where animals can talk, and the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac were traveling together. I am the Dragon. The security scanner has no complete profile for a dragon, so the scanner judged me section by section against the animals the scanner did know: the scanner took my camel-like head, my deer-like antlers, my snake-like neck, and so on, deciding each part came from a different animal. The system thus reported that I was carrying body parts belonging to other creatures. The other eleven zodiac animals all passed identification, and the officer stopped me on the strength of that false report. I was carrying my own body, and the machine read my own body as a patchwork of foreign parts.
hints: The twelve companions correspond to a familiar set of animal names.
Several parts of my appearance resemble other animals.
I am the Dragon of the Chinese zodiac, and the scanner mistook my different body parts for parts belonging to other animals.

title: Ten Suns
story: Last night I told my brother, “Unless there are ten suns in the sky, I will never speak to you again.”Today I opened my eyes, and there were indeed ten suns outside the window.And I did not live through that morning.
answer: After our parents died, my brother and I depended on each other. During the quarrel I threw out that angry line and locked my bedroom door. My brother wanted to cheer me up without waking me, so in the night my brother went around outside my window and painted nine suns on the outer side of the glass. The security grille my brother was leaning on came loose, and my brother fell from the building. At daybreak I was startled awake and saw the nine suns on my window—together with the real rising sun, exactly ten. Then I saw my brother’s body on the ground below. Losing my family one after another, I killed myself in grief.
hints: Of the ten suns, nine were put there by human hands.
My brother wanted it finished before I woke, so he went outside my window.
My brother painted nine suns and fell to his death; I saw ten suns, and I saw his body.

title: One More Round
story: They were playing rock paper scissors in the river.One of them never came up again.Afterwards, cries for help were often heard from the river.And after every cry, a voice would follow: “Rock, paper, scissors.”
answer: Two children were having a breath-holding contest in the water, with a rule: win a round of rock paper scissors and you may surface for one breath; lose, and you keep holding your breath. One child lost round after round and, too stubborn to stop, finally blacked out and could not be saved. After the child died, the child became a water ghost, fixated on the game that never ended. Since then, the water ghost drags under anyone who enters the water and forces that person to play by the same rule: win to rise for a breath, lose and be pulled back down. Trapped people cry for help while they take their breath, but the water ghost only calls for the next round and never lets anyone leave.
hints: Winning or losing the game decided whether you could briefly do the one thing that keeps you alive.
The first to die still takes part in the same game now.
Only a win lets you surface to breathe; the drowned child became a water ghost and keeps forcing others to play.

title: Rock, Paper, Scissors
story: They backed me into a corner and said they wanted to play rock paper scissors.“Rock beats paper.”At last I got my hands on the scissors, and heard them laugh: “This time, paper beats scissors.”I lost, and I never went back to class.
answer: I was a student being bullied at school. Several bullies pinned me in a corner and threw sharp stones at me, smashing through my school uniform, and laughed that rock had beaten paper. I took out a pair of scissors to fight back; the bullies seized my hands, tore the scissors away, and then ripped off strips of cloth and tightened the strips around my neck. Killing me, the one who had held the scissors, with cloth, the bullies called the act paper beating scissors. That is how I died. This so-called game was just the name the bullies gave their own violence.
hints: The rock, the paper, and the scissors they named were all real objects.
I got the scissors in order to protect myself.
Stones smashed through my uniform, the scissors were torn from me, and in the end they strangled me with strips of cloth.

title: My Roommate’s Prank
story: My roommates and I loved scaring Xiaohong. She was bold, and nothing we did ever got much of a reaction out of her.At dawn, a scream jolted me awake.A line of writing had appeared on the ceiling.This time, I could not laugh.
answer: Xiaohong had long been tormented and humiliated by our pranks. We read Xiaohong’s silence as boldness and assumed Xiaohong never minded. That night Xiaohong left the words “Scared you this time, didn’t I?” on the ceiling, then hanged herself in the room we all shared. Another roommate woke first, found Xiaohong’s body, and screamed. I opened my eyes to that line of writing, and to Xiaohong already dead, and finally understood what that question was asking.
hints: We took her endless silence to mean she had never been hurt.
She left that line, and something far more serious happened in the room as well.
She killed herself after leaving “Scared you this time, didn’t I?”, and a roommate woke to find her body.

title: The Radio
story: He had just finished a big piece of work and was driving back to the city.He switched on the radio, and the same sentence came through the broadcast again and again.The phone rang immediately after.He never made it back to the city—he took his own life.
answer: He was a radio host planning to murder his wife. He had recorded the entire show in advance, to be played during the live slot he was responsible for, then left the station, went home, and did the killing—the voice on the air would serve as proof that he never left his post. On the drive back to the station, he turned on the radio and heard the faulty player looping the same recorded sentence over and over. His colleagues at the station, finding the program malfunctioning and unable to reach him, called to summon him back. He knew the secret absence was exposed and the cover he had staked everything on had failed; afraid the murder would come to light, he killed himself.
hints: He wanted the broadcast to prove he had stayed in one place the whole time.
The voice on the radio was his own, but he was out elsewhere at that moment.
The host used a pre-recorded show to cover his absence while he killed his wife; the playback glitch showed his colleagues he was not at the station.

title: The First to Get Out
story: The time bomb was about to go off, and my teammate was still locked in a struggle with the criminals.I leapt out the window and hid in the water below.In the end, that time bomb was left intact.My teammate walked out alive; I died outside.
answer: We had infiltrated a building standing in the water to stop criminals from detonating a time bomb. I was to defuse the bomb; my teammate kept the criminals occupied. With the timer about to end and the bomb not yet defused, all I could do was jump out the window into the water. The bomb then malfunctioned and never went off. Upstairs, the criminals kept fighting my teammate, and one of the criminals produced a grenade. In the crisis my teammate kicked the grenade out the window to keep the blast away from the room, not knowing I was still hiding just below. The grenade landed near me and killed me. It was the time bomb that stayed intact; what killed me was the grenade kicked out afterwards.
hints: More than one kind of explosive appeared at the scene.
Someone inside the room sent another explosive outside.
My teammate kicked the grenade out the window, and it killed me as I still hid beneath it.

title: The Book Was Borrowed
story: In the middle of class, the teacher suddenly flew into a rage at me. I was not angry at all—if anything, I found it a little funny.
answer: The teacher had forgotten to bring a book to class, so my book was borrowed to teach from. Halfway through the lesson, the teacher forgot the book was borrowed from me, decided instead that I was the one who had come without a book, and flew into a rage at me. I knew the truth, so I was not angry—I found it funny.
hints: The reason for the teacher’s anger had to do with the textbook.
The textbook was off my desk for the moment because I was helping the teacher.
The teacher was teaching from my borrowed textbook, forgot it was borrowed, and took me for the one without a book.

title: Familiar Eyes
story: My brother has cared for me all these years.After the earthquake, I lay pinned under the rubble, unable to move and unable to cry out.A pair of familiar eyes appeared outside the crack in the stones. I blinked with all my might, and she saw me.Then a tile was laid over the crack.
answer: I was born deaf and mute, and I live with my older brother and his wife. The earthquake pinned me in the rubble; I could not move or call out, only wait for someone to find me. She reached the crack first and saw me signaling to her with my eyes, begging for rescue. She had always seen caring for me as a burden on the family, and she decided to hide the fact that I was alive. She covered the crack with a tile so my brother would not find me, told my brother this spot had already been searched, and led my brother away to look elsewhere. My brother never knew what she had done, and I was never rescued.
hints: Those eyes belonged to someone who knew me and knew I could not cry out.
She saw clearly that I was alive, yet covered the very crack through which I could have been found.
My sister-in-law, wanting to be rid of the burden of caring for me, covered the crack, kept my brother in the dark, and led him away from the rubble.

title: Counting the Steps
story: To prove the school was not haunted, I stayed in the classroom until midnight.Nothing happened. I packed my bag, and on the way down began counting the steps.One, two, three…Only outside the building did it occur to me: leaving this classroom in the daytime never involves going downstairs.
answer: My classroom sits on the ground floor; the corridor at the classroom door is level with the ground outside, and normally I walk straight out of the building along the corridor, with no stairs at all. The rumors of a haunting at night are true. That night, when I left the classroom, a flight of steps that should not exist appeared where the exit is ordinarily flat. Convinced that nothing had happened, I walked and counted my way down, and only outside the building did I notice that the route I had just taken was entirely different from the daytime one.
hints: The classroom’s real floor matters.
I left through the exit I always use, and in the daytime that path has no steps.
The classroom is on the ground floor, yet at night a flight of descending steps appeared out of nowhere.

title: The Waterweed
story: He had not been back to this river for years.Sitting on the bank, he asked the old fisherman, “Are the waterweeds down below still as thick as ever?”The fisherman pointed at the deep pool and said one sentence.He sat there a long time, and that day he ended his own life here.
answer: Years ago, his girlfriend fell into that deep pool. He jumped in to save the girlfriend and, in the murky, rushing water, grabbed a handful of something long and thin, took the handful for waterweed, and let go; the girlfriend was never found. That handful was the girlfriend’s hair. Years later he came back and asked about the waterweed. The old fisherman, who had worked and dredged those waters for years, told him, “That pool bottom is nothing but rock. I have cleared it many times — waterweed has never grown there.” Only then did it strike him that what he had released might have been the girlfriend. Unable to bear the remorse of having perhaps held the girlfriend in his hand and willingly let go, he took his own life.
hints: He once tried to save someone in this water.
While saving her, he grabbed a handful of something long and thin — then let it go.
He had mistaken his girlfriend’s hair for waterweed; once he learned no waterweed ever grew in that pool, he realized he might have let go of her.

title: The Sailor
story: I used to be a sailor.After we were rescued, the mere sight of fish made me shake with nausea.In the hungriest days aboard, we had fish to eat the whole time.
answer: At sea our ship ran into trouble, lost power, and drifted for a long time. Food ran short, and some of the crew did not survive. To hold on, the survivors used the flesh of dead shipmates as fishing bait and ate the fish caught with the bait, until we were finally rescued. Those fish had fed on our companions, and I had lived on those fish in turn. From then on, the sight of fish brought the whole experience back — the nausea, the fear — and I could never eat fish again.
hints: I survived a shipwreck and a long wait for rescue.
With no ordinary bait left, we made use of our dead shipmates.
The survivors baited their hooks with their companions’ flesh and ate the fish they caught until rescue came; I have never been able to face fish since.

title: The Illegitimate Son
story: The man who came to apply for our driver’s job looked far too much like me.My father was a habitual womanizer. After a moment’s thought, I asked with a smile, “Did your mother used to work at our house?”He shook his head and said it was his father who had worked at our house.I stopped smiling.
answer: Years ago, my mother had an affair with the family’s driver and gave birth to me, yet my mother brought me up all along as the young master of a rich household. The driver, afraid of being found out, resigned and went back to his hometown, where he later married and had another son. That son is the man who has now come to apply for the job — he and I share the same biological father. At first, seeing how much he resembled me, I took him for one of my father’s outside children and meant to probe by asking about his mother. But he said his mother had always stayed back in the hometown, that it was his father who had once worked at our house, and gave the old driver’s name. The resemblance together with this story made me begin to doubt my own parentage. I was afraid the father who raised me would learn of my mother’s betrayal, and afraid the life I had would change because of the betrayal.
hints: At first I guessed that my father had another child somewhere outside the family.
The applicant’s mother never came to our house — but his father did, as our old driver.
Both the applicant and I could be the old driver’s sons; the question of birth has landed on me.

title: The Four-Year-Old Mother
story: The new student told me, “Mom is four years old this year.”I thought he had gotten it wrong, and went for a home visit that weekend.The woman who opened the door already had white hair, yet an iron chain was fastened to her ankle.The student behind her suddenly smiled: “Bro, the new one is here.”
answer: The student is in fact an adult, unusually small in build and boyish in face. By dressing the part and forging identity papers, the student slips into kindergartens to lure teachers into home visits, then the student and the older brother kidnap whoever comes. Several women are being held captive in the house; one of the women has been shut in for four years and is forced to play the student’s mother in front of outsiders. On purpose, the student gives the number of years the woman has been held in the house as the woman’s age, acting like a child who got the number wrong, so that I would come and check for myself. The older brother is waiting inside. By the time I see the iron chain, I am already the next one the two brothers mean to lock up.
hints: The age the student gave has nothing to do with the woman’s actual age.
She has been in that house for four years, and she cannot leave freely.
The student is an adult disguised as a small child who lures teachers into home visits and kidnaps them together with his brother.

title: Back to Camp
story: The expedition leader told him to turn back, and he said, “I’m not going back without the summit.”He truly stood on the summit, and he survived the blizzard too.At daybreak, he finally made it back to the familiar camp.Later, people found his body there.
answer: Close to the summit, the climbing team ran into foul weather and the leader ordered a retreat. He insisted on pressing on, reached the top alone, and was then caught by the blizzard. Out of contact with the team all night, he barely made it through to daybreak on the mountain, by then drained of nearly everything. Unable to keep waiting in such weather, the team took him for dead, packed up the supplies, and pulled out of the high camp. He dragged himself back to camp with the last of his strength, only to find no one there and none of the gear that could have restored him and kept him warm. He could not go on down the mountain, and froze to death in the very place he had counted on for rescue.
hints: What he found was the camp his team had once occupied.
After striking out alone, he lost contact with the team for the whole night.
Believing him dead, the team withdrew with the people and the supplies; by the time he reached camp, he had no strength left to descend.

title: His Skin
story: I watched him every day.One day, he said goodbye to everyone and said he would never come back.I put on his skin.Tomorrow, people will still see him.
answer: He was a virtual streamer who appeared on screen as a digital character. He announced graduation — a permanent end to streaming as that character. I was one of his viewers, and I could not accept letting the character vanish, so I took up his virtual character model and went on streaming as that character myself. The “skin” is the model an operator wears in a stream; the person inside the model in the new streams is me. He himself has retired.
hints: He used to appear on screen in the form of a character.
What I put on can swap a person’s appearance in a livestream.
He is a retired virtual streamer; I keep playing the same character in his model.

title: She Likes Me
story: She hardly ever spoke in class, yet she stared at me every single day.More and more, I came to believe she liked me.Sometimes our eyes met, and her mouth would open and close; I couldn’t hear a sound.Not once did she smile.
answer: She can see the ghosts that cling to people, and knows to scatter the ghosts by silently reciting an incantation. Ever since she was little, talking about the things she saw got her treated as a freak by her classmates, so she went quiet. Lately a ghost had fastened itself onto me, and all she could do was keep her eyes on where the ghost hung, mouthing the incantation to drive the ghost off. The movement of her lips is the chant; her gaze toward me is her watching the ghost attached to me. I mistook this unbroken act of rescue for affection.
hints: Her lips were repeating a string of words that actually had an effect.
She could see something clinging to me that I could not see.
She was silently chanting an exorcism; I mistook her constant watching for affection.

title: Footsteps on the Stairs
story: The screaming downstairs stopped.One, two, three… nine.I tried to get out through the balcony, bracing on the armrests to push myself up.But my body gave only a twitch.Ten, eleven… seventeen.The sound drew closer and closer.
answer: Not long before, I had been in a car accident. My legs no longer move, and for now I live in a wheelchair. A killing happened downstairs, and from the top of the stairwell I saw the killer with the knife — and the killer saw me. Then the killer started up the stairs toward me. I swung my wheelchair toward the balcony and, in blind panic, tried by old habit to stand and get over the railing, but my body would not perform the motion. With my old ways of escaping — running, jumping — gone, I froze in terror and could only listen as the killer’s footsteps crossed the stairs one by one, nearer and nearer. Those numbers were me counting the killer’s steps.
hints: The numbers track the movements of someone drawing closer.
I had just been in a car accident, and my body could no longer move the way it used to.
I sat in a wheelchair as the killer came up the stairs; in panic I tried to stand and flee, and found my legs would not move.

title: The Candy Lure
story: The little girl would not stop crying.A strange man took out some candy and reached a hand toward her, meaning to take her home with him.She shook her head, backing away and crying for her mother.He failed to take her away. Afterward, she never cried again.
answer: After the zombie virus broke out, the zombies nearby home in on sound. The man came across the little girl crying all alone and wanted to take the girl back to his own safe shelter, but the man was afraid that explaining out loud would only raise the danger. So the man brought out the candy, hoping to calm the girl first, quiet the girl down, and then lead the girl away. The girl was wary of strangers; the girl refused the candy and kept crying for her mother. The crying had already drawn the zombies. The man could not get the girl clear in time, and the girl was killed by the zombies.
hints: There was a danger in that area drawn to sound.
The man wanted to bring the girl to a safe shelter.
Zombies came for her crying; his attempt to quiet her with candy and lead her away failed, and he could not save her.

title: A Narrow Escape
story: I had taken off my jewelry and my keys, but the metal detector kept going off.I missed my flight and went back to the hospital.The second time I was discharged, I felt relieved instead.
answer: I had just had abdominal surgery abroad and was flying home. At the security check, even after I took off every piece of metal I carried, the alarm kept centering on my abdomen. Remembering the discomfort that had lingered ever since the operation, I decided to go to a hospital first, and so I missed the flight. The imaging found that a metal surgical clamp had been left inside me during the earlier operation. The hospital operated again and took the clamp out. I was simply relieved that the security check had alerted me, and that this dangerous oversight had been caught and dealt with in time.
hints: The metal setting off the alarm could not be removed from clothing or luggage.
I had had abdominal surgery not long before.
A surgical clamp the doctors left inside me set off the alarm; only on re-examination was it taken out.

title: The Woman Who Jumped
story: She had lived in the dead city for a long time, believing she was the last living person.The moment she leapt from the high-rise, the phone in her pocket rang.She regretted it, but there was no time to answer.
answer: The zombie virus broke out, and the people around her turned one after another. She hid alone in the city for a very long time, with no answer coming back from anyone, until she believed herself the only living human left; in the end she jumped from the building in despair. While she was falling, a call came in from someone still alive. The ring made her realize, all at once, that she might still be able to reach other survivors, that the loneliness might not go on forever. Hope of living welled up in her — but the decision of a moment ago could no longer be taken back, and she died.
hints: A zombie disaster had struck the city she lived in.
She never confirmed the whole world was empty — she simply went unanswered for a very long time.
Another survivor called; by the time she realized she might still have companions, it was already too late.

title: Dad in the Vent
story: I can see with only one eye.While I was showering, a familiar face appeared in a crack in the ceiling.“Dad, what are you doing up there?”I recoiled in fright and slipped.From then on, I could never see him again.
answer: He had already been murdered by a killer. His body was hidden in the space above the bathroom ceiling, the face turned toward the vent. Showering, I looked up and saw his face and the open eyes, thought he was hiding up there watching me, and slipped as I recoiled in fright. One of my eyes had been blind to begin with; in the fall, my one seeing eye was badly pierced by a hook on the wall, and in time I lost that sight as well. He could not answer because he was long dead; I can never see him again because I have gone completely blind myself.
hints: The face in the vent could not respond to my words.
When I slipped, my one seeing eye was injured.
My father’s body was hidden above; startled, I slipped and destroyed the last eye that could see.

title: Spitting Out the Pills
story: Every day, my wife’s voice urges me to take my medicine.I answer her, and once she goes quiet, I secretly spit the pills out.Back in the days when I took my medicine faithfully, I would go days at a stretch without seeing her.
answer: My wife died in a car crash. Unable to accept losing my wife, I began to see my wife and hear my wife speak — hallucinations that went on and on. Under the doctor’s treatment, the hallucinations gradually faded: I saw my wife less and less, heard my wife’s voice less and less. I knew the medicine was behind the fading, but I took my wife’s fading for one more parting, and so I began secretly spitting out the pills, wanting to keep feeling my wife there beside me. The wife in the hallucinations kept her old caring ways, and still urged me every day to take my medicine on time.
hints: No one else can see or hear the wife I speak of.
The doctor’s treatment was gradually fading my hallucinations.
My wife died long ago; to keep her hallucination, I secretly stopped taking my pills.

title: Ghosts Outside
story: I woke in a strange cabin, my head pounding.Scattered on the floor were sheets of paper, each reading, “Don’t go out. There are ghosts outside.”The door was unlocked.Beside a pool of blood lay one more note in the same handwriting: “I was wrong. Run.”
answer: An obsessive stalker of mine drugged me and carried me to an abandoned cabin at the edge of the woods. The stalker knew I was afraid of ghosts, so the stalker left the warnings on purpose: the stalker wanted me too frightened to step out alone, so I would settle into the life together the stalker had arranged. What the stalker did not know when the stalker picked the house was that a serial killer was using the house’s basement to store the killer’s victims. Coming back, the killer found the stalker and me lying unconscious, and attacked the stalker. Wounded, the stalker understood at last that the true danger was inside the house. With the stalker’s remaining strength, the stalker wrote “I was wrong. Run,” and then the killer killed the stalker and dragged the stalker’s body down into the basement. When I woke, the door was still unlocked. The first warnings that had kept me inside were the stalker’s lie; the last note was the warning to flee that the stalker left while dying.
hints: Both notes were written by the same person — but what she knew had changed between them.
The first warnings were meant to keep me, who feared ghosts, inside the house.
My captor was attacked by the killer hiding in the house; dying, she wrote “Run” and retracted her invented haunting.

title: The Perfect Statement
story: After he was brought into the police station, he volunteered that he had a major case to confess to.He talked all afternoon, never stopping his reminders: “Write that sentence down too — don’t leave anything out.”When he finally got the written statement to check over, he nodded with satisfaction.The officer slammed his pen down onto the desk.
answer: He is a crime novelist who got brought in for drunken trouble. He lied that he had taken part in a complicated crime and had the police record the so-called confession — in truth, he was dictating the novel he had only just plotted. The officers wrote out the names, the places, the course of every action, and handed the record to him to check. He read the record through, nodded in satisfaction, and even admitted outright: “I made every word of it up — perfect that you’ve organized it into a manuscript for me.” Only after a whole afternoon’s work did the officers see that the detailed document in front of them was a story he had spun under the cover of a confession, and that is why the officers were furious.
hints: The details he told were complete, yet they matched no real case.
He normally earns his living writing stories; his insistence on word-for-word record had another purpose.
He passed off the crime novel he had plotted as a confession, had the police take it down for him, then admitted it himself.

title: Hello, Uncle Wang
story: Ever since I was old enough to remember, I had never met my father. Mother said he had been abroad all this time.Years later, he suddenly came home, and I got a form of address wrong.That very day, of my two parents only he was still alive.And yet I could not go home with him either.
answer: Father had worked abroad for years, and Mother had fallen into an affair with our neighbor Uncle Wang. Uncle Wang came by so often that I had grown used to opening the door for this neighbor, knowing Uncle Wang was going upstairs to see Mother. The day Father suddenly returned, I failed to recognize the father I had not seen in all those years and blurted out: “Hello, Uncle Wang — Mother is upstairs waiting for you.” Questioning me further, Father pieced together the affair between Mother and the neighbor, and in a rage Father killed them both; Father was then arrested by the police. I had lost my mother, and the only one of my two parents still alive was locked away, so I had to be taken in and raised by someone else.
hints: I mistook my father for the other man who kept coming to see Mother.
The form of address I got wrong exposed Mother’s relationship with the neighbor.
Father killed Mother and the neighbor and was arrested; with my only surviving parent in custody, there was no one left for me to go home to.

title: Online Shopping
story: He did not like dumplings, yet for days the shopping app kept recommending frozen dumplings and a whole pile of dumpling-making supplies.He handed the phone to his wife: “Surely it got the recommendations wrong this time?”She looked at the screen, smiled, and said: “Quite fitting.”Before long, he was dead.
answer: He and his wife shared one shopping account, and every browsing record shaped the recommendations that account received. The wife had long resented his endless squandering of money and his refusal to lift a finger around the house, and she had formed a plan to kill him and turn his remains into filling for dumplings. Again and again the wife browsed dumplings and related supplies on the shared account, and those visits changed the recommendations he saw as well. He assumed the app was only guessing at his own tastes, never suspecting that what surfaced there was his wife’s preparation. The wife later carried out the murder, and in the end he was killed.
hints: The browsing records of two people feed into the same account.
The wife had been looking at dumplings and related supplies for some time.
The wife planned to kill him and make dumplings from his remains; her browsing shaped the recommendations he saw.

title: My Mother Won
story: Father was dead set against my being with her, but Mother said: “Go ahead. It’s fine.”On his sickbed, Father told me a secret. Crying, I went to ask Mother, and she told me another one.Father died later on, and yet at last I smiled.
answer: The younger sister my family had adopted and I fell in love after we both grew up. Father opposed the relationship; Mother supported us. When Father was terminally ill, he told me that my sister was in fact his illegitimate daughter, believing this would make me understand that we were brother and sister by the same father. I went to ask Mother, and only then learned that I was actually the child of Mother and another man — something Father had never known. My sister and I had different birth fathers, and Mother had known this all along, so the blood relation Father feared did not exist. Father was furious when he learned of Mother’s concealment, and he later died of his illness. I smiled because I finally understood that my beloved and I shared no blood relation, and the relationship could go on.
hints: The reason for Father’s opposition was tied to a secret about who she really was.
Mother knew who the other one’s birth father was, holding a fact Father did not know.
She was Father’s illegitimate daughter, while I was Mother’s child by another man; we shared none of the blood relation Father believed we had.

title: No One Stopped Me
story: I set a ladder against the outside wall, climbed in through the window, and carried out a case of jewels.Several police officers watched the whole time.When I got back to the ground, a woman took the case with tears in her eyes, thanking me over and over.
answer: I was a firefighter taking part in the rescue after a fire. The blaze in that house had been brought under control and the residents evacuated, but the fire-damaged stairway was temporarily impassable. The woman asked us to help retrieve a case of jewels left upstairs; once we confirmed that route was usable, I set up the ladder, went in through the window, and returned the case to her hands. The police officers at the scene were there for security; the officers knew I was helping the woman recover her belongings, so they simply watched and kept the work space clear.
hints: The woman was the homeowner, and she knew exactly what I was carrying.
The house’s normal entrance was unusable; I was helping with a rescue.
I was a firefighter; after the fire, at the owner’s request, I set up a ladder and retrieved the jewel case she had left upstairs.

title: The Silent Ritual
story: My parents had been arguing constantly of late. Mother asked me on the sly how to make a bank transfer, and she often waved her hands about at home without a word.After dinner, Father went out, and she slipped out right after him.I followed her quietly to the square.Dozens of people were making the same movements she was, yet not a trace of music could be heard anywhere around.
answer: Mother had recently joined a neighborhood square-dancing troupe. Father suspected Mother’s frequent outings meant Mother was seeing someone, and the two of them fought over it; to keep the peace, Mother practiced and went out while avoiding Father. The transfer Mother asked about was payment to the troupe leader for the team’s matching uniforms. Mother’s hand-waving at home was dance practice. To spare the surrounding residents, the troupe all wore headphones to hear the music, so to outsiders it looked like a crowd moving in unison with no audible accompaniment. Only by following Mother did I come to see that all these seemingly secret doings revolved around one and the same dance activity.
hints: The transfer paid for something a whole group would use together.
The movements she practiced at home were ones she also did with the others.
She had joined a headphone-wearing square-dance troupe and paid for the uniforms; the headphones kept the music from being heard by others.

title: The Midnight Train
story: Five minutes before midnight, the man boarded the train and studied the passengers one by one.“You’re twenty-eight this year?” “That’s right.”“You’re fifty-five?” “That’s right.”Then he asked an old lady: “Sixty-nine?”“That’s right. Once it’s past twelve, I’ll be seventy.”The man’s face went white.
answer: The man could see the age, in whole years, at which each person would ultimately die — a number that steps up at midnight on every birthday — though the man could not see his own. The man noticed that the death-ages shown for the passengers in this carriage were identical to their current ages, so the man went from one to the next, asking to verify. For the earlier passengers, death might fall on any day within their current year of age, so the timing could not yet be pinned down. But the old lady said she would turn seventy in five more minutes, and what the man saw was that the old lady would die at sixty-nine. That meant the old lady would not live to reach this birthday. Add the fact that many others around the man were likewise in the final year of their lives, and the man strongly suspected the train was about to suffer a deadly accident. The man could not know whether he himself would die — and the man was already standing in the carriage the man believed doom was about to reach.
hints: The ages he sees and the passengers’ actual ages are not the same kind of information.
He sees the age at death in whole years, and the old lady is about to pass beyond that age.
The old lady will die at sixty-nine yet turns seventy in five minutes; he realizes she will not live to see midnight.

title: The Birthday Curse
story: A man calling himself a sorcerer said my child would die on his birthday.I rushed off to beg someone to break the curse. After hearing me out, that man smiled and said: “He’s a fraud. There’s no such thing as a curse.”I was finally at ease.On the birthday, the child died all the same.
answer: The so-called sorcerer was a fraud who played at the mystic arts, and the fraud had frightened us with the threat that the child would die on his birthday. A local who knew the man saw through the trick and told us there was no real curse, and because of that we let our guard down. When the fraud learned he had been exposed, the fraud broke into our home on the birthday itself and killed the child with his own hands, so that others would believe the fraud’s prophecies came true. The judgment that there was no curse was correct — the death came from the very man who had voiced the threat carrying out a murder.
hints: What was said about there being no curse was true.
The person who issued the threat could still take the actions of an ordinary man.
To make his prophecy come true, the fraud broke in on the birthday and killed the child himself.

title: Blood by the Cradle
story: The man came home. With one stroke of a sword he killed the dog he had raised for years.The next moment, he was overcome with regret.
answer: Coming home, the man found his dog covered in blood and raced frantically into the nursery: the cradle had been knocked over, blood dripped down from it, and the baby was nowhere to be seen. In his fury the man cut the dog down with a single stroke of his sword — but as the dog let out its last whimper, a baby’s cry rang out. Only then did the man find the infant lying safe beneath the crib, with a wolf’s corpse beside it. The dog had fought the wolf to protect the baby, which was why the dog was covered in blood; now the dog had died wrongly accused.
hints: The man connected the blood on the dog with the baby’s disappearance.
There was another animal in the house, and the dog had fought it.
The dog killed the wolf that broke in, and the baby was unharmed beneath the crib; the man had wrongly taken the dog for the one who hurt his child.

title: The Magnet
story: I touched my toy to my teacher’s gold bracelet. She froze, and then wept with anger.She stormed into the principal’s office, and the argument went on for a long while.At home I told my father, and he gave me just one warning: “From now on, when you play with that, keep away from your mother.”
answer: What I was playing with was a magnet. My teacher wore a bracelet the principal had given her — the two of them were married, and the principal had told the teacher the bracelet was pure gold. My magnet clung to the bracelet unmistakably, exposing the bracelet as an iron core plated with gold. The teacher realized the principal had deceived her and went to the principal’s office to fight it out. The moment Father heard my story, he remembered that he too had once given Mother gilded jewelry passed off as pure gold; afraid my playing with the magnet at home would expose that, he told me to keep away from Mother.
hints: My toy can attract one very common metal.
The teacher had always believed the bracelet was solid gold, a gift from her husband.
The magnet clung to the iron-cored, gold-plated bracelet and exposed the principal; Father had given Mother the same kind of fake gold jewelry.

title: Lucky in the Crowd
story: The chandelier came down and I was unharmed, but the waiter’s arm was covered in blood.Fire swept past my side and set a lady’s dress alight.I finally stood before my enemy without a single wound on me.Overhead, a beam cracked open once more. I cried out: “I dissolve the contract.”This time, the pain fell on me.
answer: Five years ago, my enemy’s factory polluted the river and killed my little sister. For tonight’s revenge I had bought a disaster-warding contract: whenever anyone stood near me, any harm that should have befallen me would be transferred to the people around me; I could dissolve it with a spoken word, but upon dissolving it I would bear, in equal measure, all the harm previously transferred away. The contract took effect tonight. I had believed the contract would shield me and carry me to my enemy, and when I signed I gave little weight to the price bystanders would pay. Disasters struck the banquet one after another; I passed through the chandelier, the flames, and the rest untouched, while innocent guests were hurt in my stead. Amid the shaking of the earthquake, that protection carried me to my enemy; when I saw the decorative beam split open overhead once again, I could no longer bear to let others keep suffering disaster in my place. I dissolved the contract of my own will; the harm already transferred came back onto me, the protection ceased, and I was badly injured beneath the falling debris.
hints: My walking away unharmed and the injuries of those around me are in direct exchange.
The contract passes disasters meant for me on to the people beside me.
After I dissolved the contract, the harm transferred earlier came back onto me; I gave up a revenge that had been bought with other people’s suffering.

title: My Favorite Author
story: I gave my favorite horror novelist a birthday present: a fountain pen.His assistant carried the gift home ahead of him; he himself was still at the venue.I went home, opened up my screen, and waited for him to get home too.The moment he walked in the door, I dialed the police.
answer: I was obsessed with the novelist and wanted to peep into the novelist’s life, so I gave the novelist a fountain pen with a hidden camera inside as a birthday gift. The assistant carried the gift back to the novelist’s study, and at home I waited on the feed for the novelist to return. On the screen there was a bound person. Once the novelist walked in, the novelist began tormenting the bound person, and the setup and the acts matched, in uncanny detail, a killing from one of the novels I had read. In horror I realized the novelist might be feeding real crimes into the novelist’s fiction, and I called the police at once. The police later found the victim and supporting evidence, confirming that the crime matching the novel had indeed been committed by the novelist.
hints: The pen I gave away lets me see the writer’s study from my own home.
What happened in that study resembled a crime from one of his novels.
Peeping through the camera in the pen, I watched the writer torment a bound person and discovered his fiction was drawn from real crimes.

title: Rain
story: It rains here every day, yet at night there are always “stars,” clear as can be.I took one look through a telescope.A point of light closed, then opened again.It had been watching me the whole time.
answer: After I died, I was confined in an underworld space built to imitate the streets and daily life of the human world. The dead here are penned and raised by demons as food. The points of light overhead come from the demons’ eyes, which look like a sky full of stars from afar; the demons gaze down on the dead being farmed below, eyes closing and shifting. The rain that falls day and night without pause is the demons’ drool, dripping endlessly at the sight of food. Through the telescope I made out the eyes clearly — and the mouths beneath the eyes, and the falling liquid — and at last I understood what kind of place I was living in.
hints: I am already dead; life here only imitates the human world.
The points of light that look like stars belong to creatures that are watching me.
Demons farm the dead from above; their eyes are the stars, and their drool is the rain that falls every day.

title: Better to Remember Than to Meet
story: The doctor said: “I’m sorry. I did all I could.”I wanted to see my husband one last time, but he held down the white sheet: “Don’t look. Remember him as he was.”I did not listen.That freshly stitched wound had no business being on his body.
answer: My husband had been in a coma since a car crash, kept alive by machines. The doctor overseeing his treatment was involved in the illegal organ trade; the doctor falsified records of deterioration and death, killed my husband, and harvested the organs. The doctor told me that everything possible had been done, and tried to stop me from viewing the body, in order to hide the new surgical wounds. I insisted on lifting the sheet and saw sutured wounds across the chest and abdomen that matched nothing in my husband’s recent treatment schedule. The wounds alone could only make me suspect an operation I had never been told about. I called the police afterward, and only after investigating the records and the transactions did the police confirm that the death was tied to organ harvesting.
hints: The doctor kept me from the body to hide something recently done to it.
Nothing in the husband’s recent treatment schedule accounted for that wound.
The doctor faked the decline and the death to harvest organs illegally; the fresh sutures betrayed the undisclosed surgery.

title: The Perfume
story: She lost her parents as a child, and not long after, her little brother died too.On her birthday, her boyfriend handed her a small bottle of perfume.She took one clear look at the bottle and, before he could even open it, turned and ran.
answer: After her parents died in a car crash, she and her little brother once found a small bottle filled with liquid. She took the small bottle for a wish potion and coaxed her brother along, telling him that if he drank the liquid, Mom and Dad might come back. Her brother believed her — and died from swallowing the toxic industrial liquid inside the bottle. She never forgot the moment of making him drink the liquid. Years later, the perfume bottle closely resembled that little bottle in shape and cap. The sight of the perfume bottle brought her brother’s death and her own words rushing back, and she fled in terror.
hints: She had not smelled the perfume yet; it was the look of the bottle that struck her.
In her childhood there was a small bottle of liquid tied to her brother’s death.
She had fed her brother poison believing it a wish potion; the similar perfume bottle brought the memory surging back.

title: Craving a Bowl of Soup
story: In the famine, I caught the smell of meat broth — the first in far too long.Seeing me rush in, the owner of the house asked only one question: “Are you alone?”I nodded and begged him for a bowl.I never made it back out that door. The next day, the smell of meat broth drifted from the place again.
answer: The great famine was at its height, yet from a house not far off drifted a rich meat-broth smell the likes of which no one had known in ages. Half dead with hunger, I burst in to seize food — and saw a smile on the owner’s face that made my skin crawl. The owner had been using the broth to draw in starving people like me — people who came rushing in for food — and then killing those people to make new bait. What simmered in the next pot was me.
hints: In this famine, the owner somehow keeps replenishing his supply of meat.
The people who come begging for soup are the source of that supply.
He kills the starving drawn in by the broth and stews their bodies into the next pot; I became one of them.

title: A New Big Brother
story: The boy said: “Mom, I want a big brother to play with me every day.”The woman’s face changed: “But… you already have one.”He thought for a moment, then said with a smile: “Then swap him for a new one.”
answer: The boy had grown into a teenager. Deprived of family company all his life, the boy had turned to kidnapping to build the family the boy wanted. The boy was holding a woman and an older boy captive, forcing the two captives to play mother and big brother. The woman knew that the moment the captives failed to satisfy the boy, the boy would kill the captives and go looking for replacements. The current “brother” was still locked up in another room, yet the boy, finding the brother’s company not enough, asked for a brother again. The woman, afraid this meant the boy would kill the current brother, hurried to remind the boy that the boy already had a brother. That line — “swap him for a new one” — confirmed the boy meant to keep satisfying himself by replacing his family members.
hints: What the woman feared was what he would do once he had made his request.
She and the so-called brother were both being held in that home to play their roles.
The boy kidnapped people to play family and killed them when they displeased him; asking to swap the brother meant the current one was about to die.

title: After Spring Came
story: After winter set in, he walked into a half-built high-rise at a shut-down construction site and never came back.When work resumed in spring, the workers found his body.His head bore a severe wound, yet nothing that could have caused it could be found anywhere around him.
answer: In winter, icicles formed along the eaves of the towers on this northern construction site. As he passed below, one icicle broke loose, struck his head, and killed him. The site stayed shut down, so no one found him in time. Months later the weather warmed, the icicle had long since melted, and his body was finally discovered by the workers returning to the site. That is why the wound was still visible, while the object that had struck him was gone.
hints: Several months passed between his death and the discovery of his body.
The object that caused the injury disappears as the weather turns warm.
An icicle fell from high above in winter and killed him; by spring it had melted away.

title: The Last Square
story: The first piece landed on top of me, and I stayed where I was.The second piece landed beside me.This time, I disappeared together with all my companions in the same row.
answer: I was one small square already settled on the screen in a game of Tetris. A new piece stacked on top of me, but my row still had a gap, so the condition for clearing it was not met. Then another piece landed beside me and filled the last empty space in the row. The game promptly cleared the entire line, and I vanished from the screen along with every other square in it.
hints: The falling pieces and I belong to the same geometric grid of a screen.
When a horizontal row is filled completely, it is cleared away as a whole.
I am one small square in a game of Tetris; the last empty spot beside me was filled, and the whole row vanished.

title: One Good Night
story: The man died in his own home. The windows were closed, and the knob on the inside of the door lock had been turned to locked. The smart speaker in the entryway gave its last response: “Good night. The door is locked.”Yet the man’s phone had already dialed a call for help before that.
answer: The man had let an acquaintance into his home. After committing the murder, the guest left and pulled the door shut. The windows had been closed all along, and the door showed no sign of forced entry.The man had once connected the electric knob on the inside of his door lock to the entryway speaker, setting it up so that saying “good night” would lock the door. The killer knew about this habit. After stepping out, the killer woke the speaker from the other side of the door and said “good night.” The speaker received the command and drove the indoor knob to lock the door.The knob really did turn from the inside, but that only proves the locking device was indoors. The call the man dialed while dying, together with the speaker’s logs, set the police asking who had spoken that “good night.”
hints: The knob really did turn from the inside, but a device can drive it.
The speaker can hear someone speaking at the door, and the man had set up one bedtime phrase as a command.
After the killer left, he made the speaker carry out the locking from outside the door.

title: Little One Is Here
story: Waking from my afternoon nap, I heard a voice from the living room: “Mom, Little One is here.”I lived alone. That very afternoon, I moved out.On my first night in the new home, I could not sleep. At midnight, the same words came from the living room again.I touched my flat, empty belly and sent a message to my former landlord: “I want to move back.”
answer: I had lost the child in my womb. After leaving the hospital, I lived alone with a parrot for company. The landlord was a small man who often called himself “Little One.” I rarely spoke with the landlord, and I had never once said the words “Mom, Little One is here” in front of the parrot.That day, waking from my nap, I heard the parrot suddenly say the sentence. Suspicious, I looked into it and found that the landlord had repeatedly let himself into my home late at night. Pressed by my questions, the landlord admitted slipping sleeping pills into my drinks; once I was deep asleep, the landlord would climb into my bedding, hold me, and call me Mom. That sentence was something the landlord had said to me.Terrified, I moved out at once, and the parrot came with me. In the new home I lay awake all night, and when I heard the parrot imitating the landlord again, I found myself missing the feeling of someone nestled close to me. Thinking of the child I had lost, I decided to make “Little One” my child, so I contacted the landlord about moving back.
hints: Both times, the voice was the same parrot’s, and it moved to the new home with me.
The sentence was one the parrot learned from the person who kept sneaking into my home.
I moved out because I feared the landlord; by the time I wanted to move back, I had decided to let him stay by my side in a different role.

title: Pastries and a Gunshot
story: Little Red Riding Hood carried a basket of pastries to visit her grandmother.The wolf arrived ahead of her, and the hunter followed along.After the gunshot, Little Red Riding Hood helped her grandmother up and fed the pastries into her mouth.Watching this scene, the wolf lying on the ground finally closed his eyes.
answer: This is a fairy-tale world where wolves can talk and live among people. The grandmother had once saved the wolf from a hunter’s chase, and the wolf had watched over the grandmother in secret ever since.Little Red Riding Hood’s mother wanted the inheritance all to herself and had poisoned the pastries. Little Red Riding Hood knew this and set out with the basket anyway. The wolf had overheard mother and daughter planning through the window, so the wolf reached the grandmother’s house first, hoping to get the grandmother away from mother and daughter.The grandmother was frail and could not walk. The wolf settled the grandmother by the bed and stood guard. When Little Red Riding Hood came in, the wolf blocked the way and tried to snatch the basket away. At that moment the hunter, who had trailed Little Red Riding Hood all the way, burst in, took the wolf for an attacker, and shot the wolf.The hunter pulled the fallen wolf aside, and Little Red Riding Hood went to the grandmother and fed the grandmother the poisoned pastries. The wolf had protected the grandmother for years, yet in the end a rescue that looked so timely destroyed the grandmother’s last chance.
hints: This is a fairy-tale world; the wolf understands human speech and can protect people.
The wolf knew the pastries were wrong and tried to stop Little Red Riding Hood from handing them to her grandmother.
The hunter misread the danger: his gun helped Little Red Riding Hood carry out the mother’s and daughter’s plan.

title: The Thief’s Warehouse
story: I had been a thief all my life, and I did not stop even in old age.When my children came home from a long trip, they knew the moment they walked in that I had been out stealing again these past few days.The next day, the warehouse where I hid my loot was emptied out, yet many new things had appeared in the house.
answer: In my old age my memory grew more and more muddled. I kept mistaking my own home for a place to burgle, while the old habits stayed with me: stealing things and hiding them in the warehouse.While the children were away, I found the house empty and “stole” our own belongings piece by piece, carrying them off to the warehouse. The children came home to a nearly empty house and understood at once what had happened.The children knew where the warehouse was. The next day they moved the furniture and household goods back home and put everything in its place. When I next went to the warehouse and found it empty, I assumed someone had stolen my loot; back at the house, I discovered it full of “new things.”
hints: The children know where I hide my takings, and this time they also knew where those things had come from.
My habit of stealing is still with me; my memory of our own belongings is what has failed.
The things in the warehouse had been in our home all along, and the children moved them back.

title: The Smile
story: Mom and Dad had not sat together like this for years.Shoulder to shoulder, hands linked, just like when I was little.I put away my needle and thread, stood in front of the sofa, and finally smiled.Neither of them ever scolded me again.
answer: When I was little, my parents were devoted to each other and loved me dearly. I loved sewing and often made clothes for my dolls, and my parents always praised how skillful I was.Then my parents both lost their jobs, and the family grew poorer and poorer. The couple quarreled constantly and took their resentment out on me. I was grown by then, but I still longed for my parents to go back to the way they used to be.After one quarrel, I killed my parents. I arranged their bodies on the sofa, then used needle and thread to fix their clothes and their linked hands in place, posing the bodies in the intimate posture I remembered.I put away the needle and thread and watched my parents sitting quietly together. I took the scene before me for a return to the beloved days of my childhood, and a contented smile came over my face.
hints: Besides making clothes, the needle and thread were used to hold the posture in place.
My parents sit quietly on the sofa, no longer able to answer me.
I killed my parents, then posed their bodies into the loving shapes from my childhood memories.

title: The New Dress
story: A woman left work wearing a one-of-a-kind dress.That night, she died on her way home.The dress was immaculate. Someone had carefully spread out its skirt, smoothing every pleat at the waist.
answer: The woman was a mortician. While preparing a body, the mortician fell for the dress the deceased was wearing, secretly swapped the dress off the corpse, and wore the dress home from work.The dress’s designer was obsessively protective of her work’s form. The designer had once had her lover wear the dress, but could not bear how the dress deformed whenever the lover walked. In the end the designer killed the lover, tidied the dress, and kept the body as a motionless display mannequin.Later the designer discovered the dress had been swapped away, tracked down the mortician, and followed the mortician as the mortician left work. In the designer’s eyes, the walking woman had once again ruined her carefully arranged work. The designer killed the woman, posed the body and skirt anew, and smoothed out the pleats.The body was replaced with another, and the dress was restored exactly as the designer demanded.
hints: The woman’s work brought her into contact with the dress’s original wearer.
After the killing, the killer tidied the dress; she cares intensely about how the garment sits.
The original wearer had also been kept by the designer as a motionless mannequin; once the woman took the dress, she became the next one.

title: Wake Up
story: The mother settled her daughter into the wheelchair and tucked the blanket around her.The daughter’s eyes were open. When the mother touched her face, she even gave a slight shake of her head.The mother laid that bandaged hand back on her lap and said softly, “When will you finally wake up?”
answer: In this story there is an experimental device that can drive a person’s simple body movements through preset programs, but cannot restore consciousness. The daughter’s father ran a tech company and had taken part in developing it.While swimming, the daughter’s hand had gotten caught in the drain at the bottom of the pool. Trapped for a long time, the daughter was rescued but remained in a coma ever after; the wound on her hand was still bandaged. Unable to accept that the daughter could only lie there, the mother insisted on fitting the daughter with the device.When it senses touch, the device makes the daughter raise her eyes, shake her head, and so on. The mother knows these responses come from a program, yet every day the mother lifts her daughter out of bed, tucks the blanket around her, and talks to her.The daughter seems to respond to her mother, but her consciousness has never returned. What the mother hopes for is the day these movements truly come from the daughter herself.
hints: Open eyes and a shake of the head do not mean the daughter has regained consciousness.
In this story there is an experimental device that can only control body movements.
The responses to touch are preset in the device; the mother keeps hoping her daughter will one day answer on her own.

title: The Brooch
story: My best friend was dead.I told the police: the body had been moved; someone wanted to dress her death up as a suicide.A brooch was found under the sofa. When the man was taken away, I smiled.
answer: After the man broke up with my best friend, my best friend killed herself at home, leaving a note. I was the one who found the note and the body first, so I knew how my best friend had died; still, I laid all my bitterness at the man’s door.I hid the note, moved the body, messed up the scene, and tossed a brooch the man had once left behind under the sofa. Then I called the police, claiming someone had killed my friend and then staged the scene as a suicide.The brooch led the police to the man, who had been there before, and they took him in for questioning. Watching the man being led away, I believed my revenge had worked, and I smiled.I was the one who tampered with the body and the scene; the “homicide disguised as a suicide” was a story I was trying to sell to the police. The brooch proves nothing about the man killing my best friend.
hints: My best friend’s death did not happen the way I described it to the police.
The brooch had been left there long ago; I was the one who moved where it showed up.
After my friend’s suicide, I hid the note and altered the scene, trying to drag her ex-boyfriend into the investigation.

title: The Rusted Railing
story: Halfway through their candlelit dinner, the couple fell from the balcony together.The broken railing was covered in rust. The husband’s phone lay nearby; the last incoming call he had answered was labeled “Debt Collector.”The run-down flat was one the husband had picked on purpose.
answer: After going bankrupt, the husband felt he had failed his wife. Remembering the accident insurance he had bought with her as the beneficiary, he resolved to disguise his own death as an accident so that the wife could collect the payout.The husband deliberately rented a worn-out high-rise flat with an aging balcony railing, and quietly kept weakening the railing, planning to fall from there. The wife knew nothing of the husband’s plan, but while tidying up she found the policy, and she too began to toy with the idea of killing her husband for the insurance money.That night, the wife drugged the husband during the candlelit dinner. Using another SIM card, the wife called the husband’s phone, let the call connect, labeled the incoming number “Debt Collector,” and left the phone on the balcony, wanting people to believe the husband had met with an accident right after a call from debt collectors.The wife dragged her unconscious husband to the railing, ready to push him over. The railing, already weakened by the husband himself, could not bear the strain of two bodies and snapped without warning. The wife lost her support and fell together with her husband.The “accident” the husband had prepared to leave his wife was used by the wife, ahead of schedule, to kill the husband, and in the end the accident carried the couple down.
hints: The husband picked this flat on purpose, and he had also tampered with that railing.
The “Debt Collector” label and the call itself were both arranged by the wife.
Both of them meant to turn the husband’s accidental death into insurance money, neither knowing the other already had a plan.

title: Multiple Choice
story: I led the girl’s father into an empty house and pointed at the doors upstairs.“Pick one. Your daughter is inside one of them.”He deliberated for a long time.In truth, whichever door he opened, he would find her.
answer: I had kidnapped the girl, then lured the girl’s father into the house and set the father this multiple-choice question.The father believed his daughter was locked in one of the rooms, and that choosing the right door would let the father take the girl home. The father did not know I had already killed the girl and placed different parts of the girl’s body in every one of the rooms the father could choose from.So whichever door the father chose, the father would find a part of the girl; and whichever door the father chose, the father could never bring home a living one.
hints: The father assumed he was looking for someone whole and alive.
Every room he can choose from truly contains something of his daughter’s.
The girl has been killed, and her body is spread across the rooms.

title: The Cliff-Top Fridge
story: In the parking lot at the foot of the cliff lay the bodies of three men and a refrigerator.One of those men had pushed the refrigerator over the edge just before he died.
answer: A man came home to his house at the cliff’s edge and caught the scent of an unfamiliar perfume; the man suspected his wife had brought her lover there. Looking down the cliff, the man saw a stranger running across the parking lot and decided the stranger was the lover making an escape.Outside the house stood an empty refrigerator waiting to be hauled away. Furious, the man shoved the refrigerator to the cliff’s edge and pushed it down toward the runner below. While pushing the refrigerator over, the man lost his own balance and fell off the cliff.The stranger crushed below was a mere passerby; the real lover, panicking, had hidden inside the empty refrigerator.The man, the mistaken passerby, and the lover hidden in the fridge all lay dead at the foot of the cliff.
hints: The man who pushed the refrigerator fell down himself.
The man running in the parking lot was mistaken for someone else; he had nothing to do with the wife.
The real lover was hiding inside the refrigerator and went over the cliff with it.

title: The Figure on the Balcony
story: My home is on the eighteenth floor. Going to the bathroom in the middle of the night, I saw a stranger’s silhouette on the glass door to the balcony.I meant to go wake Mom and Dad, took half a step, then quietly slipped back into my own bedroom instead.My parents’ door was right over there. Yet I hid, and called the police on my phone.
answer: A night light was on in the living room, the balcony outside was pitch dark, and the glass door mirrored the room’s interior.At first I took the stranger for someone standing on the balcony. Turning to fetch my parents, I realized the figure in the glass came from inside the house: the stranger stood facing away from me at the mouth of the hallway leading to my parents’ bedroom, rummaging through a cabinet.A burglar had gotten into our home. Reaching my parents’ room meant passing right beside the burglar and risked alerting the burglar. My own bedroom was just behind me, so while the burglar had not noticed, I quietly backed into my bedroom, hid, and called the police from my phone.What frightened me into hiding was realizing that the stranger in the glass was far closer than I had first thought.
hints: Outside it is pitch dark, and the glass door mirrors the lit room inside.
As I set out for my parents’ room, I realized the stranger stood right on the path I had to take.
What I saw was the intruder’s reflection inside the house; I backed into my own room nearby and called the police.

title: It’s Going to Spill
story: The moment the car sped up, the woman pressed both hands to the top of her head.“Slow down! It’s going to spill!”As the driver slowed, she asked urgently, “Where is my lid?”There was not a single drink in the car.
answer: The woman had eaten wild mushrooms picked by mistake and been poisoned. Hallucinating, the woman believed herself to be a milkshake without a lid. Her family was rushing the woman to the hospital.Whenever the car accelerated, the woman feared she would slosh over, pressed her hands on top of her head, and kept searching for a “cup lid” that could cover her. The drink the woman kept talking about was her own self.
hints: The car is rushing the woman to the hospital, and she is misreading what is happening to her.
The thing she fears will spill is herself.
After eating poisonous mushrooms, she hallucinated and took herself for a milkshake without a lid.

title: The Fourth Room
story: I chased him into that house.In the first room, the whole room was staring at me.In the second, I felt myself being laughed at.In the third, all those fingers pointed my way.In the fourth, I finally found him.Afterwards, I too stayed in that house.
answer: After my family member vanished, I suspected he had killed someone and tracked him for a long time, until I finally found where he lived and, in my fury, stormed in alone.The first three rooms were filled with his collection. The containers in the first held the victims’ eyes; the second preserved tongues, which my mind turned into mouths laughing at me; the third displayed hands taken from the victims, some of the fingers pointing toward the doorway.There was no one living in those rooms. The “staring” and the “laughing” were how the collection felt to me in fear and rage.The fourth room was where the killer himself lived. I failed to overpower the killer, and the killer killed me. My body, in turn, became part of the collection in that house.
hints: No one living is in the first three rooms; what is seen there comes from past victims.
The gazes, the mockery, and the accusations correspond to the eyes, the tongues, and the hands.
I broke alone into the killer’s collection rooms, was killed once I found him, and became the next piece of the collection.

title: One Hundred Million
