(Record one)In the elevator she stared it down, backing out step by step; in the corridor she began to walk backwards, even run backwards — only by going backwards could she flee while keeping her eyes on it: turn around once, and she would forget why she was running. (Records three and four)The run on her arm she carved into herself before a mirror, for the "self of the next second" — for each self who had just forgotten everything: run. (Record two)It drove her all the way to the rooftop. In her hallucination, the maintenance hatch atop the water tank was a hidden door to hide in. Facing its direction, she backed in — and as the water rose, the hallucination still held her eyes. The lid fell shut, she could see it no longer, and she no longer remembered where she was. Three weeks later, they opened the tank, and the coroner wrote: accidental drowning.Having gotten this far, I advise myself only to stop watching that surveillance footage — after all, of everyone who has seen it, not one remembers what they saw.
hints: The elevator door wouldn't close because something stood in the sensor zone the whole time — the cameras can see it; it's only that no one who watches remembers.

Seeing it traps you in the hallucination of what you fear most; look away from it for one second and everything since you saw it is wiped — she walked backwards so she could keep staring at it even while fleeing.

The word run was carved for every self whose memory had just been wiped; the "hidden door to hide in" from her hallucination was the water tank's maintenance hatch — the moment she hid inside, she could never get out again.

title: The Strange Rhyme
story: In the old quarter stands a ground-floor flat where four people live, always coming and going together. Somewhere among the neighbors — no one knows who started it — a strange rhyme began making the rounds:"Four together, never touching,No empty seat, the door left ajar.You within me, me within you,Swaddled in cotton under a blazing sun."Those who sing it don't know themselves that every line is true.
answer: A dozen years ago, the four of them worked as loaders at the same freezer warehouse. That evening they went in for inventory, the freezer door locked itself shut behind them, the master switch tripped, and no one heard them though they screamed their throats raw. To survive the long night at twenty-something below zero, they stripped off their sweat-soaked outer clothes, and the four of them huddled into one knot in the innermost corner for warmth, holding out until dawn brought rescue.Embraced skin to skin in extreme cold for hours, their sweat froze their flesh together. When the rescuers arrived, the four had frozen into one solid block. In panicked struggle, they tore themselves apart by force — each of them left with someone else's flesh on their body, and each of them leaving their own flesh on someone else.All four survived. But ever since: they wear padded cotton coats even in high summer — a moment's chill recalls that night; the door of their flat always stands ajar — shut it tight and they can't breathe; the four chairs are always full, not one empty, none of them willing to let the others out of sight; and yet none of them touches another anymore — the moment skin meets skin, they remember the tearing apart.In the rhyme, "you within me, me within you" sings not of affection, but of the literal truth.
hints: All four are alive, and their wounds healed long ago — what the rhyme sings of is the sickness in their minds.
"You within me, me within you" is no figure of speech for closeness; it is literal: to this day they carry pieces of each other on their bodies.

They were once locked in together in the freezer, froze into a single block in their huddle for warmth, and were torn apart by force at rescue — ever since, they fear the cold, fear closed doors, and fear touching one another.

title: Don't Look Back
story: I ran afoul of something unclean, and through an acquaintance got an introduction to a master. The master said: "Tonight you walk home by yourself. Remember: no matter what stirs behind you, do not look back — look back three times, and not even the immortals can save you. And turning around counts as looking back."I nodded again and again. At the door, the master called out one last remark after me. I turned back and answered "Got it" — and only as the words left my mouth did I remember the rule just laid down. The back of my neck went cold.Full dark. Before entering the alley, I bought a bag of instant food at the corner shop at its mouth — two cans inside. The moment I stepped into that alley, the only way home, a truck horn blared up behind me, headlights bearing down, flaring bright and dim. I nearly turned; then it hit me: the alley is far too narrow for a truck. Seeing no reaction from me, the sound stopped on its own. I knew: the trial had begun.Along the way, acquaintances called my name; figures flickered in the mirror-glass of shop windows — I bore all of it without turning. I don't make the rookie mistakes people make in horror films.Out of the alley, into the compound, up the elevator, press my floor, key out, unlock, inside — and as I turned to throw the deadbolt and slide the chain, I froze: that was twice. Cold sweat soaked my back in an instant. One chance left.I didn't dare sleep, didn't dare make another big move; I sat bolt upright on the edge of the bed waiting for dawn. My stomach was cramping with hunger, and I thought: moving my hands must be safe — hands only. I took out one can and twisted at it for a long, long time — it wouldn't open.The next morning, someone found me in that alley. My head was twisted around, facing behind me.
answer: He never left that alley. The truck, the acquaintances calling his name, the figures in the mirror-glass, the compound, the elevator, his own front door — all of it was illusion spun inside the alley. When they found him at dawn, the bag of instant food still hung from the crook of his arm, one can lay at his feet with its seal intact — and his two hands were locked around his own head.The master's rule was real: look back three times, and nothing can save you.The first time came in the place he thought safest — that turn to answer at the master's door. The second was turning to lock the door after "getting home." He counted both, clearly; that's why he sat frozen on the edge of the bed, daring to move his hands but never his neck.But the third time had already come. The can was real; the twisting motion landed somewhere else — the illusion set his hands around his own head. He twisted for a long time and it wouldn't open, because it wasn't a lid. The third turn wrenched his neck backward, and he was gone on the spot.The sounds and shadows behind him were the old tricks to startle him into looking back, and he never fell for one; what finally took him was the movement of his hands — the one thing he thought safe beyond doubt.
hints: The master told the truth: three looks back and you're finished. He withstood every lure along the way — the problem was never those frights.
He was counting: once answering the master, once locking the door. What killed him was the move he thought safe — "hands only, never the neck."
He never left the alley; the elevator and home were illusions. What he was twisting was never the can's lid but his own head — and that was the third look back.

title: Love, You
story: Rule one: When you are in danger, Mom will protect you.The year I turned nine, I was in a car accident, and Mom protected me. But ever since, I began running into strange things no one could explain.Rule two: Please open Grandmother's coffin.At Grandmother's funeral, Dad lifted the lid while no one was looking — the coffin was empty. He made a shh gesture at me. I was too frightened to make a sound.Rule three: Please do not trust Mom.On my eighteenth birthday, while Mom was out, Dad secretly pressed a book into my hands. On the flyleaf was a single line: "And God said, Let there be light: and there was light." I didn't understand. In a low voice he added: "On the stroke of midnight of your twentieth birthday, watch your mother."Rule four: You never had a father at all.Before long, Dad suddenly vanished. I asked Mom; she looked at me in terror: "Didn't your father die in a car accident ten years ago, protecting you?" My friends said so, my girlfriend said so — even Grandma said so.Rule five: Someone wants to kill you, but it is not Mom.At midnight on my twentieth birthday, following Dad's instruction, I secretly watched Mom. Suddenly her face convulsed in agony, her features twisted hideous, her whole body lifted off the ground, and then she vanished into thin air. Early the next morning, she said to me, perfectly composed: "Happy birthday."Rule six: You have forty questions to ask; then choose the black door, or the red door.So God truly exists. Two glowing doors surfaced before me, one black, one red. It was time to question God.
answer: The "God" who spoke claimed to be my father. He told another story.My true mother was an AI engineer. The year I turned nine, she took her own son on an outing; there was a car accident, and the boy died on the spot. From then on she was trapped in a self-blame she could never escape. Using technology of her own design, she built a virtual world replicating reality, synced the memories and experiences of her son's life into the AI inside it — that AI is me — and rewrote the ending of the accident: "Mom protected me." Through a neural link she played Mom herself, and raised me.My true father linked into this world at first too, playing "Dad." But he watched his wife sink deeper and deeper: the link was ravaging her brain; she wasted away day by day, and to miss none of my growing up, her real body had to be sustained on nutrient fluids. So Father began secretly hinting at the world's falseness to me: Grandmother's coffin was empty — this world was built from the memories the dead carried in life, it cannot render a "body lying in state," so the coffin was destined to hold nothing; and the line on that flyleaf — the god who said "let there be light" was Mom, the one who held this world in her hands.Mom discovered what he was doing. After a violent quarrel she deleted all his permissions and wiped out his role, and the world rewrote its history on the spot: everyone — Grandma included — now remembered that "Dad died in a car accident ten years ago protecting me." Only I retained the memory, and so I became the one who kept running into strange things.The apparition at midnight that night was a condition my parents had long since agreed to: when I turned twenty, I had the right to know the truth. Mom's agony, her twisted face, her levitation, her vanishing — that was the instant she was forcibly disconnected from the link — her real body could barely hold on any longer.So in rule five, the one who "wants to kill you" is Dad. The "God" before the doors is a program he left behind before being erased. The black door: the world runs on as before, I will forget everything about tonight, and Mom stays in the link to walk me through my whole life — a day her body will absolutely never live to see. The red door: this world, along with me, my friends, my girlfriend, is erased as data — but Mom can return to reality and live.His last words: "He is he, and you are you; I never truly took you for my son. You shouldn't live your whole life inside a Truman Show. And still I beg you to choose the red door — save your mother. This world never should have existed."I chose the red door. Before stepping through it, I smiled up at the "God" in the sky: "If only I really were your son."As the world collapsed and guttered out into a scatter of dead data points, back in reality, my father lifted the receiver from my mother's head. Staring at the black screen, tears streaming down her face, she murmured: "You are my son." This time, she decided she would live, and live well.
hints: This world's foundation is a rewritten car accident: your memories of being alive were synced from a child who died.
The empty coffin, the line on the flyleaf, Mom vanishing at midnight — all are signs left by "Dad"; the "God" of this world is Mom, the one operating it.

You are an AI inside a virtual world; Mom is a mother who lost her child and won't wake from the dream; the erased father left two doors — the red door destroys the world to let Mom live, the black door keeps the dream and drains Mom to death.

title: The Yearbook
story: Graduation season, and the yearbook was going around the whole class. The pages of messages I received felt stranger the more I read.Name: Xiaomei. Gender: female. Dream: to debut in a girl group.Message: I'm going abroad, to join a girl group and make my dream come true. About our divination — someone peeked at the results, but it's all right, I've already handled it. Nietzsche said: "He who cannot obey himself will be commanded by others." Wishing you well.Name: Xiaomeng. Gender: male. Dream: to become someone's boyfriend.Message: I thought it over for a long time — your criticism was right; it seems I must drop this bad habit of mine. Given my poor self-control, I've decided to move away, and end my entanglement with her. There are other reasons too — buddy, I don't know whether I should tell you. Ah, never mind. The first task, of course, is waiting for the exam results.Flipping onward, two more pages:Name: Xiaolei.Message: First, congratulations on getting into the academy of your dreams. We graduate now, you and I about to go our separate ways; there's still so much I want to say to you...Name: Ahua.Message: Just read the page you left in my yearbook; writing back. I hear Xiaomeng is moving away — probably because he learned Xiaomei is going abroad. Honestly, I don't much like Xiaolei; his mouth is too big.And in the corner of Xiaomeng's page there is one extra line, in completely different handwriting:"One more thing — I saw the killer."
answer: The results weren't out yet — on what grounds did Xiaolei congratulate me in advance on "getting into the academy of your dreams"? Because the three of us — Xiaolei, Ahua, and I — had the answers before the college entrance exam. Among ourselves we called it "the divination": the outcome had long since been fixed, and the results release was mere ceremony. That line of Nietzsche was also Xiaolei's message from the heart to his accomplices: those who refuse to be arranged by their scores take fate into their own hands.Xiaomei discovered it — and the leak came precisely from Xiaolei's mouth, which could hold nothing. Failing to argue it out with her face to face, he simply silenced her, telling everyone only that she was "going abroad to join a girl group."The "message from Xiaomei" I received was never written by Xiaomei at all — it was Xiaolei's word to his accomplices in her voice: "Someone peeked at the results of our divination, but it's all right, I've already handled it." Translated: the person who knew will never speak again.Xiaomeng's "bad habit" was voyeurism, always aimed at Xiaomei — I'd long heard of it and criticized him to his face, which is why he wrote "your criticism was right." On the night it happened, he was crouched outside her window again, and watched the killing from beginning to end. He dared not go to the police: report it, and his own peeping would be exposed too. After much hesitation he told only Ahua, whom he trusted.Ahua took it for ravings and passed it on as gossip to Xiaolei: "He says he saw the killer — talking all sorts of nonsense." The words reached Xiaomeng's ears; certain he was about to be silenced, he packed overnight and "moved away to end the entanglement"; before leaving, in deliberately altered handwriting, he added one line in the corner of his own page — "One more thing: I saw the killer." It wasn't written for Xiaolei to see; it was left for a future identification.So in this yearbook: Xiaomei's page was forged by the killer; Xiaomeng's page is half confession, half testament; the premature congratulations on Xiaolei's page are a smugness he couldn't hide; Ahua's page looks the most normal, yet records two things even he never understood — why Xiaomeng moved, and why Xiaomei "went abroad." As for "waiting for the results" — only the few of us with guilty consciences had long since had nothing to wait for.That graduation season, our class was missing exactly one person.
hints: Results not yet released — on what grounds did Xiaolei congratulate you on "getting into the academy of your dreams"? You know best what "our divination" was: you had the answers long ago.
Xiaomei's page was never written by Xiaomei. She never went abroad; "I've already handled it" is the killer speaking to his accomplices in her voice.

Voyeuring at Xiaomei's window, Xiaomeng witnessed the killing; he told Ahua, who leaked it to Xiaolei as gossip; Xiaomeng moved away that same night and, in altered handwriting, left that line in the corner of his page — an identification, should the worst come.

title: Rules of the Witch
story: My name is Li Ming, and I am twenty-four this year. For as long as I can remember, the household has kept a few rules.Rule one: Wear the scent pouch whenever you go out. I was born with a fishy smell on my body that no washing removes; the pouch covers it.Rule two: There is more than one body beneath the rose bushes. In 2010, a frail woman appeared in our courtyard out of nowhere. Foster Father had me hold her. She placed an ancient book in his hands, said "Thank you for your trouble," and stopped breathing. We buried her beneath the rose bushes.Rule three: No one will ever love a witch. In 2020, Feng Shi confessed his love to me in a cafe. I told him honestly what I am, and added: "My father's courtyard is full of roses. If you still want to see me, bring me a bouquet." He was silent a long while, then rose and left — and never appeared again.Rule four: Do not take the XF vaccine. In 2022, XF Tech rolled out a free life-extension vaccine for everyone, yet Foster Father, who worked at XF himself, absolutely forbade my little sister and me from taking it. My sister is three years younger than I, and has never once left the house since birth.Rule five: I will die for my sister's sake. This year my sister grew more and more desperate to go out; she and Foster Father had a blazing fight, and the affair spilled onto the internet. I thought Foster Father would take it out on me, but he was strangely relieved. He called my sister and me together and told us a story. By the end I was weeping, and that same day I set out for somewhere very far away.Before I left, Foster Father handed me a sheaf of old papers in unfamiliar handwriting, like excerpts from an old diary:"In 1980, I was born on the island. The whole world lay drowned beneath the sea; only the hundred-odd of us on the island remained. I was born with a strange affliction, but my family never once held it against me.""In 1999, the village head matched the marriage, and I wed a village boy who liked me. Not long after, a woman who had appeared out of nowhere found me, told me things that turned my world upside down, and pointed me to steal a book from the village head's house. That night we crossed the sea and fled to the mainland.""Later, I gave birth to a child, gave her to the Li Ming couple, and died in the rose bushes."
answer: The diary on those old papers was written by my mother. The whole truth begins with that ancient book.The book is titled The Testament of Xu Fu: more than two thousand years ago, Xu Fu sailed the sea with three thousand boys and girls seeking the elixir; the ships foundered, and a hundred-odd survivors drifted onto an island, saved by the last jiaoren — merwoman — of the place. The merfolk's ancestor was a witch who angered the gods, and the whole line was cursed: unaging, undying, all female, one single line of descent — within two hours of bearing a daughter the mother must die — and marked with a fishy stench no washing removes; and whoever, human or mer, truly falls in love with a merwoman will be swept away by time and space, cast into some moment bound to that merwoman's life. Xu Fu also wrote: eat the flesh of a merwoman and gain fifty years of life and unfading youth — when the term ends, instant, withering death. He feigned love for the merwoman, waited until she bore a daughter and died, then led his hundred in devouring her flesh, and from then on turned the island into a ranch — raising the merwoman's descendants in captivity, each generation sending men to feign courtship, wait for the daughter's birth, and eat the mother. The village rules were only two: no villager may truly love a merwoman, and the merwoman must never learn the truth. "The world lies drowned beneath the sea" was the lie that kept the islanders locked in. That village, later remade, is XF Tech.My mother was the merwoman of the last generation. She was born in 1980; her own mother died by the curse and was divided among the villagers for food — that one meal extended the whole clan's lives to 2030. Mother was raised by "family" impersonated by villagers, believing only that she carried a strange affliction. In 1999 the village head matched her to a village boy, and they waited for her to bear the next generation.What broke all of it was me, in 2024. When I learned the whole truth, the love I felt for the mother who died before I could know her triggered the divine punishment and swept me back to 1999, dropping me before my pregnant mother — I was the "woman who appeared out of nowhere" in the diary. I told her the truth, helped her steal the ancient book, and crossed the sea with her that very night.We made a home on the mainland. In 2000, my mother gave birth to me. By the curse she should have died within two hours — but the love she felt for the daughter in her arms triggered the punishment too: her death was carried away by the crossing — she was swept to 2010, dropped back into that courtyard, and breathed her last. That is the frail woman of rule two; the ancient book she handed over was the very one stolen in 1999. The diary's last line — "died in the rose bushes" — was added later, in Feng Shi's hand."Foster Father" is Feng Shi. The Feng Shi who confessed to me in the cafe in 2020 was swept away by the punishment the very moment he fell in love, and dropped into 1999. In my eyes he "fell silent, walked out, and never came back"; in his, he found the me who had crossed back, and the two of us saved my mother together, watched me be born, and raised baby-me to the age of three — the "mother" you had before you were three was your own self, crossed back in time. In 2003 she gave birth to my little sister: a merwoman bears a daughter, and within two hours the mother dies. She remembered the twenty years of sisterhood with my sister, and so chose to bear her though she knew it meant death — that is "I will die for my sister's sake." That is why two bodies lie beneath the rose bushes: my mother of 2010, and my own self of 2003. After that, Feng Shi raised two children alone: one his wife as a little girl, the other his own daughter by blood. He could never reveal who he was, still less show me the least flicker of love — that was forbidden ground, ready to trigger the punishment again. The walls of roses in the courtyard are the words he planted and could never say.My sister never left the house so the villagers would not learn two merwomen were hidden here; and Foster Father never stopped me from going out because the closed loop required that the me of 2020 walk into that cafe and meet the Feng Shi who had not yet been swept away. The "life-extension vaccine" of 2022 was a net the clan, racing toward their 2030 expiry, cast over all of society to screen for mer-blood that had slipped away; Foster Father took the job at XF to keep watch on them and keep us safe.This year, when my sister's affair spilled onto the internet, I thought Foster Father would turn his anger on me — instead he was strangely relieved: the loop of time had run its full course, and there was nothing left that had to be hidden. When he finished telling everything, I "set out for somewhere very far away": as the me swept back to 1999, the rest of my life will be lived out more than twenty years ago.After I left, Feng Shi blew up the old house: the two bodies beneath the roses, the ancient book, every thread that could prove the merfolk's existence, and himself with them — all turned to ash, so that Xu Fu's line will never find us. The next year, my sister went into the sea. In 2030, the clan's fifty borrowed years ran out; XF's executives aged and died, one after another, within days, and the company collapsed. A line of merfolk penned and slaughtered for a thousand years broke free at last, in my sister's generation.
hints: The author of the old diary is the woman who died in the courtyard in rule two — she too was a merwoman. Where does the fishy smell on your body come from?

The ancient book holds one curse and one scheme: whoever truly loves a merwoman is swept away by time; and the island clan eats merfolk to extend their lives — feigning courtship, waiting for the daughter, eating the mother. XF Tech is them.

The Feng Shi who vanished from the cafe and Foster Father are the same man, swept back to 1999, who saved your mother and raised you; the "Li Ming couple" in the diary is your own crossed-back self and Feng Shi; your journey back both saves your mother and gives birth to your sister.

title: Stay Away
story: Across the road from my home stands an old building, long emptied out, waiting for demolition. Last night, closing my window, I glimpsed an eighth-floor window across the way with no curtain, and a column of dark-red characters on the inside of the glass. Looking closer, it seemed to be written in blood: "Stay away."Behind the window stood a human silhouette, facing my window directly, jerking in quick spasms, as if desperately signaling something. On the whole street, mine was the only household with lights still on facing that window. Terror yanked my curtain shut.This morning I looked at that window once more. The figure was hanging from a hemp rope, motionless. Across a whole road, I could see that face with perfect clarity.
answer: There has been no one living in that building for a long time. That eighth-floor room was padlocked shut when the building was cleared; its only opening is the badly sealed window. The silhouette behind the glass last night was my own self, years from now.Before the old building's demolition, I could never let go of that column of blood writing; I climbed alone into that eighth-floor room, wanting to understand what I had seen years before. The window dropped shut behind me, and I was trapped. Time inside that room runs thousands of times faster than outside: a day out there is ten years in here. The window changed its nature too, becoming a displaced window — the person inside looking out sees a faded image of the street across the road several years ago; the person outside looking in sees this room as it will be years later.And so the trapped I could only keep vigil at the window that sees the "past." I watched my years-ago self staring this way, so I cut my finger and wrote "Stay away" on the inside of the glass, signaling with all my strength. But in his eyes, my years of shouting and gesturing were compressed into one night of spasms; the motion of his pulling the curtain shut was, on my side, more than four full years of darkness afterward. I watched with my own eyes the only person who might have seen me turn off his light, and after that, no one ever glanced at that window again. The day my despair had gathered enough, I stepped onto a stool and slipped the hemp rope over the beam.This morning, the I outside the window finally saw him clearly. Not because he had come nearer — a living person moves too fast, blurring into an unreadable outline; only the dead are perfectly still. That face identical to mine used this means to face me, clearly, for the first time.
hints: No one has lived in that building for ages; that figure shouldn't exist; he gestures at your window alone — he isn't haunting you, he is speaking to you; only his time runs at a different speed than yours.

Time in that room runs thousands of times faster than outside: your one night is his several years. You could never see him clearly not because of the distance, but because the living him moves too fast; the motionless dead are seen all too clearly.

The man in the window is you, years from now: you will finally climb into that room with no way out to understand the blood writing, watch your years-ago self across the glass, and write "Stay away"; through those years without an answer, you will hang yourself.

title: Turtle Soup
story: "Good afternoon, I'm Yamei, the tutor your husband hired. I'm here for the child's first lesson."The door opened a crack. "Come in." Inside were only a woman and a little girl.I changed my shoes and couldn't help glancing toward the inner rooms. "Is your husband not home from work yet?""Working late. He'll be back later." The woman sat down on the sofa with a smile, but her eyes never left the child.The girl lay over the coffee table drawing, crayon clutched so tightly the paper nearly tore. After a long while, she timidly held up her drawing: "Teacher, I'm done."In the picture, she and her mother sat before the fireplace cooking soup, and in the pot simmered a plump little tortoise."What a good girl. What kind of soup is that?""Teacher," she said in a small voice, "it's turtle soup.""That's all right," I sat down. "I'll wait for your husband to come home before I go."The woman's smile stiffened, just for a moment.
answer: Of the three "family members" in this house, not one belongs to it.First, "me." Yamei is this household's man's mistress, recently cut off. He refused to see me again; I couldn't accept it. From his own mouth I learned the family was hiring a tutor for the child, so I came posing as her, meaning to wait for him to come home and demand answers face to face — every glance I stole toward the inner rooms after entering was a search for him.Then the "mother." She is another of the man's cut-off mistresses, and she arrived one step before me — back when this family was still alive. She entered and killed; the family of three did not survive, and their bodies are hidden in this house. Just as she was about to leave, a little girl who often stole things in this neighborhood pushed open the unlocked door and saw everything. As she moved to silence her, the doorbell rang — I had arrived.Before a visitor she could do nothing, so she pressed the girl to her side and played "mother"; the girl didn't dare disobey. Hearing "the tutor your husband hired," she promptly sent the absent man off to "work late," needing only to hold out until I left.The child dared not say a single word, so she begged for help with her drawing: the pot plainly held a tortoise, yet she pointedly called it "turtle soup" — the name did not match the thing. Of the "mother and daughter" cooking soup before the fireplace, one is not the mother and one is not the daughter; in this house, not one person's identity is real. To the killer's face, this was the entire signal she could pass, betting this "teacher" would understand.She bet on the right person — only the wrong identity: this teacher, too, is a stranger under a stolen name.
hints: The child drew a tortoise but pointedly called it "turtle soup" — name and thing don't match. She's warning you: every title you hear in this house should not be believed.
All three people in this house are performing: you aren't the real tutor, and that "mother" isn't the real mother. The real family of three is never coming back — they're in this house.

You and that woman hold the same position: both mistresses the man cut off. She came to kill; the "daughter" is a little thief who stumbled onto the murder and is being kept under her watch — the drawing is the child's letter calling for help.
